And if the four do not testify, that is not done to them, even if the act is certain.

When he had mentioned the matter of women, he followed it with the ruling concerning men, in a manner that also encompasses women. So he said: ﴿And the two who commit it among you﴾; this is the dual of "alladhi" (the one who), and Ibn Kathir doubled its nūn (shaddah) to strengthen it, so that it approaches the fully declinable nouns. ﴿Who commit it among you﴾; that is, whether they are virgin or previously married, man or woman. This is established by the testimony of four witnesses, as has preceded. ﴿Then harm them﴾; and the harm in general, which is truthful, by the tongue and otherwise, has been explained by the verse of flogging and the Sunnah of stoning. ﴿But if they repent﴾; that is, through regret, giving up the act, and the resolve not to return to it. ﴿And amend﴾ (p-218); that is, by persisting in what they resolved upon, and a period passes in which their sincerity in that is known. ﴿Then leave them alone﴾; that is, leave off harming them. This indicates that verbal harm continues until purification is achieved. Then he gave the reason for that by saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾; that is, the One who possesses all attributes of perfection; ﴿is ever Accepting of repentance﴾; that is, the One who returns to those who turn back from their disobedience to the station they were in; ﴿Merciful﴾; that is, He singles out whomever He wills of His servants with success in what He is pleased with for them. So take on the character of His action, glorified is He, and show mercy to the sinners when they repent. Let your harm toward them be only for the sake of Allah, so that they may return; and let most of your speech to them be exhortation, with what turns their hearts toward what the Divinity is pleased with. What confirms that the intended meaning here is the virgin and the previously married, among men and women, is the Prophet's ﷺ explanation in his saying, as related by Muslim, the Four, and al-Darimi, from ʿUbadah ibn al-Samit (may Allah be pleased with him): "Allah has made a way for them: the virgin with the virgin, a hundred lashes and exile for a year; and the previously married with the previously married, a hundred lashes and stoning." So the hadith clarifies what was left general in the verse, regarding the mention of "the way" (sabīl).

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 17:

When He concluded that [passage] with the mention of the repentance of fornicators, and the impulse to fornication, as dictated by human nature, is intense sexual desire (shabaq) and little consideration of consequences, and this [condition] belongs only to youth, He connected to it His saying (Exalted is He), informing about the time of repentance and its condition, encouraging hastening to it, and warning against delaying it: ﴿Repentance is only [accepted] from Allah﴾. Repentance (tawbah) is the servant's turning back from disobedience, seeking pardon from Allah (Exalted is He). What is meant here is its acceptance, and He named it by its name because without acceptance it has no benefit, so it is as though it had no reality.

When He likened His acceptance of it to what is obligatory, in that He has made it binding on Himself, since His word is not changed with Him, He expressed it with the preposition of elevation (ʿalā), which indicates obligation, urging toward it and encouraging it. So He said: ﴿upon Allah﴾, meaning the One comprising all attributes of perfection, ﴿for those who do evil﴾, whatever evil it was, whether of wickedness or disbelief. He said: ﴿in ignorance﴾, indicating the severity of the ugliness of disobedience, especially fornication, by the elders, since the context implies, as a warning, that the matter is not thus with them, as the Prophet ﷺ stated in what al-Bazzar related with a good chain of narration from Salman (may Allah be pleased with him): "Three will not enter Paradise: the old man who commits adultery, the lying ruler, and the arrogant poor man." It is also in Muslim and others from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him): "Three whom Allah will not speak to on the Day of Resurrection, nor look at, nor purify, and for them is a painful punishment: an old adulterer, a lying king, and an arrogant poor man." It is related from many of the Companions through many routes. This is because the presence of death, with its near potential of action and the weakening of the forces that weaken the drive of desire, is close to its actual presence, and this should dispel the impulse of ignorance and crush the wildness of youth, whether we say that what is meant by ignorance (jahl) is the opposite of forbearance (hilm) or the opposite of knowledge (ʿilm).

Imam ʿAbd al-Haqq said in his book "al-Wa'i": Abu ʿAbd Allah, meaning al-Qazzaz, said: "Al-jahiliyyah al-jahla' is a name that applied to the people of polytheism, and it is derived from jahl, which is the opposite of knowledge, and which is the opposite of forbearance." He said: "The root of jahl comes from their saying: 'the wind shook the branch (istajhalat al-rih al-ghusn)' when it moved it. So jahl is only a movement that goes out from truth and knowledge." End of quote. So the meaning then is: they do evil while entangled in foolishness, or in a movement and lightness that took them out of truth and knowledge, so they were as though they did not know by their deed, like the people of ignorance who do not know. He added to the aversion from committing evil and the warning with His saying: ﴿then they repent﴾, meaning they renew repentance.

Since the intended purpose is encouragement toward it, even if its time is short by returning to the sin, He affirmed the preposition, so He said: ﴿from﴾, meaning from some time, ﴿near﴾, meaning from the time of the disobedience; and they are in a breathing space of the term, and this is a metaphor for not persisting until death. Perhaps He expressed it with "then" (thumma) to indicate the distance of repentance, especially with closeness to one who has committed disobedience, because generally when a person becomes entangled in its snares he is not freed except after hardship. For this reason He indicated their greatness with the particle of distance in His saying, causing it by their repentance and promising that He will certainly do what He has made obligatory on Himself, without breach, though nothing is obligatory upon Him and nothing evil can come from Him: ﴿those, Allah will turn to them﴾, meaning those of exalted rank, sincere in faith; ﴿Allah﴾, meaning the One who possesses all attributes of perfection; ﴿will turn to them﴾, meaning He will return them to what they had with Him of closeness and station before committing the sin; ﴿and Allah is﴾, meaning the One encompassing in knowledge and power; ﴿Knowing﴾, meaning of those sincere in repentance and of liars, and of their intentions, so He deals with them according to what their condition requires; ﴿Wise﴾, meaning He places things in their most fitting place, so whatever He does cannot be overturned.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 18:

When He, glory be to Him, had explained what is accepted, He followed it with what is rejected, saying: ﴿And repentance is not [accepted]﴾; that is, its acceptance is not [for] ﴿those who do evil deeds﴾; that is, one after another, persisting in them, whether they are sinners (fasiqun) or disbelievers (kafarah), not returning soon, but delaying; ﴿until when death comes to one of them﴾. And since placing the object (al-maf'ul) first, in a manner that allows every listener to take it as referring to himself, is more terrifying, because the condition of its doer becomes one that is awaited, fearful of its consequence, He said: ﴿death comes to one of them﴾; that is, to the point of the death rattle (al-gharghara), and it is (p-222) the state of direct witnessing; ﴿he says﴾; that is, with his tongue, like Pharaoh, or with his heart; ﴿"Indeed, I have repented now"﴾. So He made clear that what precedes the moment of death is near, with strong encouragement to hasten, by the expression "near" (qarib); ﴿nor [is repentance accepted] from those who die while they are disbelievers﴾; that is, repentance is not for those who, in reality or metaphorically, die without having repented, nor at the death rattle. Thus He equated sinfulness (al-fisq) with disbelief (al-kufr), as a deterrent from sinfulness, because of the difficulty of extricating oneself from it after having engaged in it. For this reason He combined the two in the punishment, by His saying, in answer to one who seems to ask, "What is the recompense of these two categories?": ﴿Those — We have prepared for them a painful punishment﴾; that is, those far from mercy, who did not repent except at the death rattle, and those who died persisting; ﴿We have prepared﴾; that is, We have readied and made present; ﴿for them a punishment﴾. And since delaying repentance is a bodily pleasure, He concluded with His saying: ﴿painful﴾; that is, We punish with it the disbelievers and whomever We will of the disobedient believers, because their repentance in that state is nonexistent; and a believer who dies without repentance is under [divine] will.

When the discussion of the mothers of heirs, and the parts interspersed within it, had ended, and He had closed it with this awesome threat against whoever does what is not lawful for him, He connected His speech about women with a command concerning one who does it, namely that he is an adulterer (zani) who persists in fornication until death, if he believes it to be forbidden, or a disbeliever (kafir) [p. 223] if he believes it to be lawful. So He said, pointing by the specification of the believers that follows: ﴿Nor of those who die while they are disbelievers﴾ [an-Nisa': 18], indicating that a disbeliever does not inherit from a Muslim. Otherwise He would have said, "O mankind," for example, deterring from that by restricting the address to what is the lowest level of faith: ﴿O you who have believed﴾. That is, faith stopped with them at Our prohibitions.

﴿It is not lawful for you to inherit women﴾, that is, their wealth, ﴿by force﴾, that is, while being averse to them. Nothing drives you to marry them except the hope of inheritance. This is because they used to marry orphan girls for their wealth, having no desire for them, but only waiting for their death in order to take their property as inheritance, as will come in the exegesis of ﴿They ask you for a ruling concerning women﴾ [an-Nisa': 127]. Alternatively, the verb may fall upon the women themselves, and "karhan" (by force) in this case would be a emphasizing circumstantial clause (hal mu'akkadah), meaning "averse" or "possessing aversion." This is because a man, when he died leaving a wife, his son from another wife, or a close relative of his agnatic kin, would come and throw his garment over her, and so become more entitled to her than her own self and than anyone else. If he wished, he could marry her without a dowry other than the first dowry that the deceased had given her. If he wished, he could marry her to someone else and take her dowry. If he wished, he could prevent her (ʿadal), holding her back from marriage, harming her so that she would ransom herself from him with what she had inherited from the deceased, or so that she would die and he would inherit her. The people of Madinah used to act on this until Abu Qays ibn al-Aslat [p. 224] died, and his son Hisn did this with a wife of his. She complained of that to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and Allah revealed this verse.

Al-Bukhari related it in the book of tafsir, from Ibn ʿAbbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: "When a man died, his guardians were more entitled to his wife. If some of them wished, they would marry her; if they wished, they would marry her off; and if they wished, they would not marry her off, and they were more entitled to her than her own family. So this verse was revealed concerning that: ﴿It is not lawful for you to inherit women by force﴾."

For this reason, He, glorified is He, followed it with His saying: ﴿Nor prevent them﴾, that is, do not hinder them from marrying after your divorce of them, or after the death of their husbands, or do not press hard upon them with harm while they are in your custody. Al-Baydawi said: "The root of ʿadl is constriction; it is said, 'the hen constricted (ʿadalat) her eggs'," end of quote. The apparent root meaning of this word is essentially to be firm, from ʿadalat al-saq (the calf muscle), which is the flesh inside it. ʿAbd al-Haqq related that it is any flesh that has gathered together. He said: al-Khalil said: "Every piece of flesh that contains a sinew," end of quote. Sometimes the firmness is viewed in terms of prohibition, and sometimes in terms of overpowering and constriction.

Then He gave the reason for that by His saying: ﴿that you may take away part of what you have given them﴾, that is, you (if they were your wives), or your heirs (if they were their wives), and you prevented them after their death, so that this would go away, due to their spending it on themselves during the time of the restriction, [p. 225] or due to their ransoming themselves with it from you.

Then He made an exception to the prohibition of restriction in all circumstances, and said: ﴿except that﴾, that is, do not do that for any reason, except for the reason that ﴿they commit a flagrant immorality﴾, that is, an act of extreme ugliness, ﴿clearly proven﴾, that is, by four witnesses. If it is fornication, then restrict them by keeping them in the houses, as has passed, because whoever hastens something before its time is punished by being deprived of it. Or [the exception applies to] whoever is accepted as a witness, if it is rebelliousness (nushuz) and bad conduct. Then you have the right of restriction at that time until reform, or ransom, by what the soul is content with.

The more fitting reading for the context of the command in ﴿and live with them in kindness﴾ is that ﴿tazlumuhunna﴾ [i.e., ʿadal] should be a prohibition, not coordinated with ﴿that you inherit﴾. ﴿In kindness﴾, that is, in speech and action, with lodging, maintenance, and affection, before they commit the immorality. ﴿Then if﴾, that is, if you do not dislike them, the matter is clear. But if ﴿you dislike them﴾, then do not rush to annoyance or separation, but be patient with them, looking at what is most beneficial, not merely at inclination of the soul, for desire by its nature does not call to good. Then He indicated this reason by His saying: ﴿perhaps you dislike a thing﴾ [i.e., ʿasā, "perhaps," is used here]. Since its indication of this is clear, it is correct to make it the answer of the condition. ﴿A thing﴾, that is, of wives or others, He did not restrict it, to generalize, for the completion of the benefit. ﴿And Allah makes﴾, that is, He who encompasses all in knowledge and power, and who by His wisdom has hidden the outcomes from your knowledge, [p. 226] so that you do not incline to what is familiar, or recoil from what is disliked, ﴿in it a great good﴾.

When He forbade mistreating the wives so as to cause them to forfeit part of what they had been given (ʿadl), He followed it with an explicit prohibition on taking anything from the wife outside the situation in which He had permitted it, namely harm (muḍārra). So He said: ﴿And if﴾; that is: if you do not mistreat the women, but rather ﴿you desire to exchange a spouse﴾; that is: you wish to marry (another woman) ﴿in place of a spouse﴾; that is: you divorce her, or not, and there was nothing on our part that would permit harm.

Since the intended meaning of "spouse" (zawj) is the category (jins), He used the plural in His saying: ﴿and you have given one of them﴾; that is: one of the women whom you were permitted to take in marriage in plurality; whether she is the one being replaced or the one who replaces her, ﴿a great amount﴾ (qinṭār); that is: abundant wealth. ﴿Then do not take from it anything﴾; that is: by way of harm, without her willing consent and without a lawful cause. Then He magnified the taking of it by means of a rhetorical question of denunciation and reproach, saying: ﴿Would you take it﴾; that is: in that manner. Since it has already been stated that among the forms of seizure in exchange for ransom is the situation of committing an immorality (al-fāḥisha), the taking in this situation, which has no cause, was likened to the taking in that situation; so the taking in this form was made to stand in the place of slander (qadhf) with what has no reality. Therefore He said: ﴿by slander and a manifest sin﴾; that is: like those who slander in taking it; and a manifest sin, because it has no cause, which produces doubt concerning it.

Then he intensified this with another rhetorical question of the same kind, saying: ﴿And how would you take it back when you have already gone in unto one another﴾; that is, while the state is that you have already had ﴿intimacy﴾ (al-mulamasa, physical contact); ﴿with one another﴾; that is, you were nearly becoming one body; ﴿and they have taken from you﴾; that is, the women have taken from you, by the intimacy and the union; ﴿a solemn covenant﴾; strong and great; that is, by fearing God in good companionship and not doing harm, because the foundation of marriage rests upon that, even if it is not stated explicitly in it.

When he repeated the mention of permission regarding marrying them, along with what it implied both explicitly and implicitly, and permission had already been given regarding marrying whatever good (ṭayyib) of women is lawful, and "good" in the Law may carry the sense of "lawful," there arose a need to specify which of them are lawful for this purpose and which are forbidden. So He said: ﴿And do not marry﴾, i.e., do not marry and have intercourse with, ﴿those whom your fathers married﴾, i.e., merely by the contract with a free woman, and by intercourse in ownership of the right hand (milk al-yamin). He clarified "mā" by His saying: ﴿of women﴾, i.e., whether they were slave-women or not, whether by marriage or by ownership of the right hand. He expressed it with "mā" rather than "man" because women generally possess a foolishness that makes them ill-regarded by one who has no understanding. (The word here is "mā" (ما), not "man" (مَن), which is used for rational beings; the commentator's point is that women, in general, are regarded as lacking the full measure of reason.)

When He forbade this, souls recoiled from what had long been accustomed and whose splendor had been familiar (p-228), and it became clear that it was in the extreme of ugliness, and that the inclination toward it is nothing but bestial lust, with no trace of intellect or manliness in it. Their custom in such matters, together with regret over having committed them, was to ask about what had passed of them, as occurred regarding facing Bayt al-Maqdis (in prayer) and the drinking of wine. So He followed it with an exception from the necessary consequence of the ruling, which is that this act necessitates the abhorrence of whoever commits it and his punishment. So He said: ﴿except what has already passed﴾, i.e., what you did of such acts in the days of ignorance (jahiliyyah). As al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said in *al-Umm*: "al-Suhayli said in his *al-Rawḍ*: This was permitted in the Jahiliyyah by an earlier law, and it was not among the sacred prohibitions which they violated."

Then He gave the reason for the prohibition by His saying: ﴿Indeed, it﴾, i.e., this marriage, ﴿was﴾, i.e., now and in what follows, a firmly established state, ﴿an abomination﴾, i.e., and an abomination is not committed by one of complete intellect, ﴿and hateful﴾, i.e., the worst of what can be among you and among people of high aspirations, because of your violation of the sanctity of your fathers, ﴿and evil is the way﴾, i.e., how wretched is the path whose path it is.

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 23:**

When He began with the honouring and reverence of fathers, regarding the marriage of sons to their wives in general, He followed it with the specific case of the mother, saying: ﴿Forbidden to you are your mothers﴾. Since the greatest purpose of women is marriage (nikah, the marriage contract), and since attaching the prohibition to their persons (a‘yan) serves to emphasise it without distorting its meaning, and since what indicates that the intended meaning is marriage had already come before, He attached the prohibition to the essence, for emphasis, saying: ﴿your mothers﴾. That is, [forbidden is] enjoyment of them, whether by marriage or by what your right hand possesses (milk yamin, ownership of a slave-woman). Thus the prohibition of mothers is mentioned twice, as emphasis, as a strengthening of the matter in itself, as a show of respect for the father, and as an exaltation of his rank. ﴿And your daughters﴾, that is, and their descendants, however far down they go, because in that there is harm to their mothers. These two categories have not been made lawful in any religion. ﴿And your sisters﴾, that is, full sisters or otherwise. ﴿And your paternal aunts﴾, likewise. ﴿And your maternal aunts﴾, also. The rule governing these two is that every male to whom your lineage traces back, his sister is your paternal aunt; and she may be from the mother's side, being the sister of your mother's father. And every female to whom your lineage traces back by birth, her sister is your maternal aunt; and the maternal aunt may be from the father's side, being the sister of your father's mother. ﴿And the daughters of a brother﴾, whether full brother or not. ﴿And the daughters of a sister﴾, that is, likewise, together with their descendants, however far down they go.

When the matter of lineage was concluded, which comprises seven categories, He followed it with the matter of causes (sabab, affinity by means other than blood), which comprises eight. The first of these is the wives of fathers, which He mentioned separately and placed first, to exalt their sanctity, since people had made light of this. The last is ﴿the married women﴾ (al-muhsanat). He began this section with the mother by milk-kinship, just as He began lineage with the mother, saying: ﴿And your mothers who have nursed you﴾, treating her as having the status of lineage. For this reason He called her "mother." Thus every woman to whom you are related through milk is your mother: she who nursed you; or who nursed a woman who nursed you; or a man who nursed you with his milk from his wife, or from the mother of his child. And every woman who gave birth to a woman who nursed you, or to a man who nursed you, is your mother by fosterage. The nursling (al-murda‘ah) is your sister. The husband of the nursing woman, whose milk she gave with his milk, is your father, his parents are your grandparents, and his sister is your paternal aunt. Every child born to him from someone other than the nursing woman, before or after the nursing, is a brother of the father. The mother of the nursing woman is your grandmother, and her sister is your maternal aunt. Every child born to her from this husband is a full brother or sister to you; and whoever is born to her from another [husband] is your brother or sister by the mother alone. Accordingly, His saying ﴿and your sisters through nursing﴾ applies as it does in lineage, on condition that there be five sucklings and that they occur within the two years; and by calling the nursing woman "mother," and by the one who shared the nursing being called "sister," it is known that nursing is like lineage, as the Prophet (ﷺ) explained by saying: "What is forbidden by lineage is forbidden by nursing." The two examples thus draw attention to the remainder of the seven: the mother draws attention to the daughter, by the common factor of birth; and the sisters draw attention to the paternal aunts, the maternal aunts, the daughters of the brother and the daughters of the sister, by the common factor of siblinghood.

When the matter of what is like the flesh of lineage was concluded, He followed it with the matter of affinity by marriage, saying: [p. 231] ﴿And the mothers of your wives﴾, that is, whether or not you have consummated the marriage with them, because in that there is generally the corruption of relations. ﴿And your stepdaughters﴾, and He mentioned the cause of the prohibition, saying: ﴿who are in your care﴾, that is, in fact, or potentially, because of the resemblance to children that they bear. ﴿Born of your wives﴾. Since the attribution (idafah) permits, in the language, even the slightest connection, He, glory be to Him, made clear that intercourse is necessary, which He referred to by the word "entering" (dukhul), because it establishes the ruling of spouses, by which their children become as his children. So He said: ﴿with whom you have gone in﴾. He restricted it with "entering," because a mother's jealousy of her daughter is less than a daughter's jealousy of her mother.

When this restriction indicated the permissibility of the daughter of one with whom a contract was made but who was not entered, He made it explicit, as a warning of the great prohibition of nursing, saying: ﴿But if you have not gone in to them﴾, that is, to the mothers; ﴿then there is no blame upon you﴾, that is, in marrying them. When He opened the list of perpetual prohibitions with the wife of the father, He closed it with the wife of the son, saying: ﴿and the wives of your sons﴾, that is, whether a wife or one possessed by right of ownership. Since the adopted son was not intended, He restricted it by His saying: ﴿who are from your loins﴾, that is, even if they are far descended. The milk-relations are included, because it is like the flesh of lineage, so the restriction does not exclude it.

When the permanent prohibitions were concluded, He followed them with the temporary one, saying: ﴿And [prohibited is] that you combine﴾, that is, He forbade you to combine, by a marriage contract, since its purpose is intercourse, [p. 232] or by intercourse through right of ownership, ﴿two sisters﴾. If one of them is married and the other is a slave-woman, the married one is lawful and the slave-woman is prohibited, for as long as lawfulness [of the marriage] lasts, because marriage is stronger. When the lawfulness is removed, the other becomes lawful, even during the waiting period (iddah) of the one who had been lawful.

Since combining two sisters was an ancient law, He said: ﴿except what has already passed﴾, that is, there is no sin upon you concerning it, out of mercy from God toward you. Then He gave the reason for lifting the blame, saying: ﴿Indeed, God﴾, that is, the One encompassing all attributes of perfection, ﴿is ever Forgiving﴾, that is, veiling what He wills of the very faults and their traces; ﴿Merciful﴾, that is, dealing with the utmost of honour that the divinity is pleased with.

(p-233) When he had mentioned the harm of combining two wives, he followed it with the harm of raiding what is lawful. The first is a combination between the two women who are married, and this is a combination between the two who marry. He said, coordinating with the deputy of the subject of "are forbidden [to you]":

﴿And the married women﴾, that is, the free women who are wed, because their private parts are protected by marriage from anyone other than their husbands; ﴿from among women, except what your right hands possess﴾, that is, from among the wives of the people of war, for ownership through capture severs the marriage.

When he had completed this, he said, emphasizing it and clarifying its greatness: ﴿The decree of God﴾, that is, take the obligation of the Greatest King, which He has made binding upon you with a binding like that of something joined to a thing and cut from it. Adhere to it without turning to anything else. He increased its emphasis with the particle of obligation, saying: ﴿upon you﴾. When this implied the permissibility of what lies beyond it, he stated it explicitly, for clarity and as a precaution, and to magnify its sanctity, in His saying: ﴿And lawful to you﴾. He showed the greatness of this prohibition with the particle of distance, saying: ﴿is what lies beyond that for you﴾, that is, beyond what has been mentioned to you of the great prohibited things.

Since the discourse concerned prohibition, he did not name the agent but said "are forbidden," out of gentleness in address and as an encouragement to good conduct. When the matter reached the permission, he made the agent explicit, to comfort hearts and make souls at ease. This is in the reading of Ibn Kathir, Nafi', Abu 'Amr and Ibn 'Amir, with the hamza and the ha' vowelled with fatha. He left it unnamed in the reading of the rest, in line with "are forbidden," because the agent of permission and prohibition is known, in the view of the People of this Book, to be the Supreme King, to whom no command whatsoever belongs.

Then he followed the permission with its cause, saying: ﴿that﴾, that is, the intention that ﴿you seek﴾, that is, you desire, ﴿with your wealth﴾, which you give as bridal gifts (mahr), ﴿being chaste﴾, that is, intending by this chastity for yourselves and for them; ﴿not committing fornication﴾, that is, not intending the mere satisfaction of desire and the pouring out of the gushing fluid for that alone. In this manner it would be nothing but fornication, secretly and openly, and in it would be the squandering of wealth and the ruin of religion. There is no corruption greater than what combines these two losses.

When it had been stated at the beginning of the surah, and within it, that the bridal gift must be given, and that nothing given to the woman may be taken back, and this applied generally whether it was after consummation or before it, named or unnamed, he said here, as a consequence of the seeking mentioned: ﴿So whatever you have enjoyed from them﴾, that is, you have brought about enjoyment, which is benefit, ﴿from them﴾, by consummating with them, seeking that in its proper forms, desiring it; ﴿give them their payment﴾, that is, in full for it, which is the bridal gifts; ﴿as an obligation﴾, that is, being an obligation from God, and specified, determined, which you have determined upon yourselves. It is also permissible that it be an emphasis for "give," by a verbal noun of its meaning.

﴿And there is no blame﴾, that is, no sin or inclination, ﴿upon you in what you mutually agree upon﴾, that is, you and the wives, ﴿after the obligation﴾, that is, after divorce, separation, an increase or a decrease, if the bridal gift was already fixed and determined; or after the customary bridal gift (mahr al-mithl), following its determination, if the woman was not named a bridal gift in a marriage contracted without specifying one.

When in these verses He mentioned types of obligations that are in the utmost of wisdom, and expressed in the highest degree of greatness, and concluded them with the removal of blame upon mutual consent, and consent is an inward matter that no one truly knows except God (exalted be He), (p-235) He urged scrupulousness (wara') regarding it by tying the ruling to the predominance of assumption. He said, encouraging obedience to His commands and avoidance of His prohibitions: ﴿Indeed, God﴾, that is, He to whom belongs complete encompassment in knowledge and power, ﴿is ever Knowing﴾, that is, of whoever advances seeking the satisfaction of his companion, or does not seek that; ﴿Wise﴾, that is, He places things in the most fitting of their places, with respect to the recompense for sins and other matters.

When this matter had proceeded in this noble manner, it became known that it is entirely concerned with free women, because that is the more judicious course in marriage. He followed it with instruction on wisdom in marrying slave women, and so He said, linking it to what is implied by the context, "This is the ruling for one who is able to marry a free woman": ﴿And whoever among you cannot afford﴾, that is, O believers; ﴿means﴾, that is, sufficiency and abundance. In the previous verse He expressed it in terms of wealth, belittling the giving of it because wealth is fickle and has no permanence. Here He used *tawl* (means), whose meaning is "the kind of woman few are able to find". ﴿to marry﴾, that is, so that he may marry ﴿the chaste women﴾, that is, the free women, for a free woman is the likely source of chastity, which, being like a fortress for her against one who intends corruption. This is because the Arabs used to guard their women, and the women guarded themselves against becoming like slave women; ﴿believing﴾, because of the high cost of maintenance and the expensiveness of the bridal gift (*mahr*). ﴿Then let him marry﴾, that is, let him marry, if he wishes, from among what your right hands possess, that is, from what others among the believers possess; ﴿from your believing young women﴾, that is, your slave women. The term *futuwwa* (youth), which means youthfulness, is applied to a slave (*raqiq*) because he does what a young man does, owing to his master's imposing service upon him and his not being respected, even if he is an old man. Then He clarified the intended meaning of the attribution, saying ﴿believing﴾, that is, not from among the unbelieving free women, nor from among the unbelieving slave women whom you own, nor from what the unbelievers own, out of caution against mixing with an unbeliever and fear of temptation, as has passed in *al-Baqara*, and so that a believing child does not become, by the rule of following his mother in servitude, the property of an unbeliever. This is what the wording conveys. However, they said that the restriction of "chaste women" by "believing" has no implicit meaning (*mafhum*); otherwise, the marriage of a free woman of the People of the Book, which is permitted by the verse in *al-Ma'ida*, would become conditional on a contract with a Muslim woman, whether free or slave, and that is not stipulated. The school of al-Shafi'i holds that it is not permitted to marry a slave woman while one is able to marry a free woman of the People of the Book. The apparent purpose of the restriction is to recommend keeping distance from the unbelievers, so that one should not marry from among them except out of necessity. It is as if this surah is the surah of association (*muwasala*), in which He dropped the people of distance; and *al-Ma'ida* is the surah of the completion of the religion, in which He mentioned what is permissible for its people. So there is no harm in the restriction, because the implicit meaning (*mafhum*) cannot prevail against the explicit statement (*manțuq*), together with what it contains of the benefit of recommending abstention. This is like how the restriction of chastity here is for recommending not marrying adulteresses, while it is permitted by the verse in *al-Nur*: ﴿And marry the single among you﴾ [al-Nur: 32], as its explanation will come there, God willing (Exalted is He).

When He stipulated belief in this marriage, and expressed it through a quality, and since it is an inward matter whose reality no one knows except God, He followed it with an explanation that it is sufficient to rely on the outward. So He said: ﴿And God﴾, that is, He to whom belongs complete encompassing knowledge of all things known and power over all things possible, ﴿knows best your faith﴾; for perhaps the weakness of someone's faith may appear while the inner state is otherwise. Yet in expressing it by this and by the quality rather than the act, there is a guidance toward greater care regarding religion: "Win the one with religion; may your hands be dust." When religion was made a condition, it was as if it were said, "What of lineage?" So it was indicated that it is not a condition, by His saying: ﴿You are of one another﴾, that is, all of you are from Adam, though you have branched out after him. ﴿So marry them﴾, that is, on condition of inability, ﴿with the permission of their people﴾, that is, from their masters. It is not permissible to marry them without their permission.

Since it is not hidden that the master who owns the person also owns the benefit by way of greater right, the command to give their bridal gifts to them indicates the recommendation for the master to console them with it, without implying that they own it, since they do not own themselves. Therefore He, Exalted, said: ﴿And give them their wages﴾, which are the bridal gifts, ﴿in accordance with what is fair﴾, that is, without harm, neither upon you, nor upon them, nor upon their people, while they are ﴿chaste﴾, that is, modest in themselves, or through the protection of their masters; ﴿not fornicating﴾ [p. 238], that is, openly committing adultery with whoever desires, nor ﴿taking secret lovers﴾, that is, secret friends for adultery, specific ones, such that the one with a *khidn* (secret lover) does not go beyond her lover to another. Al-Asbahani said: the *khidn* is the one who is with you in every outward and inward matter.

Since the definition of slave women had not been mentioned before, He stated it explaining it, saying: ﴿So when they are chaste﴾, a verb in the active voice according to the reading of Hamza, al-Kisa'i, and Abu Bakr on the authority of 'Asim, and in the passive according to the reading of the rest; that is, they move from the scope of exposure to fornication under compulsion to the scope of free women, by guarding their private parts out of their own aversion to fornication, or by their masters guarding them with their consent to chastity. Al-Shafi'i said at the beginning of *al-Risala*, at the end of the section on *al-Nasikh wa al-Mansukh* (abrogating and abrogated): "What the Book indicates in part and the Sunna indicates in part": the meaning of "*uhsin*" here is that they embraced Islam, not that they were married and thus became chaste, nor that they were freed, even if they had not become chaste. He said: If someone says, "I see you applying *ihsan* to different meanings," it is said: Yes, the comprehensive meaning of *ihsan* is that something which prevents the one protected from taking what is forbidden; Islam is a preventer; freedom is likewise a preventer; marriage is likewise a preventer; intercourse is a preventer; and confinement in houses [p. 239] is a preventer; every preventer is *ihsan*. God, Mighty and Majestic, has said: ﴿And We taught him the craft of making armor for you, to protect you from your violence﴾ [al-Anbiya: 80], and He said: ﴿They will not fight you all together except in fortified villages﴾ [al-Hashr: 14], meaning protected. He said: The beginning and end of the speech indicate that the meaning of *ihsan* mentioned here is general in one place and specific in another, since *ihsan* here is Islam, not marriage, freedom, confinement, or chastity; and these names are gathered under the name *ihsan*. End of quotation.

﴿But if they commit an immorality﴾, and this cannot happen then except by consent, not by compulsion.

Since it is characteristic of marriage that its punishment is made severe, and for free women it is made severe by stoning, He, Exalted, explained that there is no severity for slave women; rather their punishment after marriage is the same as before. So He said: ﴿Upon them is half of what is upon the chaste women﴾, that is, the free women, because they are in the likely place of chastity, even if they are not married; ﴿of the punishment﴾, that is, the prescribed penalty, just as that was their punishment before becoming chaste. This is understood by way of greater inference. What is intended here is flogging, because stoning cannot be halved.

Since it was as if it were said, "Is this for every one unable to marry a free woman?", the answer to this question was introduced by His saying, Exalted, indicating with the particle of distance that it is something from which nearness is not becoming: ﴿That﴾, that is, the permissibility of marrying slave women, from which distance should be kept, ﴿is for him who fears sin﴾, that is, falling into fornication, which entails guilt and leads to destruction [p. 240] through punishment in this world and the Hereafter, given the intensity of the drive to marriage and the hardship of enduring abstinence from it. They said: the root of *'anat* is the breaking of a bone after it has been set, so it is borrowed for every hardship and harm. Al-Asbahani said: it has been said that intense lust and great sexual excitement may lead a person to severe illnesses; for women it may lead to suffocation of the womb, and for men to pains in the hips and back. Since this relief and facilitation is specific to the believers among us, it is restricted by His saying: ﴿from among you﴾.

Since He explained its permissibility and indicated distance from it, because of what it contains of enslaving the child, He explicitly recommended restraining oneself from it, saying: ﴿And that you be patient﴾, that is, refraining from marrying them while being chaste, ﴿is better for you﴾, that is, so that you are not disgraced because of them, or your children are not enslaved through them. Then He followed this by emphasizing it to those of insight and high resolve, in a context indicating the lifting of hardship, saying: ﴿And God﴾, that is, He to whom belong majesty and honor, ﴿is Forgiving﴾, that is, toward those who are not patient, and forgiveness indicates some kind of shortcoming; ﴿Merciful﴾, that is, He acts toward them as the merciful acts, by permitting them to fulfill their need and by kindness regarding what follows of the forbidden.

(p-٢٤١) When He, glory be to Him, had completed the lawful and unlawful matters within these limits (*hudud*) and rulings (*ahkam*), and concluded them with the attribute of mercy, He explained what He intended by them of the requirements of mercy, as a reminder of the blessing so that it might be thanked, and as a warning against being forgotten and thus ungratefully rejected. So He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Allah intends﴾; that is, the Supreme King intends to send down these rulings in this order; ﴿to make clear to you﴾; that is, to bring about for you the complete clarification concerning what is for you and against you of the laws of the religion; ﴿and to guide you﴾; that is, to make you know; ﴿the ways﴾ (*sunan*), that is, the paths; ﴿of those﴾; and since what is meant is some of those who passed away, He said: ﴿before you﴾; that is, from the People of the Book: the prophets and their followers; ﴿and to turn to you in forgiveness﴾; that is, to turn you back from everything that does not please Him, especially that which leads to severance (*al-muqata'ah*), such as preventing women and children from inheritance, marrying those whom it is unlawful to marry, and other such things. Thus He informed them by this that He had not singled them out with these obligations, but rather He leads them through them on the path of those upon whom He has bestowed favour, so that this would be more conducive to their acceptance and more helpful to their compliance. And so that they might be certain that the People of the Book casting doubts upon them, and reminding them of old grudges, in order to cast enmity between them, is pure envy, because they share with them in their favours, since they were guided to their ways. How excellent is the conclusion of this with His saying: ﴿And Allah﴾; that is, the One encompassing all attributes of perfection; ﴿is All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾; so He does not prescribe for you anything except that it is in the utmost perfection of soundness; so act upon it and it will bring you to the Abode of Peace.

The explanation of this: what is in this surah includes the command to piety (*taqwa*) and urging towards it, (p-٢٤٢) and the explanation of the obligatory duties (*fara'id*), the matter of fornicators, what is lawful and unlawful of women, carefulness regarding wealth, kindness to people, especially orphans and parents, submission to the rulings, the prohibition of killing, the command to justice in testimony, and other things. All of this has its principles explained in the Torah, as is scattered in this compilation (*diwan*) from its texts in the appropriate places. But the Qur'an is better in clarification, more eloquent in exposition, more wondrous in its matter, more refined in expression, and more precise in allusion. And most remarkable is that the reason for the revelation of the obligatory shares of inheritance in our sharia was women. For in the *Sahihayn* (the two *Sahih* collections of al-Bukhari and Muslim) and others, from Jabir, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "I fell ill, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) visited me, and he came to me when I had lost consciousness." In a narration of al-Bukhari in the book of Tafsir: "The Prophet (ﷺ) and Abu Bakr visited me in Banu Salamah, walking, and the Prophet (ﷺ) found me unable to understand; so he asked for water and performed ablution, then poured his ablution water upon me, and I regained consciousness. So I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, how shall I deal with my wealth?'" In a narration of Muslim: "Only *kalalah* inherits from me," and he did not answer me with anything. In a narration of al-Tirmidhi: "I had nine sisters, until the verse of inheritance was revealed." In a narration of al-Bukhari: "So it was revealed." In a narration of al-Tirmidhi: "until the verse of inheritance was revealed: ﴿Allah instructs you concerning your children﴾ [al-Nisa': 11]." And in another narration of al-Tirmidhi: "until the verse of inheritance was revealed: ﴿They ask you for a ruling. Say: Allah gives you a ruling concerning *kalalah*﴾ [al-Nisa': 176]; the verse." And he said: it is a *sahih* hadith. And in (the collections of) Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, Ibn Majah, and al-Daraqutni, from Jabir ibn Abdullah, may Allah be pleased with both of them, who said: "The wife of Sa'd ibn al-Rabi' came with her two daughters by Sa'd, may Allah be pleased with them, to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, these are the two daughters of Sa'd ibn al-Rabi'. Their father was killed with you on the day of "Uhud" as a martyr; and their paternal uncle took their wealth and left them nothing, and they cannot be married unless they have wealth.' He said: 'Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will decide concerning that.' So the verse of inheritance was revealed." (p-٢٤٣) In the narration of Abu Dawud: "The verse was revealed in the surah of 'al-Nisa'': ﴿Allah instructs you concerning your children﴾ [al-Nisa': 11]." In the narration of al-Daraqutni: "So the surah of 'al-Nisa'' was revealed, and in it: ﴿Allah instructs you concerning your children﴾ [al-Nisa': 11], to the end of the verse. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent for their paternal uncle and said: 'Give the two daughters of Sa'd two-thirds, and give their mother one-eighth, and what remains is yours.'" And in a narration of al-Daraqutni: "The wife of Sa'd ibn al-Rabi' said: 'O Messenger of Allah, Sa'd died and left two daughters and his brother. His brother hastened and seized what Sa'd had left, and women are married for their wealth.' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not answer her in that session. Then she came to him again and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, the two daughters of Sa'd—' So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Call his brother to me.' He came, and he said: 'Give his two daughters two-thirds, and his wife one-eighth, (p-٢٤٤) and what remains is yours.'" Our shaykh, the memorizer of his age, Abu al-Fadl Ahmad ibn Ali ibn Hajar, said in *al-Isabah fi Asma' al-Sahabah*: Abu al-Shaykh narrated in his *Tafsir*, through the chain of Abdullah ibn al-Ajlah al-Kindi, from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, who said: "The people of the Jahiliyyah did not give inheritance to daughters or to young children until they reached maturity. A man from the Ansar, called Aws ibn Thabit, died and left two daughters and a young son. Then the two sons of his paternal uncle, Khalid and Urfutah, came and took his inheritance. So his wife told the Prophet (ﷺ) about that, and Allah, exalted is He, revealed: ﴿For men there is a share of what the parents and close relatives leave﴾ [al-Nisa': 7]. So he sent for Khalid and Urfutah and said: 'Do not touch anything of the inheritance.'" Abu al-Shaykh narrated it through another route, and said: "Qatadah and Urfutah." Al-Tha'labi narrated it in his *Tafsir* and said: "Suwayd and Urfutah," and it occurred to him that they were the two brothers of Aws. Muqatil narrated it in his *Tafsir* and said: "Aws ibn Malik died on the day of "Uhud" and left his wife Umm Kajjah and two daughters," (p-٢٤٥) and he mentioned the story. Our shaykh, in *Takhrij Ahadith al-Kashshaf*, mentioned that al-Tha'labi and al-Baghawi related without a chain: "That Aws ibn al-Samit al-Ansari left his wife Umm Kajjah and three daughters, and the two sons of his paternal uncle, Suwayd and Urfutah, or Qatadah and Arfajah, seized his inheritance from them. The people of the Jahiliyyah did not give inheritance to women or children, and they said: 'Only one who thrusts with spears, repels from the sanctuary, and takes the spoils inherits.' So Umm Kajjah came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) at the mosque of al-Fadikh and complained to him. He said: 'Go back until I see what Allah brings about.' Then ﴿For men there is a share of what the parents and close relatives leave﴾ [al-Nisa': 7] was revealed. So he sent to them both: 'Do not divide anything of Aws's wealth, for Allah has appointed a share for them.' He did not explain further until ﴿Allah instructs you concerning your children﴾ [al-Nisa': 11] was revealed, the verse; so he gave Umm Kajjah one-eighth, the daughters two-thirds, and the remainder to the two sons of the paternal uncle." Al-Tabari narrated it through the route of Ibn Jurayj, from Ikrimah, in a different context, and its wording is: "It was revealed concerning Umm Kajjah and the daughter of Umm Kajjah, and Tha'labah, and Aws ibn Suwayd, and they were of the Ansar. One of them was her husband, and the other was the paternal uncle of her child. She said: 'O Messenger of Allah, my husband died and left me and his daughter, and we were not given inheritance.' The paternal uncle of her child said: 'Her child does not ride a horse, nor carry a burden, nor strike an enemy.' (p-٢٤٦) So ﴿For men there is a share﴾ [al-Nisa': 7] was revealed." It was also narrated through the route of al-Suddi, who said, concerning His saying: ﴿Allah instructs you concerning your children﴾ [al-Nisa': 11]: "The people of the Jahiliyyah did not give inheritance to girls, nor to weak young boys, and they did not give inheritance except to one who could fight. Abdul Rahman, the brother of Hassan the poet, died and left a wife called Umm Kajjah, and left five sisters. The heirs came and took his wealth. So Umm Kajjah complained of that to the Prophet (ﷺ), and Allah revealed: ﴿If they are women more than two, they have two-thirds of what he left﴾ [al-Nisa': 11]. Then, concerning Umm Kajjah, He said: ﴿And for them is one-fourth of what you leave, if you have no child﴾ [al-Nisa': 12]."

All of these reports, as you see, indicate that the occasion of the revelation of the verses of inheritance was the women. It is possible that the whole group of them was the occasion, and Allah knows best. This is similar to the fact that the occasion for the sending down of the obligatory shares (al-faraid) in the Tawrah (Torah) was also the women. When He, exalted is His command, glorified is His name, and high is His majesty, caused to die those among the Children of Israel who turned away from His command, and [those] of their multitudes in the wilderness (al-tih), and brought out their sons from it, He commanded Musa (Moses), peace be upon him, to divide the land of the Canaanites among their sons after knowing their number, according to a method He mentioned. He did not mention the daughters, and among them were daughters who had no father (p-247). So they asked for the inheritance of their father, and Allah sent down their ruling. He said, in the Fourth Book of the Tawrah, the following text:

"When the great death had come, the Lord said to Musa and to Eleazar the son of Harun the priest: Count the number of the congregation of the Children of Israel, from twenty years old and upward, every one who is able to go forth to war among the Children of Israel. And the congregation was in the plains of Moab by the Jordan at Jericho; and tell them the word of the Lord; then they counted them, and their number was six hundred thousand and seven thousand and seven hundred and thirty men, besides the Levites, the tribe of Musa, for they were for keeping the Tent of Meeting and its service; and they were three tribes, one of them Kohath, from whom came Imran. The name of Imran's wife was Jochebed the daughter of Levi, who bore to him in the land of Egypt Harun, and Musa, and Miriam (p-248). Their number at this time was twenty-three thousand, every male of them from one month old and upward. But these were not among those counted by Musa and Harun, when they counted the Children of Israel in the wilderness of Sinai, for the Lord had said to them: They shall die in this wilderness, and not one of them shall remain except Caleb the son of Jephunneh and Joshua the son of Nun. And the daughters of Zelophehad from the family of Manasseh the son of Joseph drew near, and said: Our father died in the wilderness and did not leave a son; give us our inheritance. So Musa brought their case before the Lord, and the Lord said to Musa: The daughters of Zelophehad speak rightly; give them an inheritance among their father's brothers, so that the inheritance of their father may pass to them. And speak to the Children of Israel, saying: Whoever dies and leaves no son, his inheritance shall pass to his daughter; and if he has no daughter, you shall give his inheritance to his brothers; and if he has no brothers, you shall give his inheritance to his father's brothers; and if he has no father's brothers, you shall give his inheritance to the nearest kinsman from his clan, and it shall be a statute of judgment for the Children of Israel, as the Lord commanded Musa."

And he said, in its Third Book, the following text: "The statute of sins, for which a person who commits them is punished by death. The Lord spoke to Musa and said to him: Speak to the Children of Israel and say to them: I am Allah, your Lord. Do not do the deeds of the people of Egypt in which you dwelt, nor do the deeds of the people of Canaan to which I am bringing you; nor follow their statutes; but do My judgments, keep My commandments, and walk in them; I am Allah, your Lord. Keep My laws and My judgments, for whoever does them shall live. I am the Lord, and there is no god besides Me. No man among you shall dare to uncover the nakedness of his close relative; I am the Lord, and there is no god besides Me. You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father, nor the nakedness of your mother, for she is your mother; you shall not dishonor your son's wife; you shall not uncover her nakedness, for her nakedness is your son's nakedness. You shall not dishonor your sister, the daughter of your father or the daughter of your mother, born of your father or your sister of your mother not of your father; do not uncover her nakedness, for her dishonor is your dishonor. You shall not uncover the nakedness of the daughter of your father's wife, born of your father, for she is your sister. You shall not uncover the nakedness of your father's sister, for she is your father's sister; you shall not uncover the nakedness of your mother's sister, for she is your mother's sister; you shall not uncover the nakedness of your father's brother's wife; do not approach his wife, for she is your father's brother's wife; you shall not uncover the nakedness of your daughter-in-law, for she is your son's wife; you shall not uncover the nakedness of your brother's wife, for her dishonor is your brother's dishonor; you shall not uncover the nakedness of a woman and her daughter, that is, do not marry them both; you shall not uncover the nakedness of a son's daughter or a daughter's daughter, for their dishonor is your dishonor; you shall not uncover their nakedness; they are your kin, and their committing it is sin. Do not marry your wife's sister while your wife is alive, so as to grieve her; do not uncover the nakedness of both of them during your wife's life. A woman, when she is in her impurity (menstruation), you shall not approach to uncover her nakedness. You shall not lie with your neighbor's wife, and you shall not defile yourself. You shall not defile the name of your God; I am the Lord your God. You shall not lie with a male as one lies with a woman; for it is an abomination. You shall not lie with any animal, nor shall a woman stand before an animal to mate with it; it is perversion. Do not defile yourselves with any of these things, for by all these the nations I am driving out before you have become defiled, and the land became defiled, and I punished it for its iniquity, and the land vomited out its inhabitants because of their sins. Keep My statutes and My judgments, and do not commit any of these abominations, for all these abominations were done by the people of the land who were before you, and the land became defiled (p-251). Do not defile the land, lest it vomit you out as it vomited out the nations that were before you. For whoever does these abominations shall be cut off. Keep My charge, and do not practice any of the abominable customs that were practiced before you, and do not defile yourselves by them; I am the Lord your God."

Then the Lord spoke to Musa and said to him: "Speak to all the Children of Israel and say to them: Be holy, for I am holy; I am the Lord your God. Every one of you shall revere his mother and his father, and keep My Sabbaths; I am the Lord your God. Do not turn to idols, nor make for yourselves molten gods; I am the Lord your God." And in the Second Book he said: "You shall not spread a false report; do not join hands with the wicked to be a false witness; do not follow the great to do wrong and be led astray; do not join the great who pervert justice, lest you pervert it with them; do not help the poor man in injustice; do not pervert the judgment of the poor, and keep far from a false word." And in the Fifth Book he said: "Musa called all the Children of Israel and said to them: Hear, O Israel, the statutes and judgments that I declare to you today, that you may learn them and keep them and do them; and you know (p-252) that the Lord our God made a covenant with us at Horeb; the Lord did not make this covenant with our fathers, but with us, we who are here alive today, face to face the Lord spoke with us at the mountain out of the midst of the fire. I stood between the Lord and you at that time to declare to you the word of the Lord, for you were afraid because of the fire and did not go up the mountain. And the Lord said: I am the Lord your God who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage. You shall have no other gods before Me. You shall not make for yourselves a carved image or any likeness; you shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain, for the Lord will not hold guiltless him who takes His name in vain. Observe the Sabbath day and keep it holy." Until he said: "You shall do no work on it, neither you nor your male or female servant, that your servants may rest as you do; and remember that you were slaves in the land of Egypt, and the Lord your God brought you out from there with a mighty hand and an outstretched arm; therefore the Lord your God commanded you to keep the Sabbath day. Honor your father and your mother, as the Lord your God commanded you, that your days may be long and that it may go well with you in the land which the Lord your God gives you. You shall not kill. You shall not commit adultery. You shall not steal. You shall not covet your neighbor's wife." Until he said: "Nor anything that is your neighbor's. These are the commandments (p-253) which the Lord commanded the Children of Israel, and spoke to them on the mountain out of the midst of the fire, out of the cloud and the thick darkness, with a great voice that was not heard again; and He wrote them on two tablets of stone and gave them to Musa the prophet. When you heard the voice out of the midst of the darkness, while the mountain was burning with fire, you came near to me, all the heads of your tribes and your elders, and said: Behold, the Lord our God has shown us His glory and His greatness, and we have heard His voice out of the midst of the fire; we have seen this day that God speaks with man and he lives. Now therefore why should we die? For this great fire will consume us; if we hear the voice of the Lord our God any more, we shall die. Go near, you, and hear all that the Lord our God says; and speak to us all that the Lord our God speaks to you, and we will hear and do it. And the Lord heard the sound of your words when you spoke to me, and the Lord said to me: I have heard the sound of the words of this people, which they have spoken to you; they have spoken well. Oh that they had such a heart in them, that they would fear Me and keep all My commandments always, that it might go well with them and with their children forever! Go, say to them: Return to your tents. But you, stand here by Me, and I will tell you all the commandments, the statutes and the judgments, which you shall teach them, that they may do them in the land which I give them to possess. You shall observe to do therefore as the Lord your God has commanded you; you shall not turn aside to the right hand or to the left. You shall walk in all the way which the Lord your God has commanded you, that you may live and that it may be well with you, and that you may prolong your days (p-254) in the land which you shall possess. Now these are the commandments, the statutes, and the judgments which the Lord your God commanded me to teach you, that you may do them in the land where you are going over to possess it; that you may fear the Lord your God, you and your son and your grandson, all the days of your life, and that your days may be prolonged. Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God is one Lord. You shall love the Lord your God with all your heart. And these words which I command you today shall be in your heart; you shall teach them diligently to your children, and shall talk of them when you sit in your house, when you walk by the way, when you lie down, and when you rise up. You shall bind them as a sign on your hand, and they shall be as frontlets between your eyes. You shall write them on the doorposts of your house and on your gates; and do not forget the Lord your God, and serve Him, and swear by His name. Do not go after other gods, of the gods of the peoples who are around you; for the Lord your God in your midst is a jealous God; lest the anger of the Lord your God be aroused against you, and He destroy you from the face of the earth. You shall not tempt the Lord your God as you tempted Him at Massah. Keep diligently the commandments of the Lord your God, His testimonies, and His statutes which He has commanded you. Do what is right and good in the sight of the Lord, that it may be well with you, and that you may go in and possess the good land (p-255) which the Lord swore to your fathers, to cast out all your enemies from before you, as the Lord has spoken. When your son asks you in time to come, saying: What is the meaning of the testimonies, the statutes, and the judgments which the Lord our God commanded you? then you shall say to your son: We were slaves of Pharaoh in Egypt, and the Lord brought us out of Egypt with a mighty hand; and the Lord showed signs and wonders, great and severe, against Egypt, against Pharaoh and all his household, before our eyes; and He brought us out from there, that He might bring us in and give us the land which He swore to our fathers. And the Lord commanded us to observe all these statutes, to fear the Lord our God, for our good always, that He might preserve us alive, as it is this day. Moreover it will be righteousness for us, if we are careful to observe all these commandments before the Lord our God, as He has commanded us."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 26 (part 3 of 3):

He said in the Fifth Book (of Moses, Deuteronomy): "You shall not withhold your hand from giving and charity to your poor brother; but let some of you give charity to others, and let some of you give to one another. Let your heart not be constricted, nor grieve when you give charity to your brother, for when you do this thing and widen (your giving) to your brother, God will bless you in all your works and in everything to which you extend your hand, because the land will never be without the poor. Therefore I command you, and my resolve is upon you, that you extend your hand to your poor brother, and give charity to the needy in the land."

He also said in it: "Judge between your brothers justly; and judge with righteousness; do not be partial in judgment; hear the small as well as the great; do not fear any man, even if his station is great and his wealth is abundant, for the judgment is God's."

He also said in it: "Appoint for yourselves judges and scribes in all your towns, and let them judge the people with the judgment of justice and righteousness; do not be partial in judgment, do not show favoritism, and do not take bribes, for a bribe blinds the eyes of rulers in judgment. Rather, judge with truth, so that you may live, remain, and inherit the land which the LORD your God gives you."

It is thus known from this the principles of most of what He (Exalted) mentioned in this surah, together with what preceded of its forms in "al-Baqarah," at His saying (Exalted): ﴿And when We took the covenant of the Children of Israel: You shall not worship except God﴾ [al-Baqarah 2:83]; and other verses; and also in "Ali 'Imran." As for the punishment of the adulterer, and the matter of killing and wounds, it will be mentioned, God willing (Exalted), in "al-Ma'idah."

Now, when He (glory be to Him) had established His will for their well-being and encouraged them to follow guidance through His knowledge and His wisdom, He followed that with His words: ﴿And Allah﴾, with His kindness and the greatness of His authority, ﴿desires﴾, that is, by His sending down this Great Book and His sending this Noble Messenger (p-257), ﴿to turn to you [in forgiveness]﴾, that is, to return to you with clear explanation from what you were upon of the paths of error, because of the blindness of ignorance that you were in. He increased them in eagerness in this matter with His words: ﴿But those who follow their desires desire﴾, that is, in the sense of exaggeration and persistence, ﴿that you deviate﴾, that is, from the right path, ﴿a tremendous deviation﴾, that is, until you return to what you were in of polytheism and error. So He (glory be to Him) has made the call to guidance most forceful by agreeing with the Protector, the Bountiful, the Majestic, who is never touched by any imperfection, and by opposing the enemy, the envious and ignorant, who has descended from the height of reason to the depths of the natures of beasts.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 28:

Since inclining (al-mayl) is wearisome for the one who commits it, He informed them that the reason for His making His explanation clear to them for guidance, and His desire for their repentance, is kindness toward them. So He said: ﴿Allah desires to lighten (the burden) for you﴾; that is, He is the One who possesses majesty, beauty, and all greatness and perfection; ﴿to lighten (the burden) for you﴾; that is, He acts in this explanation and these rulings as one who desires that, so He will lift from you the heavy burdens (al-aṣar) that were upon those who came before you, which were what drove them toward inclination, and He will grant you concession (yurakhkhisa lakum) in some matters, such as marrying a slave woman, as has preceded. He indicated the reason for this by the conjunctive particle "wa" (and), because ﴿the human being was created weak﴾; that is, the one of whom you are a part; ﴿weak﴾ — its foundation is need; so he cannot be patient against marriage nor against other desires, and he cannot manage to do anything except through support from Him, glory be to Him.

When what had preceded was largely based on wealth, sometimes through inheritance and sometimes through the bridal gift (ju'l) in marriage, whether lawful or unlawful, (Allah) (Exalted is He) said, as a continuation of what had preceded, after He had distinguished truth from falsehood and shown the weakness of this entire category, thereby invalidating their justification for denying women and minors their share of inheritance on the ground of weakness; and after He had explained the manner of disposing of marriage through wealth and other things, in order to preserve lineages, and had mentioned the manner of disposing of wealth, in order to purify the human being, addressing the youngest in age among the believers and elevating others above this kind of matter: ﴿O you who have believed﴾, that is, who have professed faith and committed to the rulings.

Since eating (al-akl) is the greatest purpose of wealth, and the Arabs regarded eagerness for eating as the greatest shame even when it was lawful, He used it as a metaphor for consumption (al-tanawul), (p-259) and said: ﴿do not consume﴾, that is, do not take possession of, ﴿your wealth among yourselves in falsehood﴾, that is, through causing it to pass to oneself, by taking the share of women and children from inheritance, by preventing some women from remarrying, and other such matters already forbidden, and others.

Having forbidden consuming wealth in falsehood, He made an exception for what is not of that kind, saying: ﴿except that it be trade﴾, that is, the dealings that are customary and circulated among you, ﴿trade﴾. This is in the reading of the Kufans in the accusative; according to the reading of others it means: except that there be a trade existing, ﴿by mutual consent from you﴾, that is, not forbidden by the Lawgiver. Perhaps the use of the particle of the connected exception, while the meaning is that of the disconnected, is to indicate that all worldly transactions are deserving of being described as falsehood, even if the word "except" did not refer to them, as a means of discouraging attachment to them, restraining excessive accumulation of them, and encouraging what endures in its benefit through its permanence. Thus every disconnected exception in the Qur'an: whoever reflects upon it with true reflection will find that the departure from the particle designated for it, which is "but" (lakin), to the form of exception contains profound wisdom. And Allah is the Granter of success.

Since wealth is the counterpart of the soul, and He forbade its destruction in falsehood, He forbade (p-260) the destruction of the self, because most of their destruction of souls was through raids for plundering wealth and what was connected with it and caused by it. Moreover, whoever has his wealth consumed becomes agitated in soul, and this leads to strife, the final outcome of which may be killing; so the prohibition of that was most fitting, given what the surah is built upon of compassion and mutual connection. So He (Exalted) said: ﴿And do not kill yourselves﴾, that is, literally, by a person directly killing himself; or figuratively, by some of you killing others, for the souls are one, and that also leads to the killing of the killer's own soul. So do not neglect your share of thankfulness toward your souls; whoever neglects their share, it is as if he has killed them. Then He gave the reason with what softens the hardest of people, saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, that is, together with what He has of attributes of greatness, to which no greatness approaches, ﴿has been to you﴾, that is, specifically, in that He lightened for you what He made heavy for those before you, ﴿Merciful﴾, that is, abundantly merciful, in that He made obedience easy for you and granted you success in it; thereby He, glory be to Him, emphasized encouragement toward compliance.

Then He said, as a warning against falling into misguidance: ﴿And whoever does that﴾; i.e., the forbidden act, of killing and other things, that greatly distances one from the presence (ḥaḍarāt) of God; ﴿out of transgression and wrongdoing﴾; i.e., without right. His conjoining of the two descriptors with "and" (wa) indicates the extremity of each of them. Along with this, the meaning conveyed by the form ﴿ʿudwānan﴾ (fu'lān pattern, the descriptor "fuʿlān") is intensification; so the intended meaning is an enemy who is severe, excessive, transgressing the limits, arising from enmity, and wrongdoing that is extreme, with no admixture of right in it. ﴿Then We will cause him to enter the Fire﴾; i.e., We will make him enter it, with a threat that admits no failure, even if his respite is prolonged. ﴿And that is ever for God﴾; i.e., for Him who possesses majesty and beauty, ﴿easy﴾; i.e., because it does not diminish anything of His dominion, and no hindrance prevents Him from it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 31:

When (Exalted is He) had explained what is due to the doer of such acts, as a warning, and had previously mentioned a number of major sins (kaba'ir), He followed it with what is due to the one who refrains, as good news, in answer to one who seems to have said: "This is for the doer; so what is for the one who avoids them?" So He said, in a general manner: ﴿If you avoid the major sins you are forbidden⦆ — that is, exert yourselves with a sound intention to abstain thoroughly, and to keep far away from them — ﴿major sins of what you are forbidden﴾, that is: such as consuming wealth, killing without right, fornication, and other things mentioned earlier. Al-Bazzar narrated, and al-Haythami said — and its narrators are the narrators of the Sahih — from ʿAbdullah (meaning Ibn Masʿud), that he was asked about the major sins, and he said: "What lies between the beginning of Surat al-Nisa' and the end of thirty [verses]." Al-Isbahani said: Every sin for which the Shariʿa has magnified the threat of punishment and made it severe, or whose harm it has magnified concerning the five necessities — the preservation of religion, life, lineage, intellect, and property — is a major sin; and whatever else is a minor sin. ﴿We will remove from you your misdeeds﴾, that is: those which are below the major sins, all of them. If you commit some of the major sins, and you bring the expiators of the five daily prayers, Friday, fasting of Ramadan, and the Hajj, or you neglect some of them, then Allah has bestowed favour upon you by bringing you the illness [of expiation]; that which is brought expiates the minor sins, and does not counter that major sin, so it does not expiate all misdeeds, because it did not reach that major sin. ﴿And We will admit you to an honourable entrance﴾, that is: one that combines nobility, action, generosity, and every good meaning; whoever misses all of that will not have his misdeeds expiated, and will not be admitted to this entrance. It is sufficient for its negation that retribution occurs at some point. Imam Ahmad said: All Muslims are in Paradise, due to this verse and the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "I have reserved my intercession for the people of major sins of my Ummah." So Allah (Exalted is He) forgives what is below the major sins, and the Prophet (ﷺ) intercedes for the major sins; so what sin remains upon the Muslims?! Al-Isbahani mentioned it from him. This hadith was recorded by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi, and others, from Anas (may Allah be pleased with him).

[p. 263] When He forbade killing and wrongfully consuming one another's property through action, and these two are acts of the limbs, so that the outward conduct would be purified of grievous sins, He forbade wishing (tamannī, longing for what others possess), which is the precursor to consuming wrongfully. This amounts to a prohibition of consuming wrongfully by way of greater priority, since tamannī may be envy (ḥasad), and it is this that is forbidden here, as is apparent from the verse. Envy is unlawful, and being content with the unlawful, and wishing in this manner, leads to consuming wrongfully, and consuming wrongfully leads to killing, for whoever grazes around the protected pasture will likely fall into it. The prohibition here is for prohibition (tahrīm) according to most scholars. So He said: ﴿And do not wish for what Allah has favoured some of you over others with﴾, meaning: do not follow your souls in that. ﴿What Allah has favoured﴾ means He to whom all greatness belongs, so nothing diminishes Him. ﴿With it﴾, meaning: of wealth and other things. ﴿Some of you over others﴾, meaning: in inheritance and other matters, and in all the virtues of the soul that relate to the theoretical faculty (al-quwwa al-naẓariyya, the rational faculty of knowing), such as perfect intelligence, complete intuition (ḥads), and increased knowledge in its quantity and quality; or to the practical faculty (al-quwwa al-'amaliyya, the faculty of acting), such as chastity ('iffa), which is a mean between insensibility (jumūd) and debauchery (fujūr), courage (shajā'a), which is a mean between recklessness (tahawwur) and cowardice (jubn), and generosity (sakhā'), which is a mean between extravagance (isrāf) and miserliness (bukhl); and the use of these faculties in the manner that is fitting, which is justice ('adāla); or the physical virtues, such as health, beauty, and long life, together with pleasure and delight; or the external virtues, such as having many righteous children, many kinsfolk, friends, helpers, complete leadership, the effectiveness of one's word, and being loved by people and having a good reputation among them. These are the comprehensive forms of happiness, and some of them are of the theoretical kind with no room for acquisition, while some are acquired. Whenever a sensible person reflects on this, he finds it to be pure bounty from Allah. So whoever sees another surpassing him in any of these circumstances, his heart is pained, and he has two states: one is that he wishes to obtain the same happiness for himself, and the other is that he wishes its removal from its possessor. This is the blameworthy envy, for it is like an objection to Allah, who apportioned this distribution. If he believes that he is more deserving of it than him, he has opened the door of disbelief upon himself, invited the darkness of innovation, and erased the light of faith, for Allah does whatever He wills and He is not questioned about what He does, so there is no objection to Him. Just as envy is a cause of corruption in religion, it is also a cause of corruption in this world. So everyone must be content with what has been apportioned to him, knowing that this is in his interest, and that were it otherwise, he would be corrupted, for all of that is a distribution from Allah, issuing from His judgement, His management, and His knowledge of the states of the servants regarding what sets them right and what corrupts them.

As for wishing for the like of what another has: if it is in religious matters, it is good, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "There is no envy except in two cases."
