If it is in worldly matters, some people have permitted it, while others, and they are the verifiers (al-muḥaqqiqūn), say: it is not permitted, because that blessing may often be a corruption for him in religion and a harm in this world, like the story of Qarun. Imam al-Rāzī said the meaning of this.

When He, glorified is He, forbade this, He gave a reason that draws attention to striving for provision and moderation in seeking, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said in what Aḥmad, al-Tirmidhī, and Ibn Mājah related from Shaddād ibn Aws (may Allah be pleased with him): "The wise one is he who holds his soul accountable and works for what comes after death, and the incapable one is he who follows his soul's desires and wishes vainly of Allah." And as the Prophet (ﷺ) said in what Muslim, al-Nasā'ī, and Ibn Mājah related from Abu Hurayra (may Allah be pleased with him): "The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, and there is good in each of them. Be eager for what benefits you, seek help from Allah, and do not be incapable. If something befalls you, do not say: 'If only I had done such and such,' but say: 'Allah decreed, and He does what He wills,' for 'if only' opens the work of Satan." So He said, indicating that no one attains all that he hopes for: ﴿For men there is a share﴾, meaning: its measure has already been completed, so it neither increases nor decreases. He, glorified is He, made clear that seeking and working are required, as the hadith indicated, so He said: ﴿of what they have earned﴾, meaning: they burdened themselves and exhausted their souls in earning it, from the affairs of both abodes, namely reward and its causes of acts of obedience, and inheritance, and striving in gains and profits. "My provision has been placed under the shadow of my spear." "If you relied upon Allah with true reliance, He would provide for you as He provides for the birds: they go out hungry in the morning and return full in the evening." ﴿And for women there is a share of what they have earned﴾, meaning: likewise, wishing at that point is not beneficial, so occupying oneself with it is mere toil.

[p. 266] Since He indicated with the partitive (tab'īḍ) that attainment is by His decree and not by the acquisition He made a cause, for it sometimes grants success and sometimes disappoints, the sense would be: "So acquire, and do not be incapable, so that you seek by wishing." He commanded turning towards Him, in wealth and in everything, as an indication of moving the means together with moderation in seeking, so He said: ﴿And ask Allah﴾, meaning: He to whom belong all the attributes of perfection.

Since He, glorified is He, whose greatness is such that nothing diminishes Him however great it is, said: ﴿of His bounty﴾, meaning: from His treasuries which never run out and which nothing exhausts. In this is an admonition against specifying, for it may be the cause of corruption; rather, the request should be for what is good for you. The best transmitted supplication is: ﴿Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire﴾ [al-Baqarah: 201]. Then He gave a reason for that [p. 267] by His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, meaning: the Supreme King in whose hand are the keys of everything, ﴿is ever, of all things, Knowing﴾, meaning: therefore He is capable of all things, for the perfection of knowledge entails the comprehensiveness of power, as will be made clear, God willing, in Surat Ṭā Hā. The meaning is that He has done by His knowledge what sets you right, so ask Him by His knowledge and His power for what benefits you, for He knows what sets right every servant and what corrupts him.

And He connected to that what is part of the same reason, saying: ﴿And for every one﴾, that is, of the two groups, whether young or old; ﴿We have appointed﴾, by Our greatness which has no equal; ﴿heirs (mawali)﴾, that is, We have decreed that they are the protectors (awliya'), that is, the helpers (ansar), and the close relatives, for the sake of inheritance. They are the ones who take charge of the property and inherit it, whether they are a specific 'asabah (male agnatic kin), who are the heirs, or a general 'asabah, who are the Muslims.

Since the concern for providing for the young was greater, He said: ﴿from what﴾, that is, from that for which; ﴿has left﴾, that is, behind; ﴿the parents﴾, that is, to you. Then He followed that with what includes the right of ascendants and descendants, and said: ﴿and the near relatives﴾, that is, to you. Then He connected to that His saying: ﴿and those﴾, that is, and what those ones left, ﴿with whom your oaths have bound you﴾, that is, from what is left by those whom you rely upon through lineage, or through a cause: by alliance (hilf), or by patronage (wala'), or by marriage (sihr). He mentioned the oath because the pledge is made with a handshake upon it. Then He made the consequence of that His saying: ﴿so give them﴾, that is, the heirs, even if they are young or female, as I have explained to you in the previous verse on inheritance; and leave aside everything that contradicts that, for it has been abrogated (naskh) by it. ﴿their share﴾, that is, which We have ordained for them from the inheritance, ﴿in full﴾, not diminished. Do not suppose that anyone else is more deserving than them, or equal to them. Then He warned against opposing this and emphasized the matter, by way of promise and threat, with His saying: ﴿Indeed Allah﴾, that is, the One encompassing all attributes of perfection, ﴿is ever, over all things, Witness﴾, that is, He knows the protector from others and the traitor from others, even if one strives to conceal it, because nothing is hidden from Him, and He is not absent from anything, nor is anything absent from Him.

So the meaning is: "We have only done what you intended, namely giving property to the one who protects the sanctities and defends the sanctuary, while you were not placing them in their proper stations, due to your absence from the realities of affairs and their absence from you. Therefore We have not taken anything from it for anyone other than the mawali, that is, the Ansar, whether by kinship, or by the contract of patronage, or by marriage. The conclusion is that it is for the one who protects in fact, or with a near potential, or a distant potential that approaches nearness. As for the preference in shares, it is a matter We have kept to Ourselves, having knowledge of its deserving recipients."

In al-Bukhari, in the book of tafsir (exegesis), from Ibn 'Abbas: "mawali": heirs; "and those with whom your oaths have bound you": the Muhajirun (Emigrants), when they came to Madinah, the Muhajir would inherit from the Ansari, to the exclusion of his blood relatives, because of the brotherhood that the Prophet (ﷺ) had established between them. Then when the verse was revealed, ﴿And for every one We have appointed heirs﴾, it abrogated that. Then he said: "and those with whom your oaths have bound you" refers to support, mutual aid (rifadah), and counsel (nasihah), and inheritance has gone, but he may bequeath to him.

Then, glorified is He, He explained the reason some were given preference, so He said, in answer to a question as if someone had asked, "Why were men given preference?": ﴿Men are the maintainers of women﴾; that is, in the manner of rulers, ﴿over women﴾, in disciplining, teaching, and every command and prohibition. He explained the two causes of this by saying: ﴿because Allah has favoured one of them over the other﴾; that is, He who possesses perfect wisdom and a perfection that none can approach, by way of a gift from Him and a grace, not through acquisition; ﴿one of them﴾, namely the men, in intellect, strength, and courage. For this reason, prophets, rulers, the great imamate (imamat al-kubra, the supreme leadership), and guardianship in marriage, and the like, were among men, and in every matter that requires superiority of bodily strength, intellect, and religion; ﴿over the other﴾, meaning women. So He said to men: ﴿Go forth, light and heavy﴾ [al-Tawbah: 41], and He said to women: ﴿And abide in your houses﴾ [al-Ahzab: 33]. (p-270) When He mentioned the cause that is a bestowed gift, He followed it with the cause that is acquired, and He said: ﴿and because they spend﴾; that is, of the bridal gifts (mahr), clothing, and other things; ﴿of their wealth﴾; that is, upon them. Thus the excess on one side became an equivalent to the excess on the other side.

When their superiority became clear by this, the soul submitted to what they were preferred with, in inheritance and other matters. Since the mention of their marrying women and the exhortation to justice toward them had preceded, it was fitting to explain the rights of wives that are incumbent upon them, and the disciplining of one who denies the truth. So He said, presenting as a consequence of what is incumbent upon them of their rights, from the mention of their superiority: ﴿So righteous women are devoutly obedient﴾; that is, sincerely obedient to their husbands. Therefore there follows from this: ﴿guarding in the husband's absence﴾; that is, guarding the husbands' rights concerning themselves, the houses, and the wealth, during their absence from them; ﴿by what Allah has guarded﴾; that is, by the matter with which Allah, who encompasses all in knowledge and power, guarded their absence, by His acting in it as one who guards, through encouraging them to obey their husbands in what pleases Allah, and warning them against disobeying them in what angers Him, and observing the limits to which He, glorified is He, alluded in al-Baqarah, and which the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) explained.

When He had described the righteous women as those deserving maintenance in matters of necessity, He followed it with the ruling concerning other than them, and He said: ﴿And those from whom you fear nushuz (rebellion)﴾; that is, their exalting themselves over you, beyond (p-271) the station in which Allah placed them, and their disobedience to you in what Allah has made your right. The root of nushuz is being disturbed while elevated. Al-Shafi'i said: Indications of nushuz may be verbal and may be practical. The verbal is like her answering him when he calls her, and submitting to him with words when he addresses her, and then changing. The practical is like her standing for him when he enters upon her, or her hastening to his command and rushing to his bed with joy when he seeks her, and then, when she changes, nushuz is then presumed. The preliminaries of these states necessitate the fear of nushuz. ﴿Then admonish them﴾; that is, remind them of the command of Allah, with what splits their hearts open, softens them, and frightens them with the majesty of Allah.

Since admonition necessitates the realization of obedience or disobedience, He said: ﴿And forsake them﴾; that is, if they do not return through admonition; ﴿in the beds﴾; that is, those in which you used to spend the night with them, in the house; and within forsaking is his refraining from speaking to her. Al-Shafi'i said: And the forsaking of speech should not exceed three [days]. ﴿And beat them﴾; that is, if they persist, a beating of discipline (ta'dib), not severe (ghayr mubarrih), which is what does not break a bone nor disfigure a limb, and is spread over her body, not concentrated on one place, avoiding the face, for it is the gathering place of beauty, and is less than forty [strokes]. Al-Shafi'i said: Beating is permissible, and leaving it is better. ﴿Then if they obey you﴾; that is, with some of the admonition, (p-272) and the forsaking in the place of sleeping within the house, or the beating; ﴿then seek not﴾; that is, do not seek; ﴿against them a way﴾; that is, a path to harm, for past disobedience, such as reproaching them for what was similar in the past, by the superiority you have over them. Rather, forgive them what has passed, and let not what Allah has granted you of superiority lead you to scrutiny. Then He gave the reason for that by saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾; that is, and you know what perfection belongs to Him; ﴿is ever﴾; and has never ceased to be; ﴿Exalted, Great﴾; that is, He has loftiness and greatness absolutely, with perfect power and the execution of His will. So He does not love the transgressor, and does not approve of him in his transgression, and His power over you is greater than your power over them. Yet, despite that, He pardons those who disobey Him, even if they fill the earth with sins, when they obey Him, and does not hold him accountable for anything of what he neglected of His right, but rather replaces his misdeeds with good deeds. So if He took you to account for your sins, He would destroy you. Therefore, adopt the character traits of His that you are able to, so that you may attain His noble gifts, fear His punishments, and beware of His chastisement, with what He has of loftiness and greatness.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 35:

When he had explained the state of harmony, and the character traits that might mix into it, which the husband is responsible for correcting, he followed it with the state of estrangement and discord, which requires someone to do justice between the two. He said: ﴿And if you fear a breach between the two﴾; that is, O you who are God-fearing and capable of reform, from among the rulers and others; ﴿a breach between them﴾; that is, between the two spouses implied by the context, where each of them is in a faction other than the one in which the other stands. (p. 273) This does not happen except when one of them is in error. He attributed the breach to "the between" (al-bayn) in order to indicate that this action is taken only when there is fear of a specific breach, namely that the bond joining them, which is what distinguishes each from the other, cannot ordinarily be removed so that they become one thing, as they were when there was no separation between them. This is based on the assumption that there is no good in their remaining together. ﴿Then send﴾; that is, to them, for reconciliation between them, by giving the wronged party justice against the wrongdoer; ﴿an arbiter from his people﴾; that is, from the husband's side; ﴿and an arbiter from her people﴾; that is, from the wife's side. This is more complete, because their own people are closer to removing the causes of the breach than the two of them are, since they are more fit to know the inner aspects of their affairs and the realities of their conditions. The spouses themselves are closer to knowing each other's inclinations, if they are close, but they are also closer to concealing these from outsiders. The benefit of the two arbiters is that each of them should be alone with his counterpart, and seek to uncover the reality of the situation, so as to know the way to reconciliation.

Then he answered one who might be imagined to ask: "And what might they accomplish?" By his saying: ﴿If they both desire reconciliation﴾; that is, the two arbiters; ﴿reconciliation﴾; that is, between them. It seems he made it indefinite because sincerity and the presence of perfection are rare. ﴿God will bring about harmony﴾; He, to whom belongs comprehensive knowledge of the unseen and the witnessed; ﴿between them﴾; that is, between the two spouses, because the goodness of intention is the greatest helper (p. 274) in reaching one's goals. This indicates that nothing happens except by God, and that the means are only a trial from God, through which whoever engages with them is made happy, and who relies on God apart from them, and who is made wretched by them if he makes them the target of his aim and relies upon them.

Since the reformer may be thought to be a corrupter because of his breaking of the bond by speaking the truth without tact, and the corrupter may be counted a reformer because of the flattery, dissimulation and deceit seen in him, the one who doubts the promise of success may think otherwise than what is actually the case. He (Exalted is He) said, removing this illusion, encouraging and warning: ﴿Indeed, God﴾; that is, He who encompasses all attributes of perfection; ﴿is ever Knowing﴾; that is, absolutely, regarding whatever can be known, even if it is hidden from others; ﴿Acquainted﴾; that is, nothing hidden is concealed from Him, and nothing unseen is absent from Him. Thus these verses became sufficient for most of the conditions of marriage. He did not mention divorce, may He be glorified and exalted, when He mentioned the breach, because it was mentioned earlier in al-Baqarah (the Cow), and because the structure of this surah is built on connection and affection, not on separation and repudiation, as Ibn al-Zubayr said. For this reason, that is, because the surah is built on connection, harmony and unity rather than separation and disagreement, it specified the rule of a quarrel between spouses only by informing of the form of reconciliation and justice, in order to preserve that connection. Divorce was not suited to this, so no mention or allusion to it occurred here, except His saying: ﴿And if they separate, God will enrich each of them from His abundance﴾ [al-Nisa': 130]. End.

In this surah many commandments have accumulated, from its beginning up to this point, as the fruit of taqwa (God-consciousness), justice and grace, along with encouragement to seek His bounty and warning against His punishment. He concluded this by guiding the spouses to treat one another with kindness (ihsan, excellence in conduct), and He ended the verse with what is at the peak of good closing, namely the two attributes of knowledge and awareness. This was in the sense of what ended the verse commanding taqwa, with the description as Watcher (raqib). That required repeating the reminder of taqwa with which the surah opened, so the implied sense is, necessarily: "So fear Him." He linked to it, or to something similar to ﴿And ask Allah of His bounty﴾ [an-Nisa': 32], or to ﴿O mankind, fear your Lord﴾ [an-Nisa': 1], the purpose of creation, of the creatures spread out upon that attribute. This is pure worship, which is ihsan in dealing with the Creator, and He followed it with ihsan in dealing with creation. So He said: ﴿And worship Allah﴾, that is, obey the One to whom all perfection belongs, to whom nothing is similar, with pure obedience, free of any admixture of opposition, together with humility and submission, because the essence of all of this is devotion through carrying out commands and avoiding prohibitions.

Since He, glorified is He, is self-sufficient, He accepts only what is sincere. So He said, emphasising what the previous statement had conveyed (p-276): ﴿and associate nothing with Him﴾.

Since He commanded the One True God with what is fitting for Him, and this has two levels, the first of which is faith (iman) and the highest of which is ihsan, the one commanded with this became sincere in his worship. He commanded him to show ihsan in his khilafah (his role as vicegerent on earth), and began with those most deserving of it, namely the one who was the cause of his coming into being. So He said, indicating that He does not be satisfied for him with anything from this except the level of ihsan, and that whoever is sincere to Him, He makes him independent of everything other than Him, so that He continues to bestow favour upon whoever is other than Him: ﴿and to parents﴾, that is, show ihsan to them both; ﴿good treatment﴾. And what is enough to show the magnitude of their matter is that the honouring of them is placed alongside the command to affirm His oneness, glorified is He.

Since the foundation of the surah is maintaining ties of kinship, especially for the near of kin, He said, detailing what was mentioned at the beginning of the surah and emphasising it: ﴿and to the near of kin﴾, because their right is strengthened by their closer kinship, and because this surah calls for greater urging towards mutual compassion, He repeated the preposition. Then He followed this with those whose rights must be observed for Allah's sake, or for a meaning whose corruption results from neglecting it, namely the relationship between people. He began with what is due to Allah, because when that is sound, others follow. So He said: ﴿and the orphans and the needy﴾, that is, even if their kinship is not known; and He specified them because of their weakness. He placed the orphan first because he is weakest, since in his youth he is too weak to meet his own needs or to raise them to others; ﴿and the neighbour who is near of kin﴾, that is, because he has two rights; ﴿and the neighbour who is a stranger﴾ (p-277), that is, who has no kinship, because of the trial of living with him and the fear of his serious harm. The Prophet ﷺ said: "O Allah, I seek refuge in You from an evil neighbour in the abode of residence, for the neighbour of the desert moves away." ﴿and the companion by your side﴾, that is, the one close to you, the one who associates with you in some matter that requires the continuation of companionship; ﴿and the wayfarer﴾, that is, the traveller, because of his strangeness, the scarcity of his helpers, and his loneliness; ﴿and what your right hands possess﴾, that is, of slaves and female slaves likewise, for showing ihsan to them is a great act of obedience. The Prophet ﷺ's last words were: "The prayer, and what your right hands possess."

Since He mentioned ihsan, whose pillar is humility and generosity, He concluded the verse, encouraging it and warning against withholding it, giving the reason for the command to it, with His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, that is, with what He has of the Most Beautiful Names and the Exalted Attributes; ﴿does not love﴾, that is, He does not act as one who loves; ﴿whoever is self-deluded﴾, that is, arrogant, self-admiring, adorning himself with his finery, showing off with what Allah (Exalted) has given him of His bounty, in a manner of grandeur and contempt for others. He is too proud to be associated with his poor relatives, and he despises his neighbours when they are weak, so he does not show them ihsan, lest they approach him and he be shamed by them.

Since the self-deluded person may sometimes do good for show, He said, informing us that He accepts only what is sincere: ﴿boastful﴾, exaggerating in praising himself for his qualities, too proud to associate with the poor (p-278). In this is the most complete warning against the disposition that prevents ihsan, which is self-conceit toward the servants of Allah and boasting over them, belittling them. For there is no justification for this, since all come from a single soul, and bounty is a favour from Him, glorified is He, which must be thanked through humility so that it may endure, and whose ingratitude through boasting is to be feared, lest it be removed.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 37:

Since arrogance (ikhtiyal) and boasting (fakhr) over joy in fleeting accidents (a'rad faniya), and inclining toward them and relying upon them, were what drove people to stinginess (bukhl) out of fear of their loss, He said, describing them with a set of vile and manifest characters, the source of which is that: ﴿Those who are stingy﴾; that is, they inflict stinginess with the goods of this fleeting world that carried them to boasting and restricting it, so that it encompasses concealing knowledge and the like. Then He followed that with something worse than it, saying: ﴿and enjoin upon people stinginess﴾, out of hatred for generosity (sakha'). And the use of an expression derived from "nawas" (inclination, a sway) indicates that they do not attach their hopes to this except to those of base aspirations (himam safila) and deficient ranks (rutab qasira). It is also possible that the command is a metaphor (kinaya) for their driving others toward stinginess by what is seen of their arrogance and their boasting over them. Then He followed that with something more wicked than it, which is stinginess with speech, the loss of which is not feared, and denial of blessing, and showing neediness; so He said: ﴿and they conceal what Allah has given them﴾; that is, He who possesses majesty (al-Jalal) (p-279) and honor (al-Ikram); ﴿of His bounty﴾; that is, of knowledge; denying that they have anything to give generously. Al-Isfahani said: "Furthermore, this concealment may occur in a manner that necessitates disbelief, such as manifesting complaint against Allah - glorified and exalted be He - and not being content with the decree." Then He conjoined, upon: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not love﴾ [al-Nisa: 36], turning to the station of speech, as an indication of the extremity of anger and a specification of the one threatened, explicitly mentioning the manifestation of greatness, which was indicated there by the Greatest Name, saying: ﴿and We have prepared﴾; that is, We have readied and made ready; and the original would have been "for them"; but He said - generalizing, and attaching the ruling to the attribute, and informing that this carries one to disbelief -: ﴿for the disbelievers﴾; that is, by doing these traits; disbelief in its true sense, by what the adherence to base characters led them to; or in a figurative sense, by concealing the blessing; ﴿a humiliating punishment﴾; that is, because they were deceived by wealth, which drives to boasting, pride, and arrogance: "He who has in his heart an atom's weight of pride will not enter Paradise."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 38:

When he censured the stingy (al-muqtirin), he followed it with a censure of the extravagant (al-musrifin), the squanderers (al-mubadhdhirin). He said, by way of conjunction (ʿatfan) with "the disbelievers" (al-kafirin), or with "those who are stingy" (alladhina yabkhaluna) [al-Nisa’ 37], making clear that those who do not act with kindness in the manner commanded toward those whose kindness was previously enjoined are two groups: a group that withholds expenditure entirely, and a group that withholds its quality and performs it for show (riya'), thereby destroying its spirit. [He said]: ﴿And those who spend their wealth﴾; and he indicated the great eagerness they have for their spending (*p-280*) by his saying: ﴿their wealth﴾; and he pointed to the baseness of their aims and the lowness of their resolve by his saying: ﴿to be seen by people﴾; that is, due to the shortness of their outlook and its confinement to sensible things, like beasts that perceive only particulars that are witnessed.

When he mentioned the bringing forth of wealth in a manner that no person of intellect would approve, he mentioned the motive behind it, indicating that they belittled themselves by the very things with which they had magnified themselves. That is because they worshipped creatures and were arrogant toward their Creator, the Mighty, the Glorious. So he said: ﴿and they do not believe in Allah﴾, who is the Greatest King. And since those commanded to be treated kindly here, from among the parents and those mentioned with them, are more specific than those indicated in "al-Baqarah," he emphasized it by adding the negative particle, so he said: ﴿nor in the Last Day﴾, which is the motive toward every good and the restraint from every evil.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 39:

When the implied sense was: "So Satan became their companion, because of their disbelief, their self-admiration, and their arrogance," he followed it with His saying: ﴿And whoever takes Satan as a companion﴾ [al-Nisa': 38]; that is: while he is his enemy, far removed from every good, burning with every harm; ﴿then he is an evil companion﴾ [al-Nisa': 38], for he drives him toward every evil and keeps him far from every good. To this He alluded with His saying: ﴿Evil is the companion he has chosen﴾ [al-Nisa': 38].

When the implied sense was: "What then would be for them in disbelief and in spending to show off to one who has no harm or benefit in his hand?" he followed it with His saying, rebuking them and denouncing them: ﴿And what would it have cost them﴾; that is: of the smallest things and the greatest; ﴿had they believed in Allah﴾; that is: the One to whom belongs every perfection and in whose hand is everything; ﴿and the Last Day﴾, which drives one toward every righteousness; ﴿and spent﴾. Since He had described them as spending all their wealth on the lowly enemy, He pointed to their stinginess in what is for Allah, the Exalted, the Great, with a small thing through which they would gain abundant good, so He said: ﴿out of what Allah has provided them﴾, the One who possesses absolute richness and overwhelming generosity. When the implied sense was: "Then Allah was indeed Able over them, when they squandered their wealth," He followed it with His saying: ﴿And Allah has ever been of them All-Knowing﴾; that is: encompassing all attributes of perfection; ﴿of them﴾, that is: in both states; ﴿All-Knowing﴾; that is: of complete knowledge. And to inform of the greatness of His knowledge of them, He placed the prepositional phrase first, which implies exclusivity, in this place and not elsewhere.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 40:

When he had finished rebuking them, he said, giving the reason: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾; that is, the One who possesses every perfection, so He is the Absolutely Self-Sufficient (al-Ghani al-Mutlaq); ﴿does not wrong﴾; that is, it is inconceivable that any wrong at all should proceed from Him; ﴿an atom's weight﴾; that is, nor anything less than it. He mentioned it because it is a metaphor for nothingness (kinaya 'an al-'adam), since it is a proverb for smallness. That is, He does not diminish anyone's reward for what he has done, nor does He reward him for anything he did not do. So what then of the one who believes in Him, while He is (p-282) described by this supreme attribute?

When he mentioned the clearing of oneself of wrongdoing, he followed it with adorning oneself with grace (fadl), saying, conjoining it to what is implied, "If the atom is an evil deed, He does not add to it, and He requites it only with its like": ﴿And if﴾; and since the listener's eagerness for this was great, he omitted the nun (of takun) after omitting the conjoined element, to bring his aim closer, saying: ﴿it be﴾; that is, the weight of the atom. He made the verb feminine because it is attached to a feminine noun, and to belittle it, so that the multiplication of what is above it is understood a fortiori (min bab al-awla). This applies in the reading of the two Harams (Makkan and Madinan readers), with the rafʿ of ḥasana (hasanatan); that is, even if it is small; ﴿He doubles it﴾; that is, of its kind; by ten times its like; up to seventy; up to seven hundred fold; and more than that according to what is known of the goodness of the deed through the goodness of the intention; ﴿and gives from Himself﴾; that is, from the rare things He possesses; a bounty without deed, to whomever He wills. The Imam said: "In sum, that multiplication is an indication of bodily felicities, and this reward is an indication of spiritual felicities." ﴿a great reward﴾; and He named it a reward, though it is not of the same kind as that good deed, because it is founded upon faith. That is: whoever has this as his state, it is not fitting for any intelligent person to direct his resolve to anything but Him, nor to rely at all, in spending or otherwise, upon anything but Him.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 41:

When his warning about the Last Day was complete, and what he had mentioned of the manifestation of justice and its thorough elaboration, this became a cause for asking about the state of those who are rebuked in these verses at that time. So He said: ﴿How then﴾; that is, how will their state be, when they have carried loads like mountains of evil deeds; ﴿when We bring﴾; with Our greatness; ﴿from every nation a witness﴾; that is, one who testifies against them; ﴿and We bring you﴾; while you are the most noble of Our creation; ﴿against these﴾; that is, those to whom We sent you and whom We made you a witness over; ﴿as a witness﴾.

In the tafsir of al-Bukhari, from ʿAbd Allah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to me: ʻRecite to me.ʼ I said: ʻShall I recite to you, when it was revealed to you?ʼ He said: ʻI love to hear it from someone other than myself.ʼ So I recited to him Surat an-Nisa', until I reached: ﴿How then, when We bring from every nation a witness, and We bring you against these as a witness﴾. He said: ʻStop.ʼ And behold, his eyes were shedding tears."

Then he began the answer to that with His saying: ﴿On that day﴾; that is, when the witnesses stand; ﴿those who disbelieved will wish﴾; that is, those who concealed what the intellects guide to from His signs; and he showed that they are addressed regarding the subsidiary laws (al-furu') in His saying: ﴿and disobeyed the Messenger﴾; after concealing what He had made manifest of His clear proofs; ﴿if only the earth were leveled over them﴾; that is, it would become even and level over them; and it would not be so unless it had covered them and become level with them, (p-284) and nothing of crookedness or protrusion remained in it because of any one of them, or because of any part of their bodies. They only wished that out of fear of the disgrace that awaits them through their reproach, and then the humiliation through their punishment.

Since the implied sense is: "so they will not be leveled over them," he joined to it His saying: ﴿and they will not conceal from Allah﴾; that is, from the Greatest King; ﴿any statement﴾; that is, anything they invent; rather, they will be exposed through their evil reports, and they will bear the full burden of their sins, as a recompense for what they used to conceal of His signs and of the clear proofs set before people.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 43:

When He described standing before Him on the Day of Presentation, with its terrors, in which the force of His majesty and might drives one to wish for non-existence, and the power of His dominion and compulsion prevents anyone from concealing a word, and when His description implied that no one will be saved on that Day except one whose heart and limbs are pure through faith in Him and obedience to His Messenger (ﷺ), He described standing before Him in this world, in the station of intimacy and the presence of holiness, which saves one from the terror of standing on that Day. In this station, the meanings of gentleness and beauty arise, so that one does not turn to other than Him. He commanded purity while adorning oneself with this standing, away from impurities. So He said: ﴿O you who believe﴾, meaning: those who affirm by believing in the messengers and in what they brought from Allah. Its foremost and most important part is (p-285) that you do not associate anything with Him, of any kind of association. ﴿Do not approach the prayer﴾, meaning: do not be in its place, let alone perform it. ﴿While you are﴾, meaning: while you are in the state of ﴿intoxicated (sukara)﴾, that is, absent of mind due to wine or something similar. For the tongue is likely to outrun one, when Satan gains control through the loss of reason, to some form of association, and so it becomes verbal shirk, even if the heart is at rest in faith. Thus it is likely that this will be presented to one on the Great Day of Standing, for the one before whom you stand does not leave any word unrecorded. Then whoever his tongue uttered that with will wish, because of the pain he will suffer, that he had been among the people of non-existence. The root of "sukr" (intoxication) in the lexicon is blocking the way. The occasion of revelation is what Musaddad related with a chain of transmission, which our shaykh al-Busiri said has reliable narrators, from 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, that a man from the Ansar invited him and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, may Allah be pleased with him, and they were given wine to drink before wine was prohibited. 'Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, led them in the Maghrib prayer and recited ﴿Say: O you disbelievers﴾ [al-Kafirun: 1], and then this verse was revealed. This is how he related it. The authors of the Four Sunan collections (al-Sunan al-Thalatha) and Ahmad, 'Abd ibn Humayd, al-Bazzar, al-Hakim and al-Tabari also related it, and they clarified the intended meaning, which is that the one who led them in prayer recited: "I do not worship what you worship" (a'bud ma ta'buduna), while in the narration of al-Tirmidhi it is: "We worship what you worship" (wa nahnu na'budu ma ta'buduna).

(p-286) When the prohibition against approaching it in this state implied that the prohibition ends with its ending, he stated it explicitly in His words: ﴿until﴾, meaning: this prohibition remains in force until ﴿you know what you are saying﴾, with the removal of intoxication, so that no alteration (tabdil) will occur from you at that time. According to al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, the intended meaning of "prayer" is the prayer itself and its place, which is the mosque. This is among his proofs for using a term in both its literal and metaphorical senses. He forbade the intoxicated person from praying until he comprehends, that is, until he becomes sober, and he forbade each one of them from being in the mosque while in a state of janabah (ritual impurity), by His words, coordinated with the place of "while you are intoxicated" (wa antum sukara) as a conjunction: ﴿nor [approach it] while you are in janabah﴾, meaning: do not approach the prayer by being in its places, let alone performing it, ﴿in a state of janabah﴾, meaning: having emitted semen, by action or by near potential, through the meeting of the two circumcised parts, because janabah is semen, whether it is from intercourse or not, in any of the states of janabah. ﴿Except as travellers﴾, meaning: passing through without staying or praying. When He limited the prohibition of janabah with His words ﴿until you wash yourselves﴾, meaning: until you wash the body deliberately. Since a person has states in which using water is difficult or impossible, He mentioned them, saying, arranging them from the most in need of a concession to the least: ﴿And if you are ill﴾, meaning: with a wound or otherwise, an illness that prevents seeking or using water, ﴿or on a journey﴾, likewise, whether the journey is long or short, ﴿or one of you comes from the place of relieving oneself (al-ghait)﴾, meaning: (p-287) O believers, even if one is present and healthy. Al-ghait is the lowland of the earth, the open area used for relieving oneself; that is, or one comes from relieving oneself and has fulfilled a need that is unavoidable for him, so he is in greater need of relief from what follows.

When the matter of janabah, which is semen, was mentioned in a general way, whether it arises from intercourse or otherwise, He mentioned here what includes it and other things from another aspect, saying: ﴿or you have touched women﴾, meaning: by mere contact of the two skins, or by intercourse, whether or not emission occurs. He placed this later because it is something one can do without, and it does not recur as frequently as the need to relieve oneself. ﴿And you find no water﴾, meaning: either by its absence or by inability to use it. ﴿Then perform tayammum﴾, meaning: intend sincerely, by engaging with intention, ﴿with clean earth (sa'id)﴾, meaning: dust, ﴿clean (tayyiban)﴾, meaning: pure and unmixed, so that it is suitable for producing vegetation: ﴿And the good land brings forth its vegetation by the permission of its Lord﴾ [al-A'raf: 58]. ﴿Then wipe﴾. This is a worship specific to this community.

Since dust cannot reach all of a limb, even if a person makes effort in that, He introduced the preposition bi (with) in His words, as a restrictor of the verb: ﴿your faces﴾, meaning: apply the wiping with them, whether the dust covers the hair-growth area or not, ﴿and your hands﴾, meaning: with dust from it (p-288), as He stated explicitly in al-Ma'idah, not "in it" nor "on it" for example, so that rolling in dust (al-tama'uk) is understood, or so that a stone, for example, suffices. Al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, also permitted that "touching" (mulamasa) be understood as mere touching, which is the literal meaning of lams, that is, the meeting of two skins, and as intercourse, which is caused by touching; or it is a specific contact, in which case it is the naming of the whole by the name of a part.

When He prohibited what brings one close to committing the sin, which is letting the tongue utter what is not fitting for Him, glorified and exalted is He, and lightened what was severe by tayammum, He concluded the verse with His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, meaning: He who is singled out for perfection, ﴿is ever Pardoning﴾, meaning: by leaving punishment for sin, and it seems this relates to what occurred in the state of intoxication, ﴿Forgiving﴾, meaning: by leaving punishment and erasing the sin, so that it is not mentioned at all afterward. It seems this relates to tayammum, for prayer with it is good, and without it would have been a remembered sin for which one would be punished, either for abandoning it because of the hardship of using water when one is lax, or for performing it without purification in some aspects of excessive strictness. This is the meaning of His words, glorified and exalted is He, in al-Ma'idah: ﴿Allah does not intend to make any difficulty for you﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 6]. Whoever's custom is pardon and forgiveness is one who makes things easy, not one who makes them difficult.

When the conclusion of this verse made clear that severity in the rulings leads to transgression, and transgression leads to retribution, he confirmed this with the situation of the Jews, whose burdens (*āṣār*, the heavy restrictions in their law) required the punishment of the Fire. So he said, so that this would encourage acceptance of the obligations mentioned earlier because of their ease and in hope of reward, and would warn against abandoning them out of fear of punishment, and so that the speech would be sweet, pleasing and bright through the varied arrangement of its composition, sometimes with rulings and sometimes with great narratives, so that the mind would be refreshed and the disposition strengthened: ﴿Have you not seen﴾. Or it may be said: when He, glory be to Him and exalted, warned in what preceded about the People of the Scripture, with His words, glory be to Him and exalted, ﴿And those who follow their desires wish that you deviate with a great deviation﴾ [An-Nisa: 27]; and it passed on until He revealed this concerning one who, not deliberately, distorted the words from their places merely with his tongue during prayer, He followed it with an explicit expression of wonder at the state of those who distort with the heart and the tongue, deliberately and with hostility, presuming against God, glory be to Him and exalted, and alluding through the preceding verse to their desire to lead us astray from the path we have been guided to through their practices. So He said: ﴿Have you not seen﴾.

Since they were in a place of distance from His noble presence because of the curse upon them, He used the particle of reaching (*ilā*), whether the seeing was visual or of the heart, and said: ﴿to those who were given﴾. He belittled their matter by using the passive form and by His words: ﴿a portion of the Scripture﴾, that is, like Shas ibn Qays, who wanted to stir discord among the Ansar. In this is the indication that the least portion of the Scripture is sufficient to condemn misguidance, because it is sufficient for guidance. (p-290) ﴿They purchase﴾, that is, they exert themselves and insist, with what they have of worldly leadership, of wealth and status, to take ﴿the misguidance﴾, turning away from guidance and never mentioning it in any way. A major cause of much of this is what is in their religion of burdens and weights, as His words, glory be to Him and exalted, indicate: ﴿Then there succeeded them a generation who neglected prayer﴾ [Maryam: 59], that is, because of the severity imposed on them in it, by which it is performed only in the place built for it, and by other kinds of hardship. Likewise the other matters alluded to by His words, glory be to Him and exalted: ﴿for their breaking of their covenant﴾ [Al-Ma'idah: 13], and other things. Among the greatest of these is their concealing the description of the Prophet ﷺ, in order to draw near to their own religious community and to take bribes from them for that, and to make them their leaders over themselves.

When He mentioned their misguidance, which entails their misleading others, He followed it with what shows their deep immersion in it. So He said, addressing those toward whom their aspirations for misleading could be directed: ﴿And they wish that you go astray﴾, that is, O you who believe, ﴿the way﴾, so that you become equal to them. Therefore they remind you of enmities, rancors and sorrows, as Shas did, not out of love for you, and they cast doubt upon you. God, glory be to Him and exalted, is most knowing of them, (p-291) and He warned you of them with His words ﴿They spare no effort to corrupt you﴾ [Al 'Imran: 118] and what follows it, up to here.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 45:

﴿Allah﴾; i.e., whose knowledge and power encompass all things; ﴿is best aware﴾; i.e., more than anyone; ﴿of your enemies﴾; i.e., all of them, these and others; with what He knows of the inner secrets. So whoever warns you against any of them, whoever he may be, then beware of him.

Since each of the two tribes of the Ansar had allied with some of the Jews, in order to gain strength through them and to seek their support, He (exalted be He), turning them away from their alliance with them, said: ﴿And sufficient is﴾; i.e., and the situation is that it is sufficient with Him (so was the original structure); but He manifested the Greatest Name (al-ism al-a'zam) so that His greatness would be brought to mind and the matter of the enemies would be made to seem insignificant; so He said: ﴿Allah as a Protector (waliyyan)﴾; i.e., a near one, by doing everything that a near and compassionate protector does.

Since the protector may have the strength of support while the helper may not have the compassion of a protector, and since support is the greatest thing for which one needs a protector, He singled it out for mention, to make known that both qualities are combined; repeating the verb and the Greatest Name, out of concern for this matter, He said: ﴿And sufficient is Allah﴾; i.e., He to whom belongs all greatness; ﴿as a helper (naseeran)﴾; i.e., for whoever takes Him as protector; so the enmity of anyone does not harm him. So trust in His protection and His support rather than theirs, and do not care about any of them, nor anyone else, for He suffices you all.

(p-292) When these verses had sufficiently stirred up the motives for identifying those who intend to lead astray, He said, after the interjection placed between the explanatory and the explained clauses, for the greater emphasis placed on it: ﴿Among those who are Jews﴾; then He explained what they go astray with and lead others astray with, by His saying — and it is permissible that it be a resumption (isti'naf), meaning: some of them, or among them are those who: ﴿distort the words﴾; that is, what their law brought of the description of the unlettered Prophet (ﷺ), the description of his religion and his community, and other matters that they wish to distort for some purpose; so they contrive to bend it and alter it from its limit and its direction to another limit, going beyond it ﴿from their places﴾. And since, when a word is altered, the speech that follows it is affected — and it is the intended thing in itself — He drew attention to this by making the pronoun masculine, so He said: ﴿its places﴾; that is, the places for which it is most suitable. Thus their going astray and their leading others astray is complete. This includes both the case where the altered meaning is distant from the original and the case where it is near; but what is in "al-Ma'idah" is more specific.

Since He — glorified and exalted — knows all of their distortion, He indicated it by conjunction with what is understood to be: "so they say this; and they say that": ﴿And they say: We have heard﴾; that is, what you say; ﴿and we disobey﴾; giving the impression that this is a report of what happened to their forefathers long ago, whereas they only mean that they themselves heard what you say and deliberately opposed it, so that whoever hears this may think that they are well-informed in the opposition, by virtue of the divine knowledge they possess, so that this causes him doubt about his affair and bewilderment regarding his matter. ﴿And hear﴾, while you are ﴿not made to hear﴾; giving the impression that he is not made to hear what he dislikes, from their saying: "So-and-so made so-and-so hear the speech" — whereas they only mean the supplication, as one says: "Hear, may you not hear!" ﴿And [say] Ra'ina﴾; giving the impression that they intend consideration and attentiveness toward them, whereas they only mean insult by means of foolishness (ru'una). Al-Asfahani said: It is possibly a word resembling a Hebrew expression which they used to revile one another with, namely "ra'ina." Thus they — mocking the religion and deriding the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) — addressed him with speech that admits of a meaning, intending by it insult and humiliation, while displaying reverence and honor. Therefore He said: ﴿distorting with their tongues﴾; that is, turning them away from the articulation points of the letters that are proper to them in Arabic toward what the Hebrews do, namely thickening some letters and mixing some with others, for the purpose of meanings that are ugly among them, while these words also admit of other meanings that the Arabs intend, which are fine; ﴿and slander against the religion﴾; that is, by what they interpret it as for those whom they hope to deceive with those wicked meanings.

When He mentioned these addressed words, He explained what would have been their state had they stopped (p-294), so He said — cutting off their argument: ﴿And if they had said﴾; that is, in answer to him (ﷺ): ﴿We have heard and we obey﴾; that is, in place of the first word; ﴿and hear, and look at us﴾; in place of what follows it; ﴿it would have been﴾; that is, this saying; ﴿better for them﴾; that is, than that; because they would not have incurred sin; ﴿and more upright﴾; that is, because there would be no possibility of blame; ﴿but Allah has cursed them﴾; that is, has expelled them, He who possesses all attributes of greatness and perfection, and has removed them far from good; ﴿because of their disbelief﴾; that is, because of their baseness in covering up the lights of truth and the signs of goodness; so they did not say that.

Since their expulsion is the cause of the continuation of their disbelief, He said: ﴿So they do not believe﴾; that is, a faith would not be renewed for them; ﴿except a few﴾; that is, of them, as an exception from the waw (of the verb), for they do believe; or it is an exception that is emptied from the verbal noun of "yu'minu," meaning: from their faith in some of the verses, which does not benefit them because of their disbelief in the rest.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 47:

When He had rebuked them for their deeds and their words, and had explicitly cursed them, He warned them that this would be made manifest in tangible forms. So He said, turning toward them with the approach of anger: ﴿O you who﴾, calling them from a place of distance, ﴿have been given the Book﴾. He did not attribute the giving to Himself, to belittle them, and He did not limit the address to a portion of it, because in establishing agreement with the Book, only the whole of it suffices. ﴿Believe in what We have sent down﴾, that is, gradually, just as We sent down the Torah, ﴿in accordance with what We possess of greatness, which has become manifest in its inimitability (i'jaz), in its reporting of unseen matters, in the subtleties of its knowledge that are in your possession and beyond, along with its elegance and conciseness.› He informed them of their obstinacy and envy with His words: ﴿confirming what is with you﴾, since they have it present in their minds and acknowledge it in itself.

When He had commanded them and cut off their argument, He warned them. So He said, lightening the matter for them through the use of the preposition (ḥarf al-jarr) [min] to indicate that whenever faith occurs from them at a time before the effacement, He would postpone it from them: ﴿before We efface﴾, that is, obliterate, ﴿faces﴾. Indeed, ṭams (الطَّمْسَ) in the language means erasure, and it applies also to altering some of the modes. Then He stated the consequence of this: ﴿and turn them﴾. The implied sense is: "before We obliterate the traces of faces by turning them," ﴿back on their backs﴾, that is, by making what faces the front of the head face the back, and what faces the back face the front, while keeping the form of the face as it is. Or the intended meaning of turning them back upon their backs is transferring them from one state to what is below it, its opposite, by making them in the condition of the nape, having no feature in them, neither mouth nor anything else, so that the meaning of effacement is wiping out what is in the face of features. Ibn Hisham said: "Nat̤mis (نَطْمِسَ): we wipe them out and level them, so that no eye, nose, mouth, or anything seen in a face is visible in them." Similarly, ﴿So We obliterated their eyes﴾ [al-Qamar: 37]. One whose eye is ṭamus is one between whose eyelids there is no slit. It is said: "I erased the book and the trace," so nothing of it is seen. In this interpretation the face remains in its literal sense.

Then He warned them of another kind of effacement, saying, conjoining it to "We turn them" (naruddahā): ﴿or curse them﴾, that is, We remove them far from the human form by transforming their faces or their entire selves into the form of apes, ﴿as We cursed the people of the Sabbath﴾, when We said to them: "Be apes, despised." In this last interpretation the word "face" is an expression for the whole person, so it is used both literally and figuratively. It is also permissible that "faces" means the chief of the dignitaries, in which case the return of the pronoun to it is istikhdam (a device in which a word is taken in one sense and its pronoun in another). The intended meaning of turning them back upon their backs would then be making them the lowest and most debased of the base. And God, glory be to Him, knows best.

When this was a strange matter and a wondrous power, and the sense was: "The command of God concerning them with this has been carried out, as you know," He followed it with information that His power is comprehensive and that the aspects of His acts are not limited. So He said, conjoining it to what you have supposed: ﴿And the command of God is ever accomplished﴾, that is, His judgment, His decree, and His will in every matter He wills concerning them and others, with this and other than this, because He possesses a greatness that has no limit and a majesty that descriptions fall short of. ﴿Accomplished﴾, that is, existing inevitably, with no possibility of failure at all. Therefore one of the two matters must occur, if they do not believe. Since some of them did believe, it cannot be sound that they did not believe, for faith has occurred from them.

When they were committing great sins while saying, "We will be forgiven," and their obedience to their rabbis (aḥbār) and monks (ruhbān) in distorting [the religion] was a form of *shirk* (association of partners with God), as He, glorified and exalted is He, said: ﴿They took their rabbis and their monks as lords besides Allah﴾ [at-Tawbah: 31]. He said, giving the reason for confirming their threat and informing that what was pointed to regarding their distortion led them to *shirk*: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, i.e., the One who combines the attributes of greatness, ﴿does not forgive that partners be associated with Him﴾, i.e., in the sense of continual renewal until death, whether the associator is among the People of the Book or not. What adds beauty to this is that it occurs in the context of: ﴿Worship Allah and associate nothing with Him﴾ [an-Nisa': 36].

When He informed of His justice, He informed of His bounty, so He said: ﴿And He forgives what is less than that﴾, i.e., the great, momentous matter, of every act of disobedience, whether minor or major, whether its doer repents or not. And with His saying, informing that He is free in His choice and nothing is obligatory upon Him, He instilled awe: ﴿for whom He wills﴾.

Since the implied meaning was, "Indeed, whoever associates partners with Allah has strayed far astray," He followed it with His saying: ﴿And whoever associates partners with Allah﴾, i.e., there comes to be from him *shirk* at present or in the outcome; as for the past, repentance cuts it off. ﴿With Allah﴾, i.e., the One besides whom everything is, ﴿has certainly fabricated﴾, i.e., deliberately invented a lie, ﴿a great sin﴾, i.e., manifest in itself, in terms of its greatness, in that it has filled the regions of his self, heart, spirit and body, while displaying to others that it is a sin. Thus within itself it proclaims that it is falsehood, and he persists in it, so it leaves no place for reconciliation, and wisdom does not require pardoning him, because it is an affront to the King. He omitted the premise of straying and mentioned the premise of fabrication because the context concerns the People of the Book, whose straying is with knowledge, deliberate intent, and obstinacy, unlike what comes concerning the Arabs. In the use of the present tense there is restraint together with appeal, attraction, and inspiring of awe.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 49:

Since this indicates that those meant by these verses from among the People of the Book are the most misguided of people, and since they used to claim that they were the most rightly guided of people, He marvelled at them, denouncing them after their fabrication of self-praise. So He said: ﴿Have you not seen﴾, and He made them more remote by His saying: ﴿those who claim purity for themselves﴾, that is, with what does not belong to them, such as their saying: ﴿The Fire will not touch us except for a few days﴾ [al-Baqarah: 80], and their saying: ﴿None will enter Paradise except those who are Jews or Christians﴾ [al-Baqarah: 111], and His saying: ﴿and they love to be praised for what they have not done﴾ [Al 'Imran: 188], ﴿And those who follow their desires want you to deviate into a great deviation﴾ [al-Nisa': 27]. For the distancing of others (p-299) into deviation justifies their claiming purity for themselves falsely, and similar to that, of what has preceded and other than it.

Since the meaning of the denunciation is: "That is not theirs, because they lied in it and did wrong," He indicated it by His saying: ﴿Rather, God﴾, that is, the One who possesses the attributes of perfection, ﴿purifies whom He wills﴾, that is, by what He possesses of perfect knowledge, all-encompassing power, profound wisdom, and upright justice, through praise of him, and by creating the meanings of goodness that appear in him, so that righteous deeds arise from them. So when He purifies one of His chosen ones with something, such as prophethood, it is his to purify himself with that, in order to lead people to what benefits them from God. ﴿And they will not be wronged a thread﴾, that is, while those whom He purifies, or whom He makes pure, are not ﴿wronged a thread﴾, that is, the measure of what is in the cleft of a date-stone of that thing which is split; that is, a little, nor a great deal, because He knows what they deserve, and He is the Just Judge, free of injustice, because He possesses the attributes of perfection.

When God (exalted is He) informed that purification belongs to Him alone, by virtue of His greatness and all-encompassing knowledge, and this was a matter not in dispute, and He testified against them to their misguidance, and it was established that this is His speech, by virtue of its inimitability in both its expansive and concise modes, their lying was thereby proven. So He intensified their rebuke, and said, expressing wonder to His Messenger ﷺ at their audacity and boldness toward One who knows their falsehood and is able to hasten their punishment, and making clear that he ﷺ is in the presence [of God], after having clarified their remoteness from Him: ﴿Look how they invent lies against God﴾; i.e., they deliberately do so; ﴿against God﴾; i.e., the One from whom nothing is hidden and whom nothing can overpower; ﴿the lie﴾; i.e., without fear on their part of any consequence for it; ﴿and sufficient is that as a manifest sin﴾; i.e., the state being that it is sufficient, ﴿as a sin﴾ — i.e., by this lie — ﴿manifest﴾; i.e., evident in itself, and proclaiming its falsehood.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 51:

When He marvelled at their lying, He indicated it by His saying: ﴿Have you not seen?﴾ The original would have been "to them," but He said "to those who..." for the sake of added rebuke, reproach, and informing that their disbelief is obstinacy, since it stems from knowledge: ﴿to those who﴾. He used "to" (ila), indicating their distance from the noble presence: ﴿were given a portion of the Book﴾, that is, the Book which is in reality the Book, because it is from Allah. ﴿They believe in jibt﴾, which is the idol, the soothsayer, the sorcerer, whatever has no good in it, and everything worshipped besides Allah, ﴿and ṭāghūt﴾, which is al-Lat, al-'Uzza, the soothsayer, the devil, every head of misguidance, the idols, and everything worshipped besides Allah. All these meanings may be intended here, and they are among the things forbidden in their Book. Its root and its core is transgressing the limit in hostility, and it is singular, though it may also be plural. He, glorified and exalted, said: ﴿Their allies are the ṭāghūt; they bring them out﴾ [al-Baqarah: 257]. And the fact is that the least portion of the Book is sufficient for the prohibition of that and for declaring its doer a disbeliever.

(p-301) When He indicated their misguidance, He indicated their leading others astray, by His saying, expressing it in the present tense to show that they have not repented: ﴿And they say to those who disbelieved﴾. The use of the demonstrative expression rather than direct address indicates that they say this about them even in their absence, since there is nothing prompting them to say it except pure disbelief. So He said: ﴿"These"﴾, that is, the disbelievers who worship idols, ﴿"are better guided"﴾, that is, more upright in guidance, ﴿"than those who believed"﴾, that is, those who achieved this truth. Their condemnation is thus understood through the comparison with those who believe, and those above them by way of a fortiori reasoning, ﴿"in the way"﴾. Yet in their Book there is—the nullification of polytheism, its demolition, the blaming of its adherents, and its condemnation—in more than one place, as a most emphatic affirmation and a severe, grave matter.

When this brought about their disgrace, He said: ﴿Those are they whom Allah has cursed﴾; that is, those distanced from the divine presences; ﴿whom Allah has cursed﴾; that is, He expelled them by all that He possesses of the attributes of perfection, an expulsion that they deserve to be singled out for. And since their purpose in this statement was to support the polytheists, and the implied sense is: "so they obtained by that curse humiliation and abasement," He followed it with His words: ﴿And whoever Allah curses﴾; that is, the King to whom all command belongs, among them and among others; ﴿you will not find for him any helper﴾; that is, at any time whatsoever at all. He repeated the expression by the Greatest Name, because the context requires it, to indicate the extremity of disbelief (kufr), which is the greatest of the sins, by the extremity of wrath.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 53:

Since the implied sense was: "Thus it is that their being subjected to humiliation and abasement came about," he joined to it His saying: ﴿Or﴾; that is: "Is it that"; ﴿they have a share﴾; that is: a single share; ﴿of the kingdom? Then⁠﻿ they would not give the people﴾; that is: those who believed; ﴿a speck﴾; that is: anything of the worldly life; nor of the Hereafter, whether of guidance or of anything else. And "naqir" is the pit on the back of a date-stone. It has been said: it is an extreme of smallness, so it is a metaphor for non-existence. This is an explanation that, because of the extremity of their stinginess, they are fit only for the humiliation they are in; so how [could they attain] the rank of kingship? For kingship and stinginess do not come together.

[p. 303] **Am**, that is: they have no share at all in dominion. Rather, their humiliation is constant, their abasement is perpetual and lasting. So they ﴿envy the people﴾, that is, Muhammad (ﷺ), who combined the virtues of all people, from the first to the last, and whom Allah has further exalted beyond them in whatever way He willed. Or it means the Arabs, who now have no people other than themselves, since ﴿We have preferred them over the worlds﴾. They wish that their humiliation would last forever, as dominion remained theirs. The extremity of their envy is indicated by the particle of elevation, ʿalā (عَلى, "upon"), in His words ﴿for what Allah has given them﴾, that is, through what He possesses of the attributes of perfection, ﴿of His bounty﴾. They envied them because they saw the ascendancy of their ancestor, the emergence of their good fortune, and that they were the masters of the people and the leaders of those who possess generosity and courage:

*Surely the noble, when you meet them, are envied,*
*and you will never see the base among people envying.*

Allah, glorified and exalted, had given them every kind of dominion, for it is of three types: dominion over both outward and inward matters together, which belongs to the prophets, peace be upon them, by virtue of their utmost generosity, magnanimity, mercy, compassion, intercession, kindness, and gentleness, each of which is a cause of submission, along with their complete connection to Allah, glorified and exalted; dominion over outward matters only, which is the dominion of kings; and dominion over inward matters only, which is the dominion of scholars.

Since He, glorified and exalted, first censured them for ignorance and self-praise, claiming what had not been given to them, which is the cause of all deficiencies; second, for something greater than that: withholding the right from its people out of stinginess; and third, for something greater than both: wishing that no blessing should reach anyone, even though it does not diminish them. Thus they gathered the worst of blameworthy qualities, while bad qualities lower a person and good qualities raise him. From this there arose in the listener an expectation of the exaltation of the Arabs and the perpetuation of the humiliation of the Jews and their death through their envy. So He said ﴿Fa-qad (So indeed)﴾, that is, as a consequence of this, and this is followed by ﴿We had given﴾, which was the original form, but He expressed it differently to draw attention to the description they shared with them in deserving virtues. So He said ﴿We had given﴾, that is, by the greatness that is ours, ﴿the family of Ibrahim﴾, that is, the one of whom We informed you in your Book that We swore to him that We would honor his descendants and guide them, and that We would make his son Isma'il prevail over all the borders of his brothers, and his hand over all people, and his hand over everyone, and the hand of each one with him. ﴿The Book﴾, that is, the one for which there is no true book except it, because of its preservation and excellence, by its inimitability and decisive distinction; ﴿and wisdom﴾, that is, prophethood, whose fruit is sound action grounded in refined, verified, and firm knowledge; ﴿and We gave them, along with that, a great dominion﴾, that is, vast, extensive, and enduring until the Hour comes.

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 55:**

﴿So among them﴾; that is, from the family of Ibrahim (Abraham); ﴿those who believed in him﴾; and they are the majority of the Arabs; ﴿and among them are those who turned away from him﴾; that is, they turned away themselves and also barred others; such as the Banu Isra'il (Children of Israel) and some of the Arabs.

Since it is known from the context that the one who reviles him is dead through his envy, without harming him in any worldly matter, and since the intended meaning, to explain their state in the Hereafter, is: "So We decreed that the Fire be kindled with them, after humiliation in this abode, and disgrace and lowliness," He connected to it His saying (p-305) ﴿and sufficient is Hell as a blaze﴾; that is, a kindling and a flaring at the utmost degree of burning, intensity, and swiftness in harm. In the verse of the taghut (false deity, idolatrous power), they permitted the exchange of the religion, which is nothing more precious to a person, in their testimony to the disbelievers that they were guided. In the verse of sovereignty, there is an indication that they are at the lowest point of stinginess with the base, perishing thing. In the verse of envy, it shows that settling in the lowest depth of stinginess with what they were given, together with wealth, was not enough for them, until they sank even lower than that through envy of the one whom God gave what does not diminish them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 56:

When He had established the Fire for those who turn away from Him, He gave the reason for it with His words: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved in Our verses﴾; that is, they concealed what their intellects had made manifest, by means of them; ﴿We will surely burn them in Fire﴾; that is, with a threat that is established, even if the respite lasts long with it; ﴿Fire﴾. And since the Fire, as we know it, consumes and annihilates, He resumed His statement, refuting that (notion), with: ﴿Every time their skins are roasted﴾; that is, they become, through its heat, in the state of cooked flesh that is ready to be eaten; so they become like dead flesh that is in a wound, which feels no pain; ﴿We will replace them﴾; that is, We will give them; ﴿other skins﴾; that is, other than the roasted ones, in place of them; by restoring them to what they were before the Fire was applied to them. (p-306) This is like when you make a ring from a ring in a different form: it is still the first, because the silver is one, and yet it is other than it, because the form is different. Likewise the second skin is different from the roasted one in form; ﴿so that they may taste the punishment﴾; that is, the owners of the skins, who are the intended recipients of the punishment; ﴿the punishment﴾; that is, so that the renewal of its tasting may continue for them, and so that the witnessing of the return after decay is renewed for them at every moment, just as they used to renew their denial of that at every moment; so that the recompense may be of the same kind as the deed. For if He did not restore from them what had weakened, their weakness would bring them to decay; and if any part of them decayed, they would all decay, and their punishment would be cut off.

Since this is a matter of which the like has not been known, He indicated His power over it with His words: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾; that is, the Supreme King; ﴿is﴾; and has never ceased to be; ﴿Mighty﴾; that is, He overcomes everything, and nothing overcomes Him; ﴿Wise﴾; that is, He perfects His work; so their punishment was made proportionate to their sins, because their resolve was to persist in what deserved that for as long as they lived.

When he had mentioned the threat of punishment (*tarhib*, warning of punishment) for the disbelievers, he followed it with the encouragement (*targhib*, promise of reward) for the believers, so he said: ﴿And those who believe﴾; that is, who affirm faith; ﴿and do righteous deeds﴾; as a demonstration of the sincerity of their faith; ﴿We will admit them﴾; that is, by a promise that does not fail. Perhaps the use of *sin* (the particle of near future) for their admission, rather than *sawfa* (the particle of distant future), as with the disbelievers, indicates that they are the shortest of the nations in duration, or that they are the shortest-lived of them, as a relief for them from the abode of turbidity to the place of purity; and that they will enter Paradise before all the other saved groups among the people of the Standing (the Judgment). ﴿Gardens﴾; that is, orchards. He described them with what sustains their delight and magnifies their freshness and blossoming, so he said: ﴿beneath which rivers flow﴾; that is, their land is in the utmost state of irrigation, every place in it being suitable for a river to flow from it.

When he mentioned their existence and what sustains their permanence, he followed it with what souls desire of continuous residence therein, so he said: ﴿abiding therein forever﴾ [an-Nisa: 122]. When he described the goodness of the abode, he mentioned the goodness of the companions, so he said: ﴿For them therein are spouses﴾. The regular usage in describing the plural of paucity (*jam' al-qillah*) for rational beings is the *alif* and *ta'* ending (*al-alif wa'l-ta'*); here he departed from that to the singular form, to indicate that, because of their great harmony in purity, they are like one single entity. Thus it is said: ﴿purified﴾; that is, their purity is continuous, never found at any time to be otherwise.

Since gardens in this world are not beautiful except when the sun reaches them, and the sun removes the shade, causing it to move to another place, and its heat sometimes causes harm, he gave assurance against that in them by his saying: ﴿And We will admit them﴾; that is, into them; ﴿to shade﴾; that is, great shade; and he emphasized it by his saying: ﴿dense﴾; that is, continuous, without any gap in it, spread out without any constriction with it, permanently; the sun never reaches it at any time, and there is neither heat nor cold in it, but it is in the utmost moderation.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 58:

Since this surah had already commanded kindness and justice toward women and orphans, in inheritance and otherwise, and in matters of blood, property, speech, and action, and since it had mentioned the treachery of the People of the Book and the punishment that befell them for it, and mentioned that He had given this Ummah dominion, which requires rule, and had given them wisdom after their ignorance and weakness, He turned to them with His delightful address. After promising them His noble reward for obeying His command, He concluded with the shade promised for justice, in the hadith: "Seven will be shaded by Allah in His shade." So He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, that is, the One who possesses the attributes of perfection; ﴿commands you﴾, that is, O Ummah; ﴿to render trusts (amanat, "trusts," i.e., whatever is owed to another) to their owners﴾, that is, without any treachery, as the People of the Book did in concealing what they had and reporting other than it. The "amanah" (trust) is everything that is owed to another from you.

Since He had commanded what is due to a person in himself, He commanded what is due to him in dealing with others. (p-309) He confirmed for them what they had not been aspiring to regarding dominion, by His saying, using the particle of emphasis and conjoining two things to two things: ﴿And when you judge﴾. He made clear the generality of their dominion over all nations by His saying: ﴿between people﴾. He stated what was commanded by His saying: ﴿to judge with justice﴾, that is, with equity, by commanding whoever is obligated to a right to render it to the one to whom it belongs, for that is among the greatest of righteous deeds that necessitate a good resting place in the perfect shade. Al-Shaykhan (Bukhari and Muslim) and others narrated from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Seven will be shaded by Allah in His shade on a day when there is no shade but His: a just ruler..." and the hadith continues.

When He informed them of His command, He increased their desire by His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, again expressing Himself with the Greatest Name (al-Ism al-A'zam, "the Greatest Name"); ﴿how excellent﴾, that is, how excellent a great thing; ﴿is that with which He admonishes you﴾. He urged them to hasten to good compliance by His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, repeating this noble name so that they would strive to ascend in purity of character to a degree no one else had reached. Since the Watcher over trusts must necessarily have hearing and knowledge, He said: ﴿was﴾, that is, He has always been and still is, (p-310) ﴿All-Hearing﴾, that is, of perfect hearing for everything they say, in response to His command and otherwise; ﴿All-Seeing﴾, that is, of perfect sight and knowledge of everything they do in this matter and otherwise, whether of compliance or other than it.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 59:

When He, glory be to Him, had commanded justice, encouraged it, and warned against abandoning it, He commanded obedience to those who are placed in charge of it, which brings them to be gentle with people and compassionate toward them. So He said: ﴿O you who have believed﴾; that is, who have affirmed faith. He began with what is the foundation for compelling people to this, saying: ﴿Obey﴾; that is, by complying with the command, confirming your claim of faith; ﴿Allah﴾; that is, in what He has commanded you in His Book, bearing in mind His beautiful Names; and the great rank of His Prophet ﷺ, by repeating the verb, so He said: ﴿and obey the Messenger﴾; in what he has set down for you in his Sunnah from Allah, and explained from His Book, because the station of messengership requires this; for this reason He expressed it with the word "Messenger" rather than "Prophet." ﴿And those in authority among you﴾; that is, the rulers. Their obedience, in what is not disobedience, is, as is indicated by not repeating the verb, part of obedience to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ; and obedience to him is obedience to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. The scholars are also among those in authority, and they are the ones who act, for they command with the command of Allah and His Messenger ﷺ.
