When this ruling made clear the three foundations, He followed them with analogy (qiyas), so He linked to what is implied, meaning: "This applies to matters that are clear from the Book and the Sunnah, and upon which there is consensus," His saying: ﴿If you dispute over anything﴾; that is, if it is obscured, so your opinions differ concerning it; ﴿then refer it to Allah﴾; that is, to the One Who encompasses all in knowledge and power, by humbling yourselves before Him through the supplication and worship He has prescribed for you, so that He may open to you what has been closed of it and guide you to its truth; ﴿and the Messenger﴾ [An-Nisa: 69]; that is, the one whose messengership is complete, by searching for the traces of his message, either from an explicit text on that very matter, or from those versed in analogy (qiyas). The verse indicates the order of the four foundations as it is in it, and the invalidity of anything other than them. It is known from His singling out (Exalted is He) and the joining of the Prophet ﷺ with the scholars of his community that good manners consist in affirming the oneness of Allah, even in merely mentioning Him. He emphasized the clarification of the claim of obedience with His saying: ﴿if you are believers﴾; that is, constant in faith, renewing it at every time; ﴿in Allah﴾; that is, the Greatest King, Who has no equal; ﴿and the Last Day﴾, which motivates obedience and restrains from disobedience. Then He indicated the greatness of this matter and the breadth of its benefit by saying, specifying His Messenger ﷺ: ﴿That﴾; that is, this matter of lofty rank; ﴿is better﴾; that is, and other than it is worse; ﴿and better in outcome﴾; that is, in consequence; or (p-312) return and referral from your side to what sound reason requires, without regard to the traces of the message from the Book and the Sunnah. For in the rulings there are matters which reason cannot independently grasp except with the aid of the Law. Al-Bukhari narrated in the Book of Tafsir, from Ibn Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both), who said: "This verse was revealed, ﴿Obey Allah﴾, concerning Abdullah ibn Hudhafa ibn Qays ibn Adi, when the Prophet ﷺ sent him on a military expedition; that is, he commanded them to enter the fire."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 60:

Since the sense (al-taqdir), as the end of the verse conveys it and its beginning indicates, after He had gathered all creation to obedience to Him by the way He mentioned, is: "Whoever refuses that, then he is not a believer," He indicated it by His saying, expressing wonder and addressing the most perfect of creation, the one whom Allah informed about the hypocrites through the subtle meaning of speech (lahn al-qawl): ﴿Have you not seen﴾. He pointed to their distance from the sphere of His presence by His saying: ﴿those who﴾; and to their lying and the persistence of their hypocrisy by His saying: ﴿claim that they have believed﴾, meaning they brought this reality into being and established it within themselves, ﴿in what has been revealed to you﴾. And He showed that this hypocritical claimant was from the People of the Book before professing Islam by His saying: ﴿and what﴾, meaning, and they claim that they have believed in what ﴿was revealed before you﴾, meaning from the Torah and the Gospel. Al-Isfahani said: "The word za'm (claim) is not used, for the most part, except for a statement that is not verified; it is said 'Zaʿama Fulan' (so-and-so claimed) when it is doubtful and its falsehood or truth is not known." The meaning is that these people uttered a statement which, to one who does not know the hidden matters, is fit to be doubted, as evidenced by the fact that they ﴿want to go for judgment﴾, meaning they and your opponents, ﴿to the false deity (al-taghut)﴾, meaning to falsehood that is deeply rooted in vanity. ﴿And [while] they﴾, meaning while in fact they ﴿have been commanded﴾ by the One who holds command ﴿to reject it﴾, in all that has been revealed from your Book and what came before it; and whenever they submit to its judgment they become believers in it while disbelieving in Allah. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And Satan intends﴾, through their intention of that judging, ﴿to lead them﴾, meaning through judgment by it, ﴿astray, a far straying﴾, such that they cannot return to guidance.

This verse is the reason for 'Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) being called "al-Faruq" (the Distinguisher), because he struck the neck of a hypocrite who did not accept the judgment of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), in an account mentioned by al-Tha'labi, from the narration of al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas (may Allah be pleased with them both).

When al-Biqa'i had mentioned their misguidance through their desire (for judgment by the taghut), and their eagerness to refer their disputes to the taghut (idol or false authority), he mentioned their action in that matter, in their aversion from referring to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). So He said: ﴿And when it is said to them﴾; that is, by whatever speaker it may be said; ﴿Come﴾; that is, turn towards, raising yourselves from the valleys of ignorance to the nobility of knowledge; ﴿to what Allah has sent down﴾; that is, to Him in whose hand is everything; ﴿and to the Messenger﴾; that is, the one whose obedience is obligatory, on account of the One who sent him, together with the fact that he is the most perfect of the messengers, who are the most perfect of creation in their message; ﴿you see the hypocrites﴾ — this was the original wording, "you saw them" — but He made manifest the attribute that shows their lying about what they claimed of faith; so He said: ﴿you see the hypocrites turning away﴾; that is, they turn aside ﴿from you﴾; and He emphasised this with His words: ﴿with [complete] aversion﴾; that is, it is at the highest level of aversion.

Then, when their threatening was caused by this, He said, magnifying their punishment by its vagueness and expressing wonder at it through the interrogative, informing them that they will regret when regret will not benefit them and excuse-making will not avail them: ﴿Then how will it be﴾, i.e., what will their condition be, ﴿when a calamity strikes them﴾, i.e., a terrible punishment, ﴿for what their hands have sent forth﴾, from what We have mentioned and from other than it.

Since what should have been expected was that their contradiction would be far-fetched, because lying was severe among the Arabs, He said: ﴿Then they come to you﴾, i.e., submissive, because of what that calamity has softened in them, while they ﴿swear by Allah﴾, i.e., the One who encompasses the attributes of perfection, of majesty and of beauty, without bringing to mind any of His attributes, ﴿that we intended nothing﴾, i.e., in all our circumstances and in all our actions, ﴿but goodness and conciliation﴾, i.e., that matters be in the best and most suitable manner, because of what we saw in that which was hidden from others. And they lied in all of that.

(p-315) When He (glory be to Him, exalted is He) had mentioned some of the contradictions that proceed from them, while they were neither modest nor fearful, He said, informing about their condition and informing of what He does with them: ﴿Those﴾; that is, those who are far from good; ﴿are those whom Allah knows﴾; that is, the One possessing the attributes of greatness; ﴿what is in their hearts﴾; that is, of intense hatred for Islam and its people, even though they strive to conceal it from Him. Then He gave the reason, as instruction in what He does with them and as information that they harm none but themselves, for His saying: ﴿so turn away from them﴾; that is, from their punishment, from fear of them, and from reproaching them, because they are too insignificant for any reckoning to be made of them; ﴿and admonish them﴾; that is, even if you think that this will have no effect, because hearts are in the hand of Allah (glory be to Him, exalted is He), who fashions them as He wills, whenever He wills; ﴿and speak to them concerning themselves﴾; that is, by means of them (their own selves), and by that which explains their conditions and makes clear their defects from their virtues; or [speak] while alone with them, for that is closer to softening them; ﴿a far-reaching word﴾; that is, one that is in the utmost eloquence in itself.

(p-316) When He had commanded obedience to the Messenger (ﷺ), censured those who sought judgment from other than him, threatened them, and concluded His threat with the command to the Prophet (ﷺ) to turn away from them and admonish them, the implied meaning was: "We did not send you, nor any other messenger, except to show gentleness to the community, to pardon them, and to pray for them, with the utmost effort and sincere counsel." He linked to this His saying: ﴿We did not send﴾, that is, by virtue of Our majesty; and He indicated comprehensiveness in His saying: ﴿any messenger﴾. Since the signs He gives them and the miracles He bestows upon them carry in themselves a compulsion to obedience, He likened them to that which motivates the sending of a messenger, and said: ﴿except to be obeyed﴾, that is, because his exalted station requires it, as one who commands it and calls to it; ﴿by the leave of Allah﴾, that is, by the knowledge of the Supreme King, who encompasses everything, in enabling him to be obeyed, because of the distinction We placed in him through great attributes, lofty positions and noble character. As he (ﷺ) said: "There is no prophet among the prophets except that he was given signs of the like of which people believed in." Related by al-Shaykhan (al-Bukhari and Muslim) from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him).

Since the implied meaning was: "If they had obeyed you, it would have been better for them," He linked to it His saying: ﴿And if they, when they had wronged themselves﴾, that is, by seeking judgment from the taghut (false deity or tyrannical authority) or others; ﴿had come to you﴾, that is, hastening; ﴿and asked Allah for forgiveness﴾, that is, they followed their coming with a request for forgiveness from the Most Generous King, because of the majesty they had in mind; ﴿and the Messenger had asked forgiveness for them﴾, that is, for what they had neglected by disobeying him in the obedience that was due to him from them; ﴿they would have found Allah﴾, that is, the Supreme King; ﴿Accepting of repentance, Merciful﴾, that is, abundant in accepting repentance from His servants and in mercy, because He encompasses all attributes of perfection. So He accepted their repentance, erased their sins, and honored them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 65:

(p-317) When this made clear that their refusal to accept his judgment and to acknowledge their wrongdoing before him was a barrier preventing them from faith, he said, emphasizing the statement to the utmost degree, with an oath that strongly affirms its content, and with "lā" (no), which negates its opposite: ﴿But no, by your Lord﴾, that is, the One who has been good to you, ﴿they will not believe﴾, that is, they will not bring this quality into existence and renew it, ﴿until they make you judge﴾, that is, they make you an arbiter, ﴿in what has become confused﴾, that is, what has become mixed up and disputed, ﴿among them﴾, through the speech of some of them to others in dispute, until they were like the branches of a tree in their interlacing and crowding.

Since submitting to a judgment that contradicts one's desires is extremely difficult for the self, He indicated it with the particle of delay, saying: ﴿Then they will not find within themselves any resistance﴾, that is, any kind of constriction, ﴿to what you have decided﴾, that is, against them by it, and He reinforced their submission for themselves with the form of the verbal noun (taf'il), saying: ﴿and submit completely﴾, that is, they fully carry out complete submission to everything that is due from them, from themselves and from others, to Allah and to His Messenger (ﷺ), purely, free from any tinge of aversion. Then He added further emphasis with His saying: ﴿with full submission﴾.

In the Sahih (collection) it is reported that the verse was revealed concerning al-Zubayr and a man from the Ansar who was his opponent. So there is no regard for the one who said it was Hatib (may Allah be pleased with him).

Since the implied sense was: "We have indeed prescribed for them obedience to you and submission to you in this tolerant monotheism (*ḥanīfiyya samḥa*, the upright and easy faith) to which you called them and which you made them bear," he connected to it his saying: ﴿And if We had prescribed for them﴾; i.e., this opponent of al-Zubayr (may Allah be pleased with him) and the likes of this opponent, from among those whose faith was weak, as an obligatory writ ﴿that kill yourselves﴾; i.e., as was in the Torah, in expiation of some sins, directly and literally; and as the emigrants did by exposing themselves to that for thirteen years, during which they were among the enemies of Allah like a lump of flesh between the talons of eagles snatching at it; ﴿or leave your homes﴾; as the emigrants did, may Allah be pleased with them, among whom al-Zubayr was one of the leaders; ﴿from your dwellings﴾; i.e., which are for your bodies as your bodies are for your souls, as repentance to your Lord; ﴿they would not have done it﴾; i.e., due to the deficiency of their faith and the weakness of their certainty. And if We had prescribed it for them and they had not accepted it, they would have disbelieved, and thus deserved killing.

Since every turbidity is not free of its clarification, He said: ﴿except a few of them﴾; i.e., those who know that Allah, glorified and exalted, is better for them than themselves, and that their life lies only in obeying Him. It is related that among these was Thabit ibn Qays ibn Shammas (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "By Allah, Allah surely knows my truthfulness: if Muhammad ordered me to kill myself, I would have killed it." Likewise said Ibn Mas'ud and Ammar ibn Yasir, may Allah be pleased with them both. It is related from Umar (may Allah be pleased with him) that he said: "By Allah, if our Lord ordered us, we would do it; and praise be to Allah who did not do that to us." There is no doubt that the implied sense is: "But We did not prescribe it for them; so let them thank Us and hold fast (p-319) to this tolerant monotheism."

Since the foundation of the surah is on harmony, and the context is one of seeking to win hearts, he said, encouraging them: ﴿And if they had done what they are admonished﴾; i.e., these hypocrites; ﴿what they are admonished with﴾; i.e., the admonition is renewed for them at all times; ﴿it would have been﴾; i.e., their doing that; ﴿better for them﴾; i.e., than what they chose for themselves; ﴿and firmer in steadfastness﴾; i.e., than what they made themselves firm with by their broken oaths.

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 67:**

﴿And then We would surely have given them⦆; that is: and if they did what they are admonished with, We would have given them, from Our greatness, a gift that is emphatically confirmed, without any doubt about it. By His saying ﴿from Our presence﴾ he indicated that it is among the wondrous things that are with Him of extraordinary events that break habitual custom and violate what is regularly established; ﴿a great reward﴾;

﴿And We would have guided them﴾; i.e., by what We possess of greatness; ﴿to a straight path﴾; i.e., one that brings them to their goal. Glorified and exalted is He. To encourage obedience, He has magnified this reward with several kinds of greatness: among them the alerting with *idhan* (إذًا, "then, in that case"); the use of the form that expresses majesty (the plural "We"); and *ladun* (لَدُنْ, "from the presence of"), together with the magnificence and the description of the reward as "great."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 69:

When he had encouraged acting upon his admonitions, and since a promise may be given because of the harshness of the one admonished, and since what he had previously presented in his exhortation was a general matter, he encouraged, after softening the hearts through admonition, in absolute obedience, to which the whole context is directed, detailing the generality of what he had promised for it. So he said: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah﴾; that is, in carrying out His commands and halting at His prohibitions, while keeping His greatness in mind, with an obedience that is continuous and ongoing; ﴿and the Messenger﴾; that is, in everything he wills, for the station of messengership requires this, especially for one who has reached its ultimate limit; ﴿then those﴾; that is, those of high rank and great nobility; ﴿will be with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favor﴾; that is, by what He possesses of attributes of majesty and beauty; ﴿among them﴾; that is, they are counted among their party, so that whenever he wishes to visit them or see them, he reaches them with ease. This does not mean that he must be at their levels, even if his deeds are deficient. Then He specified them by His saying: ﴿of the prophets﴾; that is, those whom Allah informed of the subtle wisdoms, and who informed the people of the eloquent words, with the purity of their dispositions, their loftiness and their greatness; ﴿and the truthful﴾; that is, those who first affirmed what came to them from Allah among the people, and who were truthful in their sayings and their deeds, so they became exemplars for those after them; ﴿and the martyrs﴾; that is, those who never, even for an instant, absent themselves from the presences of holiness and the abodes of intimacy, but are with people in their bodies and with Allah, glorified and exalted be He, in their intellects and their knowledge; whether they bore witness to the truth of the religion of Allah by argument, or by the sword, and then were killed in the way of Allah; ﴿and the righteous﴾; that is, those in whom, by the power of Allah, no corruption whatsoever arises, outwardly or inwardly. The words of the knower Shaykh Raslan point to this, when he said: "You will not be righteous as long as there remains in you any remnant for other than Him." The four attributes may gather in one person, and they may not. Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, is the most worthy of the Ummah of the station of truthfulness, even if we say that ʿAli and Zayd, may Allah be pleased with them both, embraced Islam before him; for because of his age, and because he had not been a follower of the Prophet ﷺ before Islam, he was an exemplar to others, and for this reason he was the cause of the conversion of many people, and those people were in turn a cause of the conversion of others, so he had a like reward of all of them. In him, at the time of his Islam, was the strength of striving in the way of Allah, glorified and exalted be He, by defending the Prophet ﷺ, and other deeds that indicate his truthfulness. Because of the consideration of these matters, his rank comes right after the rank of prophethood, and to remove any intermediary between them. Allah, glorified and exalted be He, granted success to this Ummah that He chose, by the appointment of the Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, after their Prophet ﷺ, and his burial beside him. And among the great rank of this community is the Prophet's ﷺ mention of them at the end of his life, when he said: "With the Exalted Companion." Al-Bukhari narrated in the book of Tafsir, from ʿAʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "I heard the Prophet ﷺ say: 'No prophet falls ill except that he is given the choice between this world and the Hereafter.'" During the illness in which he died, he had a severe hoarseness, and she heard him say: ﴿with those upon whom Allah has bestowed favor, of the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs and the righteous﴾, and she knew that he had been given the choice.

When he informed that the obedient one is with these, he did not suffice with what the mention of them conveyed of their majesty and the majesty of those with them, but he increased in explaining the loftiness of their station and the station of everyone with them, by his saying: ﴿And excellent is﴾; that is, how good is; ﴿those﴾; that is, those of noble characters, the foremost on the day of competition; ﴿as companions﴾; from "rifq," which linguistically means gentleness of side and delicacy of action; and it is among the words whose singular and plural are alike.

Then he pointed to the magnitude of what He bestowed upon them, encouraging them to act in accordance with that which leads to it, using the particle of distance, so he said: ﴿That is the bounty﴾; and he increased the encouragement toward it by informing of this origination with the Greatest Name, so he said: ﴿from Allah﴾.

Since the basis of preference (tafdil) rests upon knowledge, he said, building upon what its estimated sense is: "Because of what He knows of the soundness of their inner dispositions, from which follows the nobility of their outward conduct," ﴿and sufficient is Allah﴾; that is, the One who possesses complete encompassing knowledge; ﴿as Knower﴾; He knows from the outward and the inward what merits preference for whoever He prefers over others.

When the implied sense was, "Indeed, among you is one who goes out to jihad (striving in the way of God) without resolve or caution," he followed it with his statement. This clarifies one of the most important aims of these verses: rebuking the hypocrites (*munafiqun*), warning against them, and describing them with some of what they conceal. It also emphasizes that everyone who claims faith denies being like that. He says: ﴿And indeed among you﴾, i.e., O you who believe, ﴿by Our might﴾, ﴿there is surely one who lags behind﴾, i.e., he is sluggish within himself about jihad, due to weakness of faith or hypocrisy, and he commands others to do likewise with an emphatic command, showing compassion toward you. This is pure deceit, for it produces the weakness that leads to the boldness of the enemy, which leads to annihilation.

Since the one who lags behind from them has two conditions, victory and defeat, he attached a consequence to his lagging behind, swearing to his statement regarding both. He says: ﴿If a calamity strikes you﴾, i.e., in the direction from which they held back, ﴿he says﴾, that one who sat back, out of ignorance and coarseness: ﴿God has blessed me﴾, i.e., the Supreme King, mentioning this Name without knowing its meaning, ﴿since﴾, i.e., when, or because, ﴿I was not present with them as a witness﴾, i.e., present. It is permissible that he means the martyr in the legal sense, and his use of the term is by way of condescension, as if he says: "What is the highest thing they have, I consider its loss a great favor from Him to me."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 73:

﴿And if there reaches you a bounty﴾; i.e., a conquest, a victory, and spoils; ﴿from Allah﴾; i.e., the Supreme King, in whose hand is everything. Since his regret is only over the loss of worldly aims, He emphasized his saying: ﴿he will surely say﴾; i.e., in your absence. He placed (in the midst) between the saying and what is said a parenthetical remark, as an emphasis on their blame, by his saying: ﴿as if﴾; i.e., as if he; ﴿had not﴾; i.e., his condition resembling the condition of one who had not; ﴿been between you and him any affection﴾; i.e., due to his saying: "Would that I had been with them, so that I might achieve a great achievement"; i.e., by sharing with them in that. ﴿A great achievement﴾. That is because, had he been one with affection, he would have said, in a time of calamity: "Would that it had not befallen them; had I been with them, I would have defended them," and in a time of victory: "Their might has truly pleased me." But he did not make the target of his concern, in either of the two states, anything other than the worldly object sought. Perhaps He specified the second state for the comparison, because what is attributed to him in it is not limited to one who loves; whereas in the first state, the lover may often limit himself to that, out of intent to remain, to take revenge, and to punish the disbelievers. He mentioned affection because the hypocrites used to exaggerate in displaying love, compassion and sincere counsel toward the believers.

When he had explained that the aim of the one who sits back from jihad is this world, it became known that the aim of the one who strives in jihad is the Hereafter. So he based on this his saying: ﴿So let those fight in the way of God﴾; that is, because of facilitating the path of the King, to whom all command belongs, and of preserving people for Him. ﴿Who sell﴾; that is, who sell eagerly and stubbornly, and they are the believers; or who take, and they are the hypocrites, using the homonym (al-mushtarak, a word with two meanings) in both of its meanings. ﴿The life of this world﴾; so they leave it, ﴿for the Hereafter.﴾ Since the implied sense is: "Whoever sits back from jihad has been content with this world in place of the Hereafter," he joined to it his saying: ﴿And whoever fights in the way of God﴾; that is, intends to exalt the word of the King, who encompasses the attributes of beauty and majesty; ﴿and is killed﴾; that is, in that way, and upon that intention, after destiny and decree have overcome him; ﴿or overcomes﴾; that is, the disbelievers, and so is safe; ﴿We shall give him﴾; that is, by a promise that admits no failure, through what We possess of the greatness that encompasses good and evil. The verse is of the type called ihtibak (a rhetorical device in which one part is mentioned and its counterpart left implicit): mentioning being killed first indicates safety second, and mentioning overcoming second indicates being overcome first (p-327). Perhaps the expression "sawfa" (soon/surely) indicates, for the most part, the long life of the fighter, contrary to what many people imagine, to make known that the matter depends on the act of the free chooser, not on causes. ﴿A great reward﴾; that is, in both abodes, for his striving to exalt the religion of God, glorified and exalted is He.

His restriction to these two categories is an exhortation to steadfastness, even if the enemy is more than twice in number: "How often has a small company overcome a large company." "And God supports with His help whom He wills." "And God is with the patient."

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 75:

Since the implied sense was: "Why is it that you do not fight in the way of Allah, for this great reward, against those who do not break their promise?" And they used to say: "We do not give inheritance except to one who defends the sacred honour (dhimar), protects the neighbour, and guards the territory (hawzah)." He said, conjoining this implied sense, inciting them, stirring them up, rebuking those who sit back, and reproaching them: ﴿And what﴾, that is, and what thing, ﴿is [the matter] with you﴾, whether of worldly gain or of the Hereafter, while ﴿you do not fight﴾, that is, you do not renew the fighting at every time, without growing weary of it, ﴿in the way of Allah﴾, that is, for the sake of facilitating the path of the King, who possesses complete majesty and absolute self-sufficiency, and for the sake of the deliverance of ﴿the oppressed﴾, that is, those whose weakness has been sought by the disbelievers until it became a reality. It is also permissible (and this is more firmly grounded) that it be in the accusative by way of specification (ikhtisas), as an alert that it is among the most noble of what falls under "in the way of Allah."

Since the causing of harm to the enemy is greater in the case of those from whom the hope of benefit is greater, and then greater still in the case of those for whom the shame is stronger and more binding, He arranged them in this order, saying: ﴿from the men and the women and the children﴾, that is, the Muslims whom the disbelievers had kept from emigration, and they used to torment them and tempt them away from their religion. Each of these is sufficient to rouse people of lofty resolve and noble character to fight. Then He described them with that which stirs one to help them and urges one to come to their aid, saying: ﴿who say﴾, that is, without ceasing, ﴿"Our Lord﴾, that is, O You who has done good to us by bringing us out of darkness into light, ﴿bring us out from this town﴾. Then they described it with what impels this supplication, saying: ﴿whose people are oppressors﴾, that is, through what You facilitate for us of the means; ﴿and appoint for us from Yourself﴾, that is, from Your wondrous affairs, in matters that break customary patterns, ﴿a protector﴾, who will take charge of our interests. And since a protector may not possess the power to give victory, they said: ﴿and appoint for us﴾; and since they wished that wondrous signs would come to them, they repeated their words: ﴿from Yourself a helper﴾, that is, one of perfect victory, to a degree that would astonish those accustomed to wondrous signs. Thus, with this speech it was as though He—glorified and exalted is He—had said: "I have indeed made for you the greatest share of the inheritance. So what is the matter with you that you do not fight in My way, in gratitude for My blessing? Where is that zeal and protection you claim? What is the matter with you that you do not fight in support of these weak ones, so that your protection of the sacred honour is realized, your guarding of the territory is fulfilled, and your defense of the neighbour is accomplished?!"

When He had informed them of their need for the helpers and of the oppression they suffered from the disbelievers, He resumed the report about the two groups, saying, emphasizing the encouragement to jihad (struggle in the cause of God): ﴿Those who believe﴾, that is, those who were truthful in their claim to faith; ﴿fight﴾, that is, in confirmation of their claim, without any interruption at all; ﴿in the way of God﴾, that is, the One who encompasses all the attributes of perfection, intending His face by defending what is sacred and otherwise. As for whoever does not confirm his claim in this way, he has not believed. ﴿And those who disbelieve fight﴾, that is, likewise, ﴿in the way of the Taghut﴾ (every object of worship other than God, the transgressor). So there is no protector for them, nor any helper.

Since the Taghut is Satan, or whoever Satan has adorned (with evil), and since everyone who disobeys God is of Satan's party and among those he has led astray, He made the following a consequence of this: ﴿So fight the friends of Satan﴾. Then He gave the reason for boldness against them in His saying: ﴿Indeed, the plot of Satan﴾, that is, the one who is the head of the disobedient, ﴿was﴾ by his innate nature and disposition, ﴿weak﴾.

When He had made them aware of these arduous stages of the Hereafter and these worldly glories, and concluded with what rouses the coward and strengthens the heart, and encouraged them with what He had made them yearn for of the bliss of the Gardens, He wondered at the state of those who, after that, became slack and submissive. So He said (exalted is He), addressing the most devout of His servants and the most obedient to His command: ﴿Have you not seen﴾. He indicated that they were in a place far from His presence, to rouse them, with His words: ﴿those to whom it was said﴾. That is, in answer to their saying: "We want to extend our hands against the disbelievers in fighting, because our trial by them has lasted long." ﴿Restrain your hands﴾, that is, do not extend them against them, for We have not commanded this. ﴿And establish the prayer﴾, that is, a connection with the Creator, and seeking help against the opponents. ﴿And give the zakat﴾, as a means of increasing wealth, a purification of character, and a bond with creation.

﴿When fighting was prescribed for them﴾, that is, what they had asked for, while they were being commanded to forbear, a decree that does not cease until the end of time, ﴿behold, a party of them﴾, that is, people from whose action division follows, ﴿fear men﴾, that is, those who are like them, that they might harm them. And the situation is that it is disgraceful for them to be more daring than those who are people like them, ﴿as they fear God﴾, that is, just as they fear God, who is the Capable, not other than Him.

Since their restraint from fighting was so pronounced that it would make whoever saw them suspect them of cowardice, so that he would be uncertain in weighing their fear of men against their fear of God, He expressed it with the particle of doubt and said: ﴿or with even greater fear﴾, that is, or their fear of men, in the eyes of the observer, was greater than their fear of God. This indicates that their fear of men is certainly not less than their fear of God, but rather either equal to it or greater. The ambiguity may also reflect variation according to two times, so that their fear of them at one time is equal and at another time greater, and so it is uncertain between these two states. It is also possible that this is a metaphor for their dislike of fighting at that time, and their wish to postpone it to some other time.

He confirmed what preceded of this supposition with His words, which serve as a kind of explanation for their aversion: ﴿And they say﴾, out of distress at death or at hardships, if they were believers; or as objection, if they were hypocrites; regarding the supposed truth of what the Messenger ﷺ says: ﴿Our Lord﴾, that is, O You who are good to us, near to us, ﴿why have You prescribed fighting for us?﴾, that is, while we are weak. ﴿Why did You not﴾, that is, would that You had, ﴿defer us﴾, that is, from the command to fight, ﴿to a near term﴾, that is, so that we might take a respite from the hardship we were enduring from the disbelievers in Makkah.

The occasion of its revelation was that ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf, al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad al-Kindi, Qudama ibn Maz'un, Sa'd ibn (p-332) Abi Waqqas, and a group, may God be pleased with them, used to suffer much harm from the polytheists in Makkah before they emigrated, and they would say: "O Messenger of God, permit us to fight them, for they have harmed us." The Messenger of God ﷺ would say to them: "Restrain your hands, for I have not been commanded to fight them; establish the prayer and give the zakat." When they emigrated to Madinah, and God, glorified and exalted, commanded them to fight the polytheists, this grieved some of them. This was related by al-Baghawi from al-Kalbi, and al-Wahidi related it from him in similar wording. He also narrated with his chain from Ibn ʿAbbas, may God be pleased with them both, that ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn ʿAwf and his companions, may God be pleased with them, came to the Prophet ﷺ in Makkah and said: "O Messenger of God, we were in honor while we were polytheists; when we believed we became humiliated." He said: "I have been commanded to pardon, so do not fight the people." When God (exalted) transferred him to Madinah, He commanded him to fight, and they held back. So God, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿Have you not seen those to whom it was said, "Restrain your hands"﴾, the verse. This indicates that attributing the saying to them refers only to their state of delaying the rush to fighting, in the condition of one who says this. Thus the purpose of the verse is to incite them to fighting and stir them up, and nothing else.

When he (upon him be prayers and peace) wondered at them, in disapproval of them, it was as if he had said: "What should I say to them?" So He commanded him to admonish them, to expose the folly of their minds and to weaken their opinions, with His words: ﴿Say: The enjoyment of this world is little﴾, that is, even if it were supposed that your lives were extended until you grew weary of living, every thing that ends is little. Moreover, its bliss is not certain to be attained, and if it is attained it is spoiled by turbidities. ﴿And the Hereafter is better for those who are mindful of God﴾, that is, because its bliss does not perish, and it is certain and free of any turbidity. And it is worse than this world for those who are not mindful, because its punishment is long and does not cease. ﴿And you will not be wronged a whit﴾, that is, neither in your worldly life, by having your lifespans shortened through your fighting, nor your provisions through your preoccupation; nor in your Hereafter, by losing any part of your reward for the hardship you endure. For He, glorified and exalted, is Wise; He places nothing in other than its proper place, and He does nothing except according to the rule of wisdom. So why do you speak the words of one accused: "Why did You do this?" Do you fear injustice in imposing what was not obligatory upon you, and in diminishing your provision and lifespan? Exalted is God above that. Rather, He, while His custom is justice and He may do what He wills and is not questioned about what He does, is good and bestows, upon whoever accepts His goodness, the completeness of grace.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 78:

When He (Exalted is He) had made them renounce the abode of toil and troubles on the assumption of a long life, and they behaved as though, by abandoning fighting, they hoped for eternity, or for postponement of a death that fighting would cause, He alerted them to what they were certain of: that death is a watering-place that must be reached at the time decreed for it, even if a person shuns it by staying in fortresses or throws himself into destruction. So He said (Exalted is He), rebuking those who said this, emphasizing with "mā" (the negating particle, opposing the content of their statement, because their condition was that of one who denies death apart from fighting), and answering with the plain truth, after having first given the answer on the basis of concession: ﴿Wherever you may be﴾, O people, all of you, obedient and disobedient, ﴿death will overtake you﴾; that is, it is a seeker that no fleeing person can escape. ﴿Even if you were in towers﴾; that is, fortresses, a tower inside a tower, or each one of you in a tower.

Since this was in the plural, it suited the intensifying form intended for abundance in: ﴿well-built﴾; that is, lofty, each one of them towering into the air and impregnable, and yet plastered with gypsum (shīd), that is, with lime, so that there is no flaw in it at all. It is also possible that "tashīd" means simply perfect construction, meaning that they are greatly fortified in their defenses, since the context also requires this. So if death is unavoidable, then it is more fitting that it occur in jihad, which brings about eternal happiness, than in anything else.

Then He connected what remained of their statements to what preceded from them, in His saying: ﴿Our Lord, why have You prescribed for us?﴾ [al-Nisa: 77] to the end; even though these people were not the first group among them. It is also possible to say that when He reported that caution does not avert destiny, He followed this with a state of theirs, rebuking by it those who were lax in His command, signaling a shift to the third person, turning away from addressing them with some anger, because they combined with failing to glorify God (Exalted is He) a failure in courtesy toward the Messenger (ﷺ), whom He sent to be obeyed by the permission of God. So He said: ﴿And if﴾; that is, they say this while the situation is that if ﴿good befalls them﴾; that is, some of those invited from the community, who are those in whose hearts is sickness, ﴿a good thing﴾; that is, something that pleases them and has a pleasing effect upon them, of whatever kind it may be, ﴿they say, "This is from God"﴾; that is, the One to whom all command belongs, and you have no part in it. ﴿And if an evil befalls them﴾; that is, a state that grieves them, of whatever kind, ﴿they say, "This is from you"﴾; that is, from your coming to this town, considering you a bad omen.

Since this was a grave matter, and burning and wounding to the heart, He eased it for him by His saying: ﴿Say, "All﴾; that is, of the evil and the good, in reality, whether worldly or otherworldly, ﴿is from God"﴾; that is, the One to whom belongs everything, and nothing belongs to anyone else. This happened, as they related, when Abu Umama As'ad ibn Zurara, chief of the Banu al-Najjar (may Allah be pleased with him), died when the Prophet (ﷺ) had migrated, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said, as in the Sirah: "Evil is the dead man Abu Umama for the Jews and the hypocrites of the Arabs! They say: 'If he were a prophet, his companion would not have died. I possess neither benefit nor harm for myself or for my companion from God.'" Since this led to the knowledge that they had erred in this, and so deserved denunciation, He said, denouncing them: "What is the matter with"; and He demeaned them by His saying "these people"; as if He had said: ﴿the people﴾, which indicates standing and sufficiency; either mockingly toward them, or attributing to them strength of bodies and weakness of minds: ﴿who scarcely understand﴾; who are not near to comprehending ﴿a statement﴾; that is, one that is addressed to them at all with good understanding.

When He answered them with what is true in terms of existence (ījād), He taught them proper conduct (adab), by directing their attention to the cause. So He said, beginning a new sentence (mustaʾnifan): ﴿Whatever good befalls you, it is from Allah﴾; that is, a worldly blessing or an otherworldly one; ﴿it is from Allah﴾; that is, by His bringing it into existence and by His bounty. Faith is the best of good things. The Imam said: They say that they agreed that His saying, ﴿And who is better in speech than one who calls to Allah﴾ [Fussilat: 33], refers to the statement of testimony (kalimat al-shahada).

﴿And whatever evil befalls you﴾, though you are the best of creation; ﴿it is from yourself﴾; that is, because of it. So others are so by way of greater reason.

(p-337) Since their statement implied denying his prophethood (ﷺ) unless he performed every extraordinary feat, and since He, glory be to Him and exalted, had informed them that he is equal to the creation in power, He, glory be to Him and exalted, said, informing them of what He had singled him out with: ﴿And We have sent you﴾; that is, singling you out for Our greatness; ﴿to mankind﴾; that is, comprehensively; ﴿as a messenger﴾; that is, to do what messengers are required to do of conveying the message and the like. You have striven in conveying and advising, and We did not make you a god who brings about whatever good or evil is demanded of you. So if they deny your message, Allah bears witness through the establishing of miracles and clear signs. ﴿And sufficient is Allah﴾, who encompasses all in knowledge and power, ﴿as a witness﴾ for you concerning the message and its conveyance.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 80:

When He had negated their excuses for lagging behind His obedience, right up to concluding with the testimony to His Messenger's mission, He said, encouraging and warning, in a general manner that calms his heart, lightens the burden of their continual disobedience toward him, and indicates his infallibility in all his movements and stillnesses: ﴿Whoever obeys the Messenger﴾; that is, as his state requires; ﴿has indeed obeyed Allah﴾; the Greatest King, to whom there is no equal; because he is a caller to Him, and he does not speak from desire; he only reports what is revealed to him. ﴿But whoever turns away﴾; that is, from his obedience. Since the implied sense is: "then he has only disobeyed Allah; and Allah, glorified and exalted is He, knows him and is able over him; if He willed, He would turn him back, and if He willed, He would destroy him for his transgression; so leave him and that," (p-338) He expressed all of that by His saying: ﴿We have not sent you﴾; that is, by Our greatness; ﴿as a guardian over them﴾; We have only sent you as a caller.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 81:

Since it is the duty of the Messenger (ﷺ) to protect those who obey him and those who disobey him, so that the one who sent him is conveyed this, and since He, glory be to Him and exalted, had indicated to him that he should turn away from this, because he cannot encompass it in knowledge, however hard he strives, He began to inform him of some of what they conceal. So He said, relating some of their sayings and making clear their hypocrisy and deception in this: ﴿And they say﴾, meaning: when you command them to do something of Our affair while they are in your presence, ﴿obedience﴾, meaning: every obedience from us to you, always. We remain steadfast in that. The indefinite form (tankir) is for magnification, through generality. ﴿But when they go out﴾, meaning: they leave ﴿from your presence, a group of them plots by night﴾, while they are in the utmost rebellion, ﴿other than what you say﴾, meaning: they decide and devise upon a high degree of planning and precision, with circling around and mutual opposition, like the action of one who arranges affairs, makes them firm and perfects them at night. ﴿Other than what you say﴾ means: other than their repeated saying to you at every time of the obedience which they showed, or other than your saying which you conveyed to them. Abu 'Amr and Hamza assimilated the ta' (idgham, assimilation) into the ta' (ṭā’) after it was made quiescent, to avoid the succession of vowels on the ṭā’, since the two articulation points are close, and the ṭā’ is heavier by emphatic articulation (ițbāq). So assimilating the lesser into the greater was good. The rest pronounced it clearly (izhar). Assimilation is more fitting to their state, and clear pronunciation is more fitting to what is spoken from their places of articulation. (p. 339)

Since it is the habit of a human being to record in writing the matters he wishes to make permanent, He ordered the matter according to that, and said: ﴿And Allah﴾, meaning: and the state is that the King, who combines all the attributes of perfection, ﴿records what they plot﴾, meaning: they renew their plotting every time they do it. He is free of need for it, but that is so that He may present it to them on the Day when the witnesses stand, and establish the proof against them according to what their habits have been. Or it may be that it is revealed to you, so that He exposes them through its writing and its recitation for all time, so that they will not think that their plotting will avail them anything.

Since His providing for this important matter for His Prophet (ﷺ) was a consequence of that, He said: ﴿So turn away from them﴾, meaning: for by that they harm only themselves. ﴿And rely upon Allah﴾, meaning: in their affair and in other matters, ﴿upon Allah﴾, meaning: the One from whose will nothing escapes. ﴿And sufficient is Allah﴾, meaning: the One who encompasses everything in knowledge and power, ﴿as a Disposer of affairs﴾. So you will see how the outcome will be in your affair and their affair.

When the cause of their concealing what contradicts what they openly display was their belief that he (ﷺ) was a mere leader who knows only what they openly show, and not a messenger from God, who knows the secret and what is more hidden, He (exalted be He) built upon this, as a rebuke, a guidance for them to reason from the proof of his prophethood, with what removes doubt and clarifies the matter. That is *tadabbur* (deep reflection) of this Qur'an, whose meanings are harmonious and whose composition is inimitable, which surpasses the powers of created beings, and which reveals their hidden states despite their striving to conceal them. So He, glorified and exalted, said, indicating the obligation to reflect upon the Qur'an and to derive meanings from it: ﴿Do they not then reflect upon the Qur'an?﴾ That is, do they not ponder it? It is said, "I reflected upon the matter" when you consider its outcome and its final result. ﴿The Qur'an﴾ means that which comprises everything whose knowledge is sought, including distinguishing truth from falsehood, in an arrangement that does not fail and a method that does not weary. Al-Mahdawi said: This is evidence for the obligation to learn the meanings of the Qur'an, and for the corruption of the view of those who say that nothing may be taken from it except what has been transmitted from the Prophet (ﷺ), and who prohibit interpreting it in a way that the language of the Arabs permits. It also contains evidence for reasoning and inference.

Since the implied sense was: "Then, had it been from other than God, it would not have disclosed their secrets," He joined to it His words: ﴿And if it had been from other than God﴾ — that is, from one who has complete comprehensiveness, as the disbelievers claimed — ﴿they would have found in it much contradiction﴾. That is, in its meaning, through contradiction and deviation from truth in reporting unseen matters, or some of them; and in its composition, through variation in its inimitability. When they know that it is from God by this decisive proof, they keep their inner thoughts just as they keep their outward actions, because the command to obedience is equal in secret and in public. The restriction to "much" indicates that the created being is unable to guard himself against great deficiency by himself. And mentioning, when negating the consequent, the existence of slight difference in it, is refuted by plain evidence.

[p. 340]

When Allah, glorified and exalted, commanded going forth to jihad, [urging] caution and vigilance, and then informed [the believers] that among the people there are the one who deceives and the one who discourages, explicitly mentioning the second and alluding to the first, and warned against both of them and against others besides them, until He concluded with the command concerning the deceivers, and with the statement that the Qur'an is upright, without crookedness in it, He also mentioned the discouragers and the deceivers in a manner clearer than the first, explaining what they were like. So He said: ﴿And when there comes to them﴾, that is, these people who cause unrest, ﴿a matter of security﴾, without firm grounding, ﴿or of fear﴾, likewise, ﴿they spread it﴾, that is, they carried out the spreading [of it], because of the corruptions they are able to cause, ﴿about it﴾, that is, because of it, ﴿without knowledge on their part of its truth from its falsehood, and its authentic [part] from its disputed [part]﴾, so that the grave harm falls upon the people of Islam, the least of which is the inversion of realities. In al-Qamus, [it says]: "adhaʿahu" and "bihi": he disseminated it, and proclaimed it among the people. This is what they did in the matter of security, when the people of polytheism were routed at Uhud, and [the believers] abandoned the position in which the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had placed them, and opposed his command and the command of their commander. Thus it became the cause of the polytheists' counterattack and the defeat of the believers. And in the matter of fear, when Satan shouted: "Muhammad has been killed," they believed him, some of them spread it to others, and they fled, and they wished to seek protection from the disbelievers, from Abu Sufyan and Abu ʿAmir. (p-342) Likewise [was] what they spread when going out to Badr, the appointed meeting place: that Abu Sufyan had gathered for them an uncountable multitude, and that if they met him not one of them would remain, along with other such rumours, until Madinah was seething with evil like a boiling cauldron, so that they all held back, or all except a few of them, until the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "By Allah, I will go out even if no one goes out with me." Then they responded, and this statement gave them courage and brought them tranquillity, so they returned with a blessing from Allah and a favour, [and] no harm touched them, as Allah, glorified and exalted, and His Messenger (ﷺ) had promised them if they were patient and God-fearing. So their assumption was proven false, and Allah and His Messenger spoke truly. In this there is guidance toward using as evidence for the Qur'an's being from Him, glorified and exalted, the fact that what comes from them of these reports which they circulate is contradicted and varies; and that whatever comes from other than Him (exalted) is varied, even if one who resembles [the truth] strives to be precise in it, and even if his intellect is great and his nobility lofty; unless his intellect is grounded in what has come from the One who knows the outcomes and encompasses existing things, through the tongue of the Messengers, upon them be prayer, peace, greeting and honour. It also [points] to the fact that analogy (qiyas, reasoning from a known ruling to a new case) is a proof, that the taqlid (following of a scholar's view) of the unqualified person to the scholar is obligatory, and that istinbat (deriving rulings by inference from the sources) is obligatory upon the scholars, and the Prophet (ﷺ) is the head of the scholars. To this alludes His saying (exalted): ﴿And if they had referred it﴾, that is, that matter for which there is no explicit text, ﴿to the Messenger﴾, that is, to himself if he is present, and to his reports if he is absent, ﴿and to those in authority among them﴾, that is, those qualified to command and forbid, from the rulers in actuality or in potential from the scholars and others, ﴿they would have known it﴾, that is, that matter, in its reality, and whether it is of the kind that is to be spread or not, ﴿those who derive it﴾, that is, who extract it by their acuity and experience, as the water-finder extracts water and the benefits of the earth, ﴿from among them﴾, that is, from among the Messenger and those in authority.

Since the implied sense is: "Had it not been for Allah's favour upon you, and His mercy through the Messenger and the heirs of his knowledge, the core of the religion would have been violated by these rumours of theirs, and the affairs of the Muslims would have collapsed," He followed it with His saying: ﴿And had it not been for Allah's favour upon you﴾, that is, O you who are marked by Islam, by the sending down of the Book and the rectifying of minds, ﴿and His mercy﴾, by the sending of the Messenger, ﴿you would have followed Satan﴾, that is, the expelled, burning one, ﴿except a few﴾, that is, of you; for they do not follow him, by Allah's protection, glorified and exalted, through what He bestowed upon them of sound intellect, without the mediation of a Messenger. This verse is among the passages difficult for minds to grasp without a specification of what is meant by the favour, except for one whom Allah, glorified and exalted, has given knowledge of the connections [between verses] and a penetrating understanding of what is meant by the contexts, and an acuity regarding circumstances and situations, which brings one close to unveiling. The reason is that it is established that the exception must differ in ruling from that from which it is excepted; and here the ones upon whom the favour and mercy were bestowed are those who were guided. The exception's contrary [ruling] would be one of three matters, each of which is corrupt: either they lack the favour and so follow [Satan], which would entail that the astray are fewer than the guided, and that is contrary to observation; or they lack it and so do not follow [Satan], and they would then be guided without any favour; or the favour is present upon them and yet they follow [Satan], and then they would be astray despite the favour and mercy, which were the cause of preventing error from those addressed, so they would be both preventing and not preventing at times, and thus they would have been of no benefit. Moreover, this also entails that the astray are fewer than the guided. So when the speech is understood to mean that the favour is the sending [of the Messenger], the meaning becomes clear, and the implied sense would be: "Had it not been for the sending of the Messenger, you would have followed Satan, except for a few of you, for they do not follow him without the guidance of the Messenger, but by a guidance from Allah, glorified and exalted, and a favour, without intermediary, like Qass ibn Saʿida, Zayd ibn ʿAmr ibn Nufayl, and Waraqa ibn Nawfal." The evidence for this implied sense is that the context concerns referring all matters to the Messenger (ﷺ), and forbidding independence in anything apart from him.

When He, glory be to Him and exalted, made clear their hypocrisy, which necessitates their holding back from jihad with their own selves and their discouraging others, that became a reason for the Prophet (ﷺ) to proceed with His command, glory be to Him and exalted, without paying attention to them, whether they agreed or hypocritically held back. So after commanding them to go forth "in groups or all together" [p-345] and clarifying that some of them are slow to go, He, glory be to Him and exalted, indicating that the command remains in force even if all of them hold back, said: ﴿So fight in the way of Allah﴾; that is, the One to whom all command belongs; "even if you are alone."

Since it was as if it had been said, "What shall I do with those to whom I have been sent if they do not go forth?", He said, informing [him] that He had made him the bravest of people and the most knowledgeable in warfare and its management. Although He strengthened him with this, He had also undertaken to support him and did not leave him to anyone: ﴿You are not burdened except with yourself﴾; that is, there is no sin upon you for the sins of your followers if they stay behind you, and Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, has protected them from that. Nor is there any harm to you in this world from their abandoning [the jihad], for Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, alone is your Helper, and victory is only in His hand, glory be to Him and exalted. He would not command him with anything except that he is equal to it; so he is capable of fighting all the disbelievers alone, even if they were all the people of the earth. Indeed, at the Battle of Badr, which is the appointed encounter, and which is said to be the occasion of the revelation of this verse, he resolved to march out against the disbelievers even if no one went out with him. His companion al-Siddiq (the Truthful, i.e., Abu Bakr), may Allah be pleased with him, followed his example in fighting the people of apostasy (ridda), and he said to the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them: "By Allah, if I could find only these two, meaning his two daughters, [p-346] 'Aishah and Asma', may Allah be pleased with them both, I would fight them with them."

Since that might cause a slackening in calling [the believers to fight], He said: ﴿And urge the believers﴾; that is, command them to jihad, forbid them from abandoning it and from keeping company with anyone who discourages them from it, admonish them, and exert yourself in their affair, until they are prepared to go forth whenever they are called, to the extent that they are, because of the intensity of their readiness, as if present in the ranks at all times. Then He resumed the mention for the fruit of that, saying: ﴿It may be that Allah﴾; that is, the One who possesses all attributes of perfection; ﴿will restrain﴾ by His greatness; ﴿the might of those who disbelieve﴾; that is, from preventing you from manifesting the religion through your fighting and the fighting of those whom you urge. Indeed, He, glory be to Him and exalted, did so: He fulfilled His promise, supported His servant, and defeated the confederates alone, until the religion became manifest. It remains manifest, and the final outcome of this will be at the hand of ʿIsa (Jesus), peace be upon him.

Since the listener might understand that their restraint could not be achieved except by this, He said, as encouragement, warning, and precaution: ﴿And Allah is greater in might﴾; that is, the One who has no like; ﴿and greater in punishment﴾; that is, in torment and severity, [greater] than the fighters and those who are fought; ﴿and greater in making an example﴾; that is, in punishing with the greatest punishment, so that this destroys the one punished and prevents others from doing the same. Al-Imam Abu ʿAbd Allah al-Qazzaz said: it is said "nakkaltuhu tankilan" (I made an example of him) when I do an act to him that serves as a deterrent (nakal) to others, that is, a lesson, so that they turn back from the intent behind it [p-347], which is that whoever looks at it, or whoever hears of it, fears that the like of it will befall him, so that this becomes a restraint (qayd) preventing him from advancing. And "al-nikl" (nikl, a shackle or fetter), with a kasra, is the restraint.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 85:

Since this (the verse's preceding content) necessitates eagerness to obey the Prophet (ﷺ), especially in jihad; and eagerness toward those who have the attributes of the believers in devoting themselves to obedience; and turning away from everyone who has the attributes of the hypocrites; and persistence in expelling them, distancing them, being harsh toward them, and beware of sitting with them, until their sincerity becomes clear; and there were kinship ties between many of the sincere Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) and them, which necessitate a tenderness that calls for compassion toward them, bearing intercession on their behalf: either by permission to stay behind from jihad, due to the false excuses they embellish in speech; or by pardon for them when their faults are discovered; or by helping them, or helping others, with wealth and person, in the matter of jihad, when they claim that what prevents them is incapacity; and in other matters. Repentance was offered to them and to others. Righteousness is what the heart is at rest with, and sin is what stirs unease in the chest, and a person is a witness against himself. The inner states are known only to Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, and a person may display evil in the form of good. He, Glorified and Exalted is He, encouraged righteousness and warned against sin, by His saying, generalizing and beginning a new statement in answer to one who seems to have said: (p-348) "Will intercession not be accepted for them?":

﴿Whoever intercedes with a good intercession﴾; that is, brings it into being and renews it, whoever he may be, at whatever time; ﴿a good intercession﴾; that is, he establishes thereby the excuse of a Muslim in everything permissible in the religion, in order to bring him some good or ward off some harm from him; ﴿will have a share (nasīb) of it﴾; by the reward of his causing good.

﴿And whoever intercedes﴾, whoever he may be, at whatever time; ﴿with an evil intercession﴾; that is, by defending a criminal in a matter that is not permissible, and causing his elevation and the healing of his disease. He magnified evil intercession because the averting of harms takes precedence over the securing of benefits. So He said, expressing it with what conveys a share and conveys more than that, as a sharpening of the rebuke: ﴿he will have a portion (kifl) of it﴾. This is an explanation that intercession for them is evil if their criminality is established, and good if their repentance and submission are known.

Since each of the incitement of the believers to jihad and the good intercession is of the same valley as: "Whoever establishes a good practice (sunnah), he will have its reward and the reward of whoever acts upon it until the Day of Resurrection," their pairing is very fitting. The nasīb is a distinct portion of a thing, belonging to the one to whom it belongs; and likewise the kifl, except that usage indicates that it is greater than the nasīb. This is supported by what they said, that it may be meant to denote double. So it is as if it were a portion that bears responsibility for what belongs to him (p-349) of happiness and distance.

The people of lexicography said: "al-nasīb" is the share and the lot; and "al-kifl", with a kasra, is double, and the portion and lot. The root نصب revolves around a raised sign, and it entails elevation, placing, distinguishing, origin, return, and fatigue, so it entails pain. Among its implications also are limit, end, earnestness, and standing. The root كفل revolves around "al-kifal" (with vowel), which is incapacity, or its back part; and it entails guardianship, softness, gentleness, and delay. The Imam said: "al-kifl" is the portion upon which a person relies in obtaining benefits for himself and averting harms from himself; and what is intended here is the occurrence of the opposite of that, as in His saying: ﴿So give them tidings of a painful punishment﴾ [al-Inshiqaq: 24]. The purpose of it is to draw attention to the fact that intercession which leads to the falling away of the right and the strengthening of falsehood is greatly punished by Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He; end of quotation.

This stern warning is only intensified because of the knowledge that most souls incline toward intercession for falsehood on behalf of their companions. And since what is most suitable to eagerness is that it should not be cut off from its requirement, even if it is great in truth, so that this may serve as a deterrent from committing any part of it, even if small, He expressed the good with nasīb and the evil with kifl. What supports the intention of this is that (p-350) He, Exalted is He, when He mentioned what necessitates Paradise from faith and piety, and this was in the context of admonition to the People of the Book, who follow a law whose origin is true, by legislation of a messenger from Allah, so their abandonment of that is remote and requires an increase of encouragement, He expressed it with kifl, and said, Exalted is He: ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah and believe in His Messenger; He will give you a double portion (kiflayn) of His mercy﴾ [al-Hadid: 28]; to the end of it.

Since the nasīb is ambiguous in relation to our knowledge, because it varies according to the deficiency of the intercessors, and their advancing to intercession with knowledge or ignorance, and other matters that cannot be comprehended except by Allah, Glorified and Exalted is He, in knowledge and power, He said, Exalted is He, encouraging and warning: ﴿And Allah is over all things﴾; that is, the Possessor of Majesty and Honor; ﴿over all things﴾, of the intercessors and others, and of the reward of intercession; ﴿Vigilant (muqīt)﴾; that is, Watchful, and Witness, and Capable of giving what sustains, of the characters of souls, the states of hearts, the provisions of bodies, and everything by which subsistence is maintained; as reward and as beginning, from all directions; and according to what each one deserves of reward for intercession and of every good and evil.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 86:

When that was bound to lead to turning away from them altogether and rejecting them, both in word and in deed, Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, made clear that greeting (al-tahiyyah) does not belong to the category of intercession (al-shafa'ah), and that intercession follows from action, whereas greeting follows from outward appearance. So He, glory be to Him and exalted, said, joining it (ʿatifan) to what is implied in the sense: "So do not intercede for them while you know the evil of their intentions." Then He said, using the particle of certainty (ta'kid bi-adat al-tahaqquq) as good news to them that they will become, after the hardship they are in now, kings, or in the position of kings, who live, and for whom intercession is made; and as an exhortation to humility:

﴿And when you are greeted with a greeting﴾; that is, whatever greeting it is, provided it is prescribed. The root meaning of tahiyyah is kingship, and its derivation is from "al-hayah" (life). So it is as if the life of kingship is life, and whatever else is non-existence. Then it was applied to every supplication begun at the time of meeting. Al-Isfahani said: the word tahiyyah has become a metonym for honoring, so all kinds of honoring enter under the word tahiyyah.

﴿then greet with something better than it﴾; such as adding to it.

﴿or return it﴾; that is, without addition or reduction. This indicates the obligation of returning the greeting by the imperative form, and immediacy by the particle fa'; and consensus (al-ijma') agrees with that. Leaving the reply is contempt (ihanah), contempt is harm (darar), and harm is forbidden (haram). Al-Isfahani said: the one who initiates says, "al-salamu 'alaykum," and the one who replies says, "wa 'alaykumu al-salam," so that both the opening and the closing mention Allah, glory be to Him and exalted.

How excellent is placing this verse following the verse of jihad: it indicates that whoever offers peace must be left alone, even in war. Moreover, among the requirements of these two verses is that the foundation of this surah is the encouragement toward goodness, sympathy, (p-352) and connection. The cause of that is either wealth, and its command has already been mentioned in His saying (exalted is He): ﴿And when the division is present﴾ [al-Nisa': 8]; or other than that, and among its greatest forms is speech, because it is the interpreter of the heart, by which sympathy exists. Among the greatest of these is intercession and greeting. The Prophet (ﷺ) said, as reported by Muslim and the Four from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him): "By Him in whose hand my soul is, you will not enter Paradise until you believe, and you will not believe until you love one another. Shall I not direct you to something which, if you do it, you will love one another? Spread the salam among you."

Thus the mention of these two verses after the verse of jihad, which concludes with severity and punishment, is appropriate.

Since intercession is the greatest of these in goodness, it was put first; especially since its requirement is turning away, and the aim of the surah is connection, so its matter is more important and looking to it is more emphatic. Then he encouraged goodness in the response and warned against abandoning it, by His saying, giving the reason: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾; that is, the One who has encompassing knowledge and power; ﴿is ever﴾; that is, eternally and everlastingly; ﴿over all things a Hasib﴾; that is, one who counts all countable things, minute and great, sufficing them in their sustenance and rewards, calling to account for them, recompensing for them. All of that is the attribute of al-Muqit (the Sustainer).

Then he gave the reason for that by his words, indicating the inseparability of Tawhid (divine unity) and justice: ﴿Allah﴾; that is, the One who has no like; ﴿there is no god but He﴾; that is, and He has commanded you to be just in intercession and in greeting; so if you do not do it, because of the deficiencies you have (p-353), among which is the lack of unity, then He is the one who does it, and you must beware of Him, because He is One, so there is no opponent to Him in anything of the reckoning or otherwise, and nothing is hidden from Him. Judgment upon inward matters belongs to Him (exalted is He); as for you, you are only charged with the outward.

When it became clear that He has no opponent, it produced His words, clarifying the time of the Great Reckoning: ﴿He will surely gather you﴾; He emphasized it with the lam and the nun, indicating the presumption of an oath, to refute those who deny it. And since the gradual process of causing death occurs little by little, he expressed it with the particle of limit, so he said: ﴿until the Day of Resurrection﴾; the hā' is for emphasis. Then he confirmed it with his words: ﴿there is no doubt about it﴾; that is, He will separate you from those whom they informed you about among the hypocrites; He will scrutinize their conditions, clarify their places, and recompense each according to what he deserves.

Since the implied meaning is: "Who is greater in power than Allah?", he joined to it his words: ﴿And who is more truthful than Allah﴾; that is, the One to whom all perfection belongs, so no flaw attaches to Him; ﴿in speech﴾; and He has promised this, because it is the very essence of wisdom, and He swore to it, so it must come to pass.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 88:

Now that it has been established from what preceded that the hypocrites are disbelievers, with no ambiguity regarding their situation, and that He, glory be to Him and exalted, has revealed the ruling concerning their inner state by way of their being left to their fate, and their outward state by way of greeting them, and has warned whoever opposes this with what His wisdom has made obligatory upon Himself of gathering [them] for the Day of Judgment of Decision, to judge with justice, and has concluded by stating that the report about them and about all of that is true, this became a cause for firmly pronouncing their wretchedness, turning away from them, keeping far from interceding for them, and the consensus on this among every believer. Although the framework of the surah is based on connection, that is only where it does not lead to cutting off the command of God. So He (exalted) said, rebuking those who hesitated to firmly declare their distance from them: ﴿Why is it that you are divided into two groups concerning the hypocrites?﴾ O believers, meaning: what is the matter with you, in regard to the affairs of this world or the Hereafter, that you have split into ﴿two groups﴾, one part of you being harsh toward them and another part being gentle toward them?

Since this was clear in the manifestation of the obeyed command between the statement of their disbelief, He clarified it with His saying: ﴿And God﴾, meaning: while the case is that the King, with whom no one has any command, ﴿has reverted them﴾, meaning: has returned them upside down and overturned, ﴿because of what they earned﴾, meaning: after their profession of faith, due to such great offenses; so beware of that, and do not differ concerning their affair after this clarification.

In the Battle of "Uhud," and in the Tafsir of al-Bukhari, from Zayd ibn Thabit (may God be pleased with him), he said: "When the Prophet ﷺ went out to "Uhud," some people who had gone out with him turned back. The Companions of the Prophet ﷺ were two groups: one group said, 'We shall fight them,' and another group said, 'We shall not fight them.' Then the verse was revealed: ﴿Why is it that you are divided into two groups concerning the hypocrites?﴾ up to the end of the verse." And he said: "It is good, it expels sins," and in another narration: "As fire expels the impurity of silver." End of quotation. So the meaning then is: "Agree to proceed regarding them according to what is revealed to you in these verses."

Since the state of one who is gentle toward them is the state of one who wishes to guide them, God, glory be to Him and exalted, explicitly denounced this in them, to settle the matter of their disbelief. So He said: ﴿Do you wish to guide﴾, meaning: O believers, ﴿to guide﴾, meaning: to bring guidance into the heart of, ﴿whom God has misguided﴾, meaning: while He is the Supreme King, whose command is never reversed; and this is the meaning of His saying: ﴿And whomever﴾, meaning: while the case is that whoever ﴿God misguides﴾, meaning: with all His names and attributes, ﴿you will never find﴾, meaning: at all, O addressee, whoever he may be, ﴿for him any way﴾, meaning: to that from which He has misguided him at all. The meaning is: if your gentleness toward them is in hope of their guidance, that is a matter belonging to God alone; you are only obligated to invite. Whoever responds becomes fit for association, and whoever refuses, his severance becomes a religious duty, his killing an act of devotion, and harshness toward him obligatory.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 89:

When he had informed them of their misguidance and their steadfastness in it, he made known how deeply they were immersed in it. So he said: ﴿They wish﴾; that is, they love and desire with an intense longing; ﴿that you would disbelieve﴾; that is, that you would bring disbelief into being, renew it, and persist in it constantly; ﴿as they disbelieved﴾. Since their wish for your disbelief and your being equal to them did not entail a necessary connection, he joined to the wished-for act, without causing it, the phrase: ﴿so you would be alike﴾; that is, and they wish (p-356) that as a consequence of that there would follow and result that you and they would be alike; ﴿equal﴾; that is, in misguidance; that is, you would bring disbelief into being, renew it, and persist in it constantly. Thus you hope, in a time of gentleness toward them, for their guidance, while they wish for your disbelief and your misguidance. You have then become far apart in your paths and divergent in your aims.

When he had informed them of this wish, he made the command to disassociate from them, until they make it right, a consequence of it, as a clarification that their profession of faith is not accepted unless they confirm it by deed. So he said: ﴿Therefore do not take﴾; that is, O believers; ﴿from among them allies﴾; that is, close associates from among you; ﴿until they emigrate﴾; that is, until they actually perform emigration; ﴿in the way of Allah﴾; that is, they abandon whoever opposes them, for the sake of the One who has no likeness, and bring about their own abandonment of him: if they are in the abode of war, by leaving it; and if they are with you, by abandoning friendship with the disbelievers and agreement with them in their words and deeds, even if they are the closest of their relatives. Their emigration in all of this is by your joining with them in all your words and deeds. General emigration is abandoning what Allah, glorified and exalted is He, and His Messenger (ﷺ) have forbidden.

When he had forbidden allying with them, and limited the prohibition by emigration, he made a consequence of it his saying: ﴿But if they turn away﴾; that is, from the emigration mentioned; ﴿then seize them﴾; that is, subdue them by capture and otherwise; ﴿and kill them wherever you find them﴾; that is, in a place of lawfulness or in the sacred precinct. Since they, in this state, do not befriend the believers except under constraint, he said: ﴿And take not from among them a friend﴾; that is, do not strain to take from them anyone with whom you would act as one does with a close and sincere companion; ﴿nor a helper﴾; against any of your enemies. Rather, keep wholly away from them.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 90:

When Allah, glorified and exalted is He, had commanded regarding them, on the assumption of their turning away, what He commanded, He made an exception from it, saying: ﴿Except those who join a people between whom and you there is a covenant﴾, fleeing from you, and they are, according to the majority (jumhur), among the disbelievers; ﴿or who come to you, their hearts restrained from fighting you or fighting their own people﴾.
