The meaning of the restriction is: "They are nothing but non-gods, because of the deficiency they possess." ﴿Wa in yad'una﴾, meaning they in reality worship; ﴿illa shaytanan﴾, meaning because he is the one who commands them to do this and who makes it attractive to them; ﴿mariday﴾, meaning rebellious, stiff-necked, disobedient, constantly persisting in disobedience, stripped of all good, consumed by evil deeds, and far removed from all safety. It derives from *شاط* (\*shaṭa\*), *شطن* (\*shaṭana\*), and *مرد* (\*marada\*), with the 'ayn vowelled either with a fatḥa or a ḍamma. He expressed it with the pattern *فعيل* (\*fa'īl\*), which is used for intensification, in the context of condemning them, as a warning that they had worshipped something whose wickedness is beyond doubt, because it is entirely evil. This differs from what occurs in surah al-Saffat, since its context requires that there be no intensification, as will come, God willing (Exalted is He).

Then He explained that by His saying: ﴿May Allah curse him﴾; that is, the Supreme King removed him from every good, so he was distanced and burned.

And since the implied sense is: "He said, persisting in enmity through envy: 'By Your might, I will surely strive to misguide others as You have removed me,'" He followed it with His saying: ﴿And he said, "I will surely take﴾; that is, by Allah, I will surely strive to take; ﴿from Your servants﴾; those who are under Your subjugation and do not depart from Your will; ﴿an appointed portion﴾; that is, a share which You Yourself have decreed for me;

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 119:

﴿And I will surely lead them astray﴾; that is, away from Your straight path, by means of the whisperings (al-waswasa) and the adorning of falsehoods with which You have empowered me; ﴿and I will surely arouse false desires in them﴾; that is, every falsehood I am able to inspire: denial of the resurrection and other such things; the prolonging of works and the attainment of hopes in this world and the Hereafter, through reliance on mercy, pardon, benevolence, and the like, which are a cause of postponing repentance; ﴿and I will surely command them﴾

Since he knew, from the appetites and the portions of pleasure with which they were created, which prepared them to obey him, and since his commandment is, in the view of every intelligent person, extremely unlikely to be corruption, he emphasized his statement: ﴿so they will surely slit﴾; that is, they will cut (them) in many cuts, ﴿the ears of the cattle﴾; splitting them, as a mark of what they forbade for themselves; ﴿and I will surely command them, so they will surely alter the creation of Allah﴾; that is, the one who possesses perfect wisdom, for whom there is no equal, through various kinds of alteration: from altering the original sound nature (al-fitra) to what is less than that, such as gouging out the eye of the protected camel, and similar things. This is an allusion to what the people of ignorance (ahl al-jahiliyya) forbade for themselves by drawing near to the idols, such as the sa'iba and what accompanies it, whose annulment was indicated at the beginning of "al-Ma'ida" by His saying: ﴿Lawful for you are the beasts of cattle, except what is recited to you﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 1], and which was stated explicitly at its end by His saying: ﴿Allah did not ordain any bahira﴾ [al-Ma'ida: 103]. The alteration may be by tattooing and by filing the teeth, and everything that opposes the religion enters into it, since the original nature calls to the opposite of that. To the point that they included in it the resemblance of men to women in effeminacy and what branches from it, and the resemblance of women to men in lesbianism and what tends toward it.

Since the intended sense is: "Whoever follows him in that has indeed lost, because he has become a protector (waliyy) of the Shaytan," he joined to it, in a generalizing manner, His saying: ﴿And whoever takes﴾; that is, whoever burdens himself, from among them or from others, with altering the original nature, ﴿the Shaytan as a protector (waliyy)﴾. Since that entails opposing Allah, glorified and exalted, and what is lower than that rank is extremely numerous, he used the partitive form, so that the totality may be understood a fortiori; so He said: ﴿instead of Allah﴾; that is, the One who combines every beautiful attribute; ﴿then he has indeed lost﴾ by taking that, even if at the lowest degrees of association; ﴿a manifest loss﴾; that is, in the utmost clarity and worthlessness, as the pattern of the word "khusranan" (fu'lan) indicates, because he has taken as a protector one from whom there is no good.

Then he gave the reason for that in His words: ﴿He promises them﴾; that is, by causing them to imagine, through what reaches their hearts by whispering (al-waswasa), concerning some of the falsehoods, that it (the attainment) is near at hand; and that (p-408) there is no difficulty in obtaining it; and that if it does not come about, there is harm in its loss. So they strive to obtain it, and time is wasted for them in that, and they commit in pursuit of it what is not lawful of dreadful deeds and humiliation. ﴿And He arouses in them desires﴾; that is, He adorns for them the hanging of hopes on what cannot be attained. Then he clarified that with His words: ﴿And not﴾; that is, while the state is that He does not ﴿promise them﴾; and he used the explicit noun in place of the pronoun to draw attention to greater aversion, so he said: ﴿Satan﴾; that is, the burnt one (al-muhtariq), the far removed from good; ﴿except as deception﴾; that is, adorning with falsehood; cheating, deceit, and delusion; displaying what has no reality, or has an evil reality, in the most splendid, noblest, and most pleasing guise to the soul and most appealing to the natural disposition. For the root "gh-r" and the root "r-gh" revolve around honor, beauty, and comfortable living, so *ghurur* is the removal of that.

Since He had established this for them, it inevitably produced His saying: ﴿Those﴾; that is, those far removed from every good; ﴿their refuge is Hell﴾; that is, it will scowl at them and blaze upon them because of what they took, of those created from it, as protectors; ﴿and they will not find from it any escape﴾; that is, any place; they will not incline toward it, not even a little of inclining.

When he had mentioned what is for the disbelievers, as a warning, he followed it with what is for others, as an encouragement, so He said: ﴿And those who believed﴾; that is, with a promise that admits no breach; ﴿gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾ (p-409). He brought it close and made it partial by His saying: ﴿beneath which rivers flow﴾; that is, to irrigate its land; wherever a river is channelled from them, it flows.

Since departing from the homeland in general, even for a passing need, is very hard, how much more so is this? He said: ﴿abiding therein﴾. And since abiding (khulud) is applied to mere long staying, He indicated that it has no end by His saying: ﴿forever﴾. Then He confirmed this by the fact that reality corresponds to it, and it does correspond to reality; so He said: ﴿a promise of Allah in truth﴾; that is, reality corresponds to it, because He is the Greatest King, and His promise has come forth with this; and who is more truthful in promise than Allah, and in report, whose report is true and corresponds to reality? ﴿And who is more truthful in speech than Allah﴾; that is, the One singled out by the attributes of perfection; ﴿in speech﴾. He emphasized more here, because it stands in contrast to the promise of Satan; and the promise of Satan agrees with the desire upon which souls are formed, so one turns away from it only with great difficulty.

When He (exalted be He) had informed them of the punishment prepared for them and for those who misled them, and of the reward prepared for the believers, and since they were feeding themselves vain wishes, claiming that there would be no consequence for them for toying with the religion, neither in this world nor in the Hereafter, and the People of the Book (ahl al-kitab) encouraged them in this and claimed that they were the sons of God and His beloved, and that He would not call them to account for anything, and that no one would enter Paradise except Jews or Christians, or those for whom intercession was made, and similar falsehoods by which they gave hope to whoever allied with them, that they would save him. (p-410) The polytheists would say: ﴿We have more wealth and children, and we will not be punished﴾ [Saba': 35], and similar things, as al-'As ibn Wa'il said to Khabbab ibn al-Aratt, when the latter demanded a debt that he owed him: "Leave me to that abode, and I will pay you from what I will have there. By God, you and your companion will not be more favoured with God there than I, nor have a greater share." So God revealed concerning that: ﴿Have you seen the one who disbelieved in Our signs?﴾ [Maryam: 77], and the verses at the end of "Maryam." And the People of the Book would say to them: "You are better guided in the way." When this was the case, He (exalted be He), refuting both groups, said: ﴿It is not﴾, i.e., what God has promised and threatened, ﴿by your wishes﴾, i.e., O Arabs, ﴿nor by the wishes of the People of the Book﴾, i.e., those with which Satan gives all of you false hopes.

Since their wishes were that they would not be requited for their wicked deeds, this necessarily led to His saying: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾, i.e., with calamities, such as illnesses and other things, in this world if good is intended for him, and in the Hereafter if evil is intended for him. How excellent is its placement in response to the satanic delusion mentioned in His saying: "He promises them and gives them false hopes"! Thus the discourse fully exposes the deceit of the devils of the jinn and then of mankind, in their deception of whoever keeps company with them, and it gives despair to whoever accepts from them. And how wonderful is its conclusion with His saying: ﴿and he will not find for himself, (p-411) besides God, any protector or helper﴾! Since every person falls short of his Lord, He expressed it with His saying: ﴿besides God﴾, i.e., the One who possesses all greatness; ﴿a protector﴾, i.e., a close friend who does with him what a close friend does; ﴿nor a helper﴾, i.e., one who will help him at any time. And how closely it is linked with the conclusion of the first verses warning against them: ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book, who purchase error?﴾ [al-Nisa': 44], up to His saying: ﴿And God is sufficient as a protector, and God is sufficient as a helper﴾ [al-Nisa': 45]! This indicates that the aim of the hypocrites in following and aligning themselves with the People of the Book is nothing but protection and support; and that they have lost their hope, so they sought help from one who has no power to help, and abandoned the One to whom alone belongs true help.

When He had shown the recompense of the evildoer as a warning, He followed it with the reward of the good-doer as glad tidings. He said: ﴿And whoever does righteous deeds﴾; and God (Exalted is He) lightened the burden upon His servants with His words: ﴿of the righteous deeds﴾. When He generalized by mentioning whoever it is that this implies, in His words: ﴿whether male or female﴾, He restricted that with His words: ﴿while he is a believer﴾; that is, while the state is that he is ﴿a believer﴾, so that his building of deeds is upon the foundation of faith. ﴿Those﴾; that is, the people of high rank. He put the verb of entering into the passive form in the recitation of Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, Abu Ja'far, Abu Bakr from 'Asim, and Rawh from Ya'qub, and into the active form in the recitation of others, because the intended meaning is the act itself, not its being from a specific agent; although the recitation of the first group is more informative: ''yudkhalun'' (they will be made to enter); that is, God will cause them to enter ﴿the Garden﴾; that is, the one described; ﴿and they will not be wronged﴾. He put the verb into the passive form, because the intended meaning is their being spared from it, not restricted to a specific agent; ﴿a speck﴾; that is, God does not wrong the obedient among them by diminishing anything at all, nor the disobedient by adding anything at all. The ''naqir'' is what is in the back of a date-stone, that very small pit; it was used as a metaphor for nothingness. This is according to what people commonly understand; otherwise, God (Exalted is He) may do whatever He wills, for His dominion and kingdom are general, and no injustice can be conceived of from Him, however He acts.

Nazm al-Durar of al-Biqa'i on surah 4, verse 125:

When Allah, glorified is He, exposed their falsehood and made clear their wickedness, He denied that anyone could have a better religion than one who follows the religion of Ibrahim (Abraham), whom they claim to have followed, a claim whose hollowness was already exposed in Surat Al 'Imran. Joining this to what is implied, the sentence reads: "Who then is better in religion, in reckoning, and in judgment than Allah, glorified and exalted?" So: ﴿And who is better in religion﴾. Or the implied sense may be: "Because they did good in their religion, who is better in religion than them?" But He stated the attribute in general terms, to make the ruling universal, to teach the believer what to do, and to urge him toward it, saying: ﴿than one who submits﴾, that is, gives himself over. Since the intended meaning is sincerity (ikhlas), which is the noblest of things, He expressed it through the face, which is the noblest of the limbs, saying: ﴿his face﴾, that is, his direction, the orientation toward which he turns his face, meaning his whole intention, which is bound to submission itself, ﴿to Allah﴾ entirely. He has no movement and no stillness except in what pleases Him, because He is the One who has no like. This is a restriction (hasr) without the form of restriction. It conveys the corruption of the path of one who turns his face toward other than Him, whether by seeking help from someone else or otherwise (p-٤١٣). This applies especially to the Mu'tazilah (the rationalist school), who hold that obedience comes from themselves and that it necessitates their reward, and that disobedience likewise necessitates their punishment. In reality, then, they hope only in themselves and fear nothing else. The people of the Sunnah (Ahl al-Sunnah) entrusted management, creation, and bringing into being to the Truth, and they are the Muslims.

When He (exalted is He) expressed perfect belief in the past tense, He made continuity a condition, along with the outward deeds, by saying: ﴿and he is a doer of good﴾, that is, and the situation is that he is a believer, watchful, with no heedlessness in him at all, rather goodness (ihsan) is a firmly rooted attribute of his, because he worships Allah as though he sees Him. These ten words thus comprise the whole religion, its foundations and its branches, together with an encouragement through complete praise for the one who follows it, and a conveying of complete blame for anyone else.

Since this encompasses whoever follows the religion of any prophet at all, before its abrogation (naskh), He restricted it by saying: ﴿and followed﴾, that is, with effort on his part, ﴿the religion of Ibrahim﴾, who was famous among all the communities for calling only to Allah, glorified and exalted, alone, and for disavowing everything else: spheres, stars, idols, nature, and other things, while that follower is ﴿hanif﴾, that is, flexible, easy, inclined toward evidence. "Religion" (millah) is what the original natural disposition (fitrah) calls for, with the aid of sound reason, of the perfection of Islam through monotheism (tawhid).

Since the implied sense, to encourage this following, is: "Allah, glorified and exalted, has made the religion of Ibrahim the best of religions, and created him on the day He created him as a hanif," He joined to it His words: ﴿And Allah took﴾, that is, the Supreme King took, the taking of one who is helping in this and striving in it, ﴿Ibrahim as a khalil﴾ (intimate friend), because he was a hanif. This is an expression of his being singled out for a dignity resembling the dignity of an intimate friend with his friend: the repeated sending of messengers with revelation between him and Allah, the answering of his supplication, the manifestation of extraordinary signs (kharq) upon him and upon his family, support against enemies, and other gracious kindnesses. He made his name explicit in the place of a pronoun, to state the intended meaning clearly, to guard against ambiguity, and to exalt his rank by honoring his mention.

Now when He had informed of whom He loves, whom He hates, what pleases Him, and what angers Him, and it might be supposed that He lacks the power to take (a people) other than those who were taken, or to make (a people) other than those who were made, or that some hair-splitter might carp at this, and so suppose that the speech involves some dependence on a need, whether for the (divine) wisdom or otherwise, He said: ﴿And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens﴾; that is, and the state of affairs is that it belongs to the One singled out for Oneness, for there is no equal to Him, ﴿and whatever is on the earth﴾. Since the context concerns the hypocrites and the polytheists, He emphasized, saying: ﴿and whatever is on the earth﴾, including Ibrahim, peace be upon him, and others besides him, indicating that He is the Perfect in dominion and the Mighty in sovereignty. Therefore He does not give except to one who follows His friends and keeps away from His enemies, and He does not choose except one whom He knows to be among the best, (p-415) and He is, along with that, capable of whatever He wills, of confirmation and of alteration. For this reason He said: ﴿And Allah is ever, of all things, Encompassing﴾; that is, the King to whom belongs all perfection, ﴿of all things﴾, that is, of the two (heavens and earth) and of other than them, ﴿Encompassing﴾ in knowledge and power. Thus, however much (the servants) increase, He, in His promise and His threat, concerning the obedient and the disobedient, nothing of them is hidden from Him, and nothing overcomes Him.

(p-416) Since He, glory be to Him and exalted, arranged this Book so that it mentions rulings on the fundamentals (al-usul) and the branches (al-furu') and then explains them with promise and threat, and with encouragement and warning, and binds them together with the proofs of His greatness, majesty, immense benevolence and perfection, and then returns to explaining the rulings in the most wondrous order, because placing the intended meaning in such a mould is closer to acceptance, and such an arrangement is more fitting to make an impact on hearts, since souls do not submit to the imposition of burdensome deeds unless it is accompanied by glad tidings and warning, and this has no effect except when one is certain of the utmost perfection of the one from whom that speech issues; and since it does not pass from one style to another except with the utmost suitability between the end of each type and the beginning of what follows, with perfect connection in wording and meaning, then He, glory be to Him and exalted, did in this surah, regarding the rulings of justice with which He began the surah, concerning the union whose foundation is marriage and inheritance and other matters connected with it, as He has explained, until He concluded here with Islam, which brings about acceptance of all that (p-416), and with the greatness of the King, which necessitates the completion of Islam. The proofs were established and the evidences shone forth. Among the greatest aims of the surah is justice toward the weak among orphans and others, in inheritance and other matters. The granting of inheritance to women and children, whether males or females, is something their souls refused and their hearts were saturated with hatred for it. Distinguishing in establishing what is of this kind is more effective, and delivering it little by little in the moulds of eloquence is more beneficial. Therefore He connected to that His saying, exalted be He: ﴿They ask you﴾, in a circumstantial clause (jumlah haliyyah) relating to the Name of Majesty (ism al-jalalah, the Name Allah) preceding it, meaning: He has what has been mentioned, so there is no room for objection to Him, while they ask you, seeking that you give them a verdict concerning some of what He has granted of His dominion to some of His creatures, ﴿concerning women﴾, hoping to monopolize them with wealth and other things, arguing that wealth should belong only to one who protects the honour. Yet they had worshipped females besides Him, and had assigned to them a share of the produce of tilth and cattle that He had provided them, and had granted them as sustenance, by way of weakness. So do not be surprised at the state of those who repeatedly seek a verdict, which in custom is usually sought only about what is subject to objection, concerning living females and male children. He, the King of perfect dominion, the great in possession, granted them some of what He wills, and He did not object to Himself when He granted females who have neither life nor benefit, from what is in His hand, while their ownership truly belongs to another, and the owner has not permitted what the giver does not benefit from.

Since the occasion, by the frequency of their asking, required increased attentiveness, He said: ﴿Say: "Allah"﴾, commanding, expressing with the Greatest Name (al-ism al-a'zam), alerting to the recollection of what was mentioned at the beginning of the surah; ﴿gives you a verdict﴾, meaning: He makes clear His ruling for you; ﴿concerning them﴾, meaning: now, so that you may stand for them with justice; ﴿and what is recited to you﴾, meaning: whose recitation is renewed among you until the end of time, as a decisive sword and a binding and comprehensive ruling; ﴿in the Book﴾, meaning: in what preceded at the beginning of the surah, in His saying: ﴿And if you fear that you will not be just with orphans, then marry what seems good to you of women﴾ [al-Nisa': 3], and other than that; ﴿concerning the orphan women﴾, meaning: concerning the matter of orphans of this category; ﴿to whom you do not give﴾, meaning: due to holding back in this matter and repeatedly seeking a verdict about it; ﴿what has been prescribed for them﴾, meaning: what has been obligated of inheritance and all rights as an obligation, which is of the utmost binding force; ﴿and you desire to marry them﴾, meaning: in that you desire, or out of aversion to them, ﴿for their beauty or their ugliness﴾; and [He gives a verdict] concerning ﴿the weak among the children﴾, meaning: those whose weakness exists and whose weakening is intended by withholding their rights from them. Since the intended sense was: "concerning standing for them with justice, that is, regarding their inheritance and all their rights, and not belittling them for their youth", He followed it with His saying: ﴿and that you stand for orphans﴾, meaning: that you act with the strength and haste of one who rises and is energized, ﴿in justice﴾ (p-418), of males and females, meaning: with justice regarding inheritance and other matters.

Since the intended sense was: "whatever evil you do in that, Allah is indeed Knowing of it, and Capable over you", He followed it with His saying, as encouragement: ﴿And whatever good you do﴾, meaning: in that or in other matters, ﴿indeed Allah﴾, meaning: to whom belongs all perfection, ﴿is Knowing of it﴾, meaning: He is worthy, and He is the most Generous of the generous and the wisest of judges, to give the doer according to His generosity and the loftiness of his rank; so be content of soul and comforted in eye. Al-Bukhari in the chapters on partnership and marriage, Muslim at the end of the Book, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i in the chapter on marriage narrated from ʿUrwah that he asked ʿĀ'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, about the saying of Allah, mighty and majestic: ﴿And if you fear that you will not be just with orphans﴾ [al-Nisa': 3], up to "four". She said: "O son of my sister, she is the orphan girl who is in the care of her guardian, who shares with him in his wealth, and he is pleased with her wealth and her beauty, so the guardian wants to marry her without being just regarding her dowry, giving her the same as others give her. So they were forbidden to marry them unless they are just to them and bring them up to the highest custom of dowry; and they were commanded to marry whatever women are lawful to them other than them." ʿUrwah said: ʿĀ'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "Then the people sought a verdict from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ (p-419) after this verse concerning them, so Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿They ask you﴾ up to ﴿and you desire to marry them﴾."

What Allah mentioned that is recited to you in the Book is the first verse in which He said: ﴿And if you fear that you will not be just with orphans, then marry what seems good to you of women﴾ [al-Nisa': 3]. ʿĀ'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "And the saying of Allah, exalted be He, in the other verse: ﴿and you desire to marry them﴾, it is the desire of one of you for his orphan girl, and Muslim said: for his orphan — who is in his care, when she is little in wealth and beauty. So they were forbidden to marry those orphan women whose wealth and beauty they desired except with justice, because of their aversion to them." Muslim added: "When they are little in wealth and beauty." Al-Bukhari said in the chapter on marriage: "Just as they leave her when they are averse to her, so it is not permitted for them to marry her when they desire her, unless they are just to her, and give her her full right in the dowry." In al-Bukhari and Muslim, in the chapter on tafsir, also from ʿUrwah: ﴿They ask you concerning women﴾, the verse; she said: "It is the man who has the orphan girl under his care, he is her guardian and her heir; she has a share with him in his wealth, even in the palm-cluster; so he desires to marry her, and dislikes to marry her to another man who would share his wealth with what she shares, so he withholds her; so this verse was revealed." In a narration of Muslim: "It was revealed concerning the man who has an orphan girl under his care, he is her guardian and her heir, and she has wealth, and she has no one who disputes on her behalf; so he does not marry her for her wealth, and harms her and treats her badly. So He said: ﴿And if you fear that you will not be just with orphans, then marry what seems good to you of women﴾ [al-Nisa': 3], meaning: what I have made lawful to you; leave this one whom you harm." In another narration of his and of al-Bukhari, in the chapter on marriage: "He turns away from her, desiring not to marry her, and dislikes that she be married to someone else, so that he would share with him in his wealth" — al-Bukhari said: "so that he would enter upon him in his wealth" — "so he withholds her, and does not marry her, and does not allow her to marry." Al-Bukhari added: "So Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, forbade them from that." The summary of this, as transmitted by al-Asbahani, is that in the pre-Islamic era a man would have an orphan girl under his care, and he would throw his garment over her; once he did that, no one could ever marry her. If she was beautiful and he desired her, he would marry her and consume her wealth; and if she was ugly, he would prevent men from her until she died, and then he would inherit her (p-421).

How fitting is the mention of this ruling, about which many references have been made, in a manner that indicates that some souls do not submit to it, right after the verse of Islam, whose meaning is submission, humility and goodness, which in custom has come to be used most for giving, affection and compassion, especially toward the weak; and the mention of Abraham, peace be upon him, who, as previously stated, fulfilled the words with which Allah tested him and carried them out without reconsideration or hesitation; and that he was a ḥanīf, inclining toward the proof, as a reproach to whoever has the proof of reason established against him and the clear transmitted text comes to him, yet he keeps reconsidering! And if you reflect on His saying, exalted be He: ﴿Whoever does evil will be recompensed for it﴾ [al-Nisa': 123], together with His saying before it: ﴿And let those fear who, if they left behind them weak offspring, would fear for them﴾ [al-Nisa': 9], an excellent connection will also appear to you.

(p-422) When they began to give the orphans their property, and to marry the wealthy women among them while mistreating some of them, Allah (Exalted is He) followed this with a ruling on cases of discord between spouses. He said: ﴿And if a woman﴾, meaning one woman, or [a woman] among co-wives. Since the expectation of something disliked is a matter of concern, He said: ﴿fears﴾, meaning she anticipates it, and suspects, from the indications that appear to her, ﴿ill-treatment (nushuz) from her husband﴾, meaning haughtiness, as she sees him belittling her by withholding her rights, or treating her badly in companionship; ﴿or aversion﴾ on his part, in his heart, by her no longer seeing from him the conversation, companionship and intimacy that she saw before. She fears this may lead to separation, even though he makes an effort to be kind to her in word and deed. ﴿There is no blame﴾, meaning no sin or inclination, ﴿upon them both if they make peace﴾, meaning that the spouses bring about ﴿a settlement between themselves﴾ through reconciliation. This is according to the recitation (qira'a) of the majority. According to the recitation of the Kufans, with a damma on the yā' [yuṣliḥā], a sukūn on the ṣād and a kasra on the lām, the implied reading is "reform" (iṣlāḥan). However, since what is commanded is achieved by the least thing that can be called a settlement (ṣulḥ), He formed the verbal noun on neither of these two verbs, and said, in an unqualified form: ﴿a settlement﴾, by her giving up part of the dowry, or part of her share of time, or something similar, and by him being gentle with her in return by treating her well.

Since the implied meaning is: "There is no blame upon them if they separate on a fair basis," He followed it with His words: ﴿and settlement is better﴾, meaning, than the separation alluded to by the omitted clause, because settlement is founded on complete kindness with mutual contentment from both sides, whereas separation is founded on justice, which usually entails the anger of one of them. Although separation shares in good with settlement, it is inferior. The separation is omitted (tayy) because the basis of the surah is on keeping ties. (p-423) Since the source of the quarrelling that prevents settlement is a harshness of temperament, Glorified and Exalted is He depicted this to make people averse to it. He said, as an interruption between these clauses, to urge generosity, and by making the verb passive, to indicate that no one would want this presence attributed to him: ﴿And the souls are made present to stinginess (shuḥḥ)﴾, meaning the souls that look at their own preciousness with self-admiration; ﴿stinginess﴾, meaning greed, bad character, meanness, unhappiness, and withholding what one has. All of this returns to bad character, a poor disposition, and a crookedness of the original nature, which He alluded to with the term "presence" that is constant and cannot be separated from it except through great striving, by which one gains much reward.

Since this is a bad trait, He did not name its agent. The meaning is that someone made it present to them, so it became constant with them and they could not be freed from it except by Allah's enabling them, by overcoming it through remembering what Glorified and Exalted is He has of good reward. Since the implied meaning is: "If you are stingy, then He knows best what in stinginess entails blame," He followed it with His words: ﴿And if you do good﴾, meaning you bring about good by upholding your marriages and what you have been encouraged to do of good companionship, even if you dislike it; ﴿and fear Allah﴾, meaning you bring about piety by avoiding everything that causes any kind of harm, indicating that the stingy person is neither a doer of good nor one who is pious. ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, meaning He who combines the attributes of perfection, (p-424) ﴿is ever﴾, eternally and everlastingly, ﴿Acquainted with what you do﴾, meaning in every instance of stinginess and good; ﴿Acquainted﴾, meaning His knowledge of it is complete. You know that He is the most generous of the generous, so He will reward you for it with the best reward.

When the Exalted and Glorified (Allah) mentioned that standing firmly upon the truth, let alone upon excellence (ihsan), is difficult, even when a wife is only one, He followed it by stating that this is even more difficult when there are several. He said (ﷻ), emphasizing with the particle of emphasis: ﴿And you will never be able to be just between the wives﴾; that is, you will never be able to produce within yourselves a fully sustained and constant inclination (to justice); ﴿to be just﴾; that is, without any injustice at all; ﴿between the wives﴾; in all the rights that each one of them is owed from you; ﴿even if you strive to do so﴾; that is, to accomplish that. This, together with His saying (ﷻ): ﴿But if you fear that you will not be just, then [marry only] one﴾ [al-Nisa': 3], serves as a conclusion that restricts the matter to one wife.

When the Exalted and Glorified (Allah) informed that plural marriage (nikah al-'adad) cannot be free of inclination, He made the following statement a consequence of it: ﴿So do not incline﴾; that is, if plurality is unavoidable for you, or if inclination occurs while you have only one wife, then do not incline. Since inclination in its absolute sense is not within one's power to abandon, one is not held accountable for it. So He clarified the intended meaning by His saying: ﴿completely﴾. Then He made a consequence of it His saying: ﴿[away from one] and leave her﴾; that is, the woman; ﴿as if suspended﴾; that is, between being married and being unmarried, between wedlock and being alone.

Since great inclination is within one's power to abandon, the meaning is: "If you incline completely, while maintaining the marital bond, then indeed Allah is ever Avenger and Reckoner." He then joined to it His saying: ﴿And if you amend and fear Allah﴾; that is, by bringing about reform through justice in the division (of time and provision), and piety through abstaining from oppression, at all times; ﴿then indeed Allah﴾; that is, the One to whom belongs all perfection; ﴿is ever Forgiving and Merciful﴾; that is, the One who effaces sins, abundant in honoring; so He is worthy to forgive you the absolute inclination and to lavish upon you garments of blessing.

[p. 425]

And when it is among reform to live with one another in kindness, he mentioned its counterpart, saying: ﴿But if they separate﴾; that is, each of the two spouses parts from the other. ﴿Allah will enrich each﴾; that is, the One who possesses all attributes of perfection; ﴿each﴾; that is, each of them; meaning He will make him or her self-sufficient: this one with a man, and that one with a woman, or with something else of His kindness. He then explained the source of this sufficiency, saying: ﴿from His abundance﴾; that is, from the all-encompassing scope of His power and from every other attribute of perfection. And for greater care in establishing these meanings in the souls, so that they are present to the mind against stinginess, He repeated His greatest, all-comprehensive Name, saying: ﴿And Allah is ever﴾; that is, the Possessor of majesty and honour, from eternity and to eternity; ﴿All-Encompassing﴾; that is, encompassing everything; ﴿All-Wise﴾; that is, He places things in their most fitting positions.

[p. 426] Since the foundation of this surah rests on mutual affection, mercy, and kinship, He did not mention divorce in it except by way of allusion in this verse, explaining His tenderness, the vastness of His mercy, and the comprehensiveness of His nurture. In that is the meaning of connection and affection. Ibn al-Zubayr said: Because of the abundance of what arises from pursuing the desires of the self within marriage, together with kinship, and that is subtle and obscure, therefore the command to taqwa (God-consciousness) is repeated often in this surah, and it opens with it: ﴿Be mindful of your Lord﴾ [al-Nisa larger: 1] ﴿and be mindful of God, through whom you ask one another, and the wombs﴾ [al-Nisa: 1] ﴿And We had certainly enjoined those who were given the Scripture before you﴾

When He (exalted is He) mentioned the verse of separation and concluded it with the two attributes of vastness and wisdom, He indicated the first by encouraging the seeking of His bounty: ﴿And to God belongs﴾; i.e., the One to whom all greatness belongs; ﴿whatever is in the heavens﴾. And since the context is the explanation of the weakness of souls and their inclination toward deficiencies, and they needed a strengthening of speech that would remove them from the falsehood to which they had become accustomed, He said: ﴿and whatever is on the earth﴾. He indicated the second by the enjoining of taqwa, because He repeated the exhortation to taqwa in these sentences, in the context of the conditional, with His saying: ﴿And if you do good and are mindful﴾ [al-Nisa: 128] ﴿And if you reform and are mindful﴾ [al-Nisa: 129]. Thus He informed, after the kindness of that context, that His enjoining of it is emphatic and has not ceased, anciently or recently, because knowledge of sharing in a matter is more conducive to acceptance and lighter on the soul. So He said (exalted is He): ﴿And We had certainly enjoined﴾; i.e., by what We have of greatness.

Since sharing in the rulings necessitates desire for them and lightens their burden, and since an enjoining addressed to the whole world is more worthy of acceptance, He said: ﴿those who were given the Scripture﴾; i.e., the Torah, the Gospel, and others. He made the verb passive, because the aim is to show that they were people of knowledge, so as to encourage what they were enjoined; and as an indication that knowledge in itself prepares one for acceptance; and to convey that their enjoining is more general, whether it was in a Book or upon the tongue of the Messenger without a Book. And since their being given the Scripture did not encompass the entire past, and likewise the enjoining, He said: ﴿before you﴾; i.e., from the Children of Israel and others; ﴿and [to] you﴾; i.e., and We enjoined you just as We enjoined them. And since al-tawsiyah (enjoining) means speech, he explained it with His saying: ﴿that be mindful of God﴾; i.e., the One whose vengeance cannot be withstood, because there is no equal to Him.

Since the implied meaning is: "If you are mindful, then it is your portion and your happiness in both abodes," He joined to it His saying: ﴿But if you disbelieve﴾; i.e., by abandoning taqwa; ﴿then to God belongs﴾; i.e., the One who has absolute perfection; ﴿whatever is in the heavens﴾. And since the context is the supposition of disbelief, the emphasis in His saying was fitting: ﴿and whatever is on the earth﴾; of you and of others, of animals and inanimate things, bodies, spirits, and states.

Since the meaning is: "Nothing goes out of His dominion or His will, and no harm reaches Him through your disbelief; if you do it, you harm only yourselves, because He is free of need of you; [p. 428] His majesty does not increase through acts of obedience, nor decrease through sins and misdeeds," He emphasized it with His saying, indicating His self-sufficiency and His deserving of praise: ﴿And God is ever﴾; i.e., the One to whom all encompassing belongs; ﴿Free of need﴾; i.e., free of every thing, absolutely independent in His essence; ﴿Praiseworthy﴾; i.e., praised by every tongue, both in speech and in state, whether you disbelieve or give thanks. Thus this was the utmost in explaining His wisdom.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 132:

Since the king may not prevent objection against the owner, he made clear that this applies only to a deficient kingship, whereas His kingship is complete: ﴿To Allah belongs﴾; that is, the One who possesses complete knowledge and all-encompassing power; ﴿whatever is in the heavens﴾. He emphasized this for the same reason as before, saying: ﴿and whatever is on the earth﴾; that is, He is the one who sustains the welfare of all of that, who independently manages all of its affairs, with no one objecting to Him. Rather, both of them and everyone in them manifest their incapacity to manage their own affairs, and they entrust the reins of themselves and their states to Him, willingly or unwillingly. Thus He is the Trustee (wakil) over all of that, acting upon it as a trustee acts, by taking, seizing, and extending. For this same reason He repeated the Greatest Name, saying: ﴿And sufficient is Allah﴾; that is, the One to whom all command belongs, and there is no command for anyone with Him; ﴿as Trustee﴾; that is, sustaining the welfare, dominant, singularly in charge of all affairs, able over all that is within power.

It has become clear, as you see, that the phrase "li-Allah" (to Allah), repeated three times, mentioned with each occurrence a proof for something different from the one before it. It was repeated because a single proof that indicates many signified things is fitting to be cited for each one of them, and repeating it with each one is better than being satisfied with mentioning it once, because when it is repeated, what necessitates knowledge of the signified comes to mind, so the knowledge gained of that signified thing becomes stronger and more exalted. Ending each clause with one of the beautiful attributes alerts the mind that this proof indicates noble secrets and lofty subjects that cannot be enumerated, so the listener strives in reflection to bring out these secrets and to infer the attributes of perfection. This is because the overall aim of this Book is to turn minds and understandings away from occupation with other than Allah (Exalted) toward total absorption in knowing Him, glory be to Him. This repetition serves to achieve and confirm this sought-after goal, and so it is at the utmost of beauty and perfection.

Now that it has been established that the knowledge of the One of this nature is all-encompassing, and that His power is complete, He brings forth His words, threatening, warning, and instilling dread: ﴿If He wills, He can remove you﴾. He makes the address general, indicating the generality of the sending, with His words: ﴿O mankind﴾, i.e., those branching out from that single soul, all of them. This is because of His independence from you and His power over what He wills from you. ﴿And bring others﴾, i.e., from other than you, who will obey Him. ﴿And God is﴾, i.e., the One who has no partner, eternally and everlastingly, ﴿over that﴾, i.e., this great matter of bringing into existence and annihilation, ﴿capable﴾, i.e., of utmost power. This is the ultimate clarification, owing to His independence, His being praiseworthy, dominant, and mighty. If you reflect on the conclusion of His words, may He be exalted, in the story of Jesus, peace be upon him, at the end of this surah: ﴿Glory be to Him that He should have a son﴾ [al-Nisa larger: 171], this adds clarity to this secret, which is that there is no objection to Him.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 134:

When this contained a powerful warning and an acquaintance with the vastness of dominion and the completeness of control, and since the basis of the circumstances of those who quarrel over inheritance and the rights of spouses and other matters was the worldly affair, and since He, glory be to Him and exalted, had explained earlier that the foundation of the circumstances of the hypocrites was based on seeking fleeting worldly gain in particular, such as the story of Ṭu'mah ibn Ubayriq, who was content to be disgraced in obtaining a trifling thing, He, exalted is He, said, belittling their opinions and debasing their aspirations, since they descended to the lowest while having the capacity to seek the highest, and while they also sought the lowest from Him, exalted is He, so that nothing of what they depend upon escapes them, along with securing their own selves:

﴿Whoever desires the reward of this world﴾, because his view is limited to the sensible and present, along with his baseness, like the beasts. ﴿Then with Allah﴾, i.e., let him turn to Allah, for with ﴿Allah﴾, i.e., the One who possesses absolute perfection, is ﴿the reward of this world﴾, the base and perishing, and ﴿the Hereafter﴾, i.e., the precious and enduring; so let him seek them from Him, for He gives whatever He wills to one who desires. As for one whose aspiration is elevated above that, so he turns his heart toward Him and confines his concern to Him, seeking nothing but what endures, glory be to Him and exalted, He gathers both for him, just as one who strives for Allah sincerely, for He gathers for him between the reward and the spoils. How fitting is its harmony with what precedes it! For whoever has complete power and vast dominion is like that.

Since what arises from desire is either speech or action, and action may be inward, He said: ﴿And Allah is ever Hearing﴾, i.e., the One singled out with all attributes of perfection, ﴿Seeing﴾, i.e., of far-reaching hearing for every utterance, even if concealed, whether inward or spoken; ﴿Seeing﴾, i.e., of far-reaching sight for everything among the actions that can be seen, and with knowledge of everything that is seen and not seen, among them and others; so it combines sight and insight. Therefore let the servant watch over Him in speech and action.

When this was among the finest admonitions for the people of Tu'mah, who had rallied around him, He turned to them, seeking their inclination, by the form of faith, and came with the form of command in a manner that encompasses others besides them. He said what is like a conclusion to what had preceded of the command to justice (qist) from the beginning of the surah up to here, in a manner that emphasized and urged it: ﴿O you who believe﴾, that is, who affirm faith with their tongues; ﴿be steadfast in upholding justice﴾, that is, be standing firmly, with eloquent standing, persistent in it, striving in it.

Since the greatest foundations (mabani) of this surah is justice ('adl), He placed it first, saying: ﴿justice﴾. This is unlike what comes in "al-Ma'idah" (The Table), for there the focus is on fulfilling (covenants), which only occurs by considering the one to whom it is fulfilled. ﴿Witnesses﴾, that is, present and vigilant, like an accountant's presence over everything you wish to enter into. ﴿For Allah﴾, that is, for the Face of the One in whose hand is everything, not for anything else. ﴿Even if﴾ that justice was ﴿against yourselves﴾, that is: I will only increase you in honor by it; and if you do not do that, I will compel you to testify against yourselves before all witnesses, and you will be disgraced on a day when the first and the last of all creatures are gathered.

When He mentioned what is most dear to a person, He followed it with what is next to it, and began with those who combine that with awe, saying: ﴿or﴾, that is: or if that justice was against ﴿the parents﴾; and He followed it with what encompasses both them and others, saying: ﴿and the relatives﴾, that is: from among the children and others. Then He gave the reason for that by His saying: ﴿whether he be rich﴾, that is, the one testified for or against; ﴿or poor﴾. You see testimony for a rich man in something false as averting harm from him to others, from the one testified against or someone else, or as preventing a greater corruption than it; or against him with what is not righteous, out of desire to benefit the poor man with what does not harm the rich; and the like. ﴿Or poor﴾, so it seems to you that testimony for him in what is not for his benefit is mercy to him, or against him in what is not due to him for one stronger than him, it quiets a strife. ﴿Then Allah﴾, that is, the Possessor of majesty and honor, ﴿is more worthy of both of them﴾, that is, of both types, rich and poor, of which these two whom the testimony concerns from among you are included. So He is the one hoped for to bring benefit and to repel harm, in ways other than what you assumed. The pronoun here is of istikhdam (a rhetorical device in which one pronoun refers to one sense of a term and another pronoun to a different sense); and if it had returned to the mentioned referent, the pronoun would have been singular, because the one spoken of is a single unspecified person.

(p-433) Since this is so, His saying follows as a consequence: ﴿So do not follow [your own] desire﴾ [al-Nisa’: 135]; that is, do not strain to follow ﴿desire﴾ [al-Nisa’: 135], and do not immerse yourselves in it with the immersion of one who exerts himself in loving it; ﴿lest you deviate﴾ [al-Nisa’: 135]; that is, out of desire to ﴿deviate﴾ [al-Nisa’: 135]; for it has become clear to you that there is no justice in that.

Since the implied sense is: "If you follow it for that reason, or for another, then indeed Allah is ever Competent over you," He joins to it His saying: ﴿And if you distort [your testimony] or refuse [to give it]﴾ [al-Nisa’: 135]; that is, you twist your tongues so as to distort the testimony by some kind of distortion, or you turn your tongues, that is, you speak testimony that is false. Ibn ʿĀmir and Ḥamzah read it with a ḍammah on the lām, from al-wilāyah (ولاية, "administration"), meaning: you render the testimony in a manner of justice; or from al-layy (لَيّ, "twisting"). ﴿Or refuse [to give it]﴾ [al-Nisa’: 135]; that is, refuse to give it, though it is the truth, so you do not render it for any reason whatsoever. ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾ [al-Nisa’: 135]; that is, the One encompassing in knowledge and power; ﴿is ever﴾ [al-Nisa’: 135]; that is, He has always been and still is; ﴿Acquainted with what you do﴾ [al-Nisa’: 135]; that is, of comprehensive knowledge, both inward and outward; so He will recompense you for that according to what you deserve. Therefore beware of Him if you betray, and hope in Him if you fulfil [your trust]. This is after what has passed of His disciplining them, by way of allusion and hint, without an explicit command. How fitting this is for the conclusion of the verse before it, and how strongly the two conclusions harmonize: the conclusion of this one is by way of the attribute of being Acquainted, and that one by way of the two attributes of Hearing and Seeing.

(p-434) Since He commanded justice in this manner, He commanded the thing that moves one to it, which is faith in the Lawgiver, the Messenger, and the Book that makes clear His laws and that clarifies its secrets, the Book with which the story was opened by affirming its truth and explaining its benefit. So He said: ﴿O you who have believed﴾ [al-Nisa’: 136]; that is, who have professed faith. Since He addressed them by the description of faith, He commanded them with what is attained only through it, and He said, detailing it: ﴿Believe in Allah﴾ [al-Nisa’: 136]; that is, because He is worthy of that in Himself, the One who combines all the attributes of perfection in their entirety.

Since faith in Allah is not valid except through faith in the intermediaries, and the nearest of the intermediaries to a human being is the Messenger, He said: ﴿and His Messenger﴾ [al-Nisa’: 136]; that is, because he is the one who conveys from Him, whether he is from the angels or from mankind. ﴿And the Book which He sent down﴾ [al-Nisa’: 136]; that is, sent down in parts, according to what is beneficial, gradually, for strengthening and understanding; ﴿upon His Messenger﴾ [al-Nisa’: 136]; that is, because he is the one who explains your Law and who undertakes what you need of rulings, admonitions, and all that sets you right; this is the Qur’an, which reaches you through the agency of the most noble of creation. ﴿And the Book which He sent down before﴾ [al-Nisa’: 136]; that is, its sending down came into being and has passed. Since its sending down did not extend over all of past time, He explained the intended meaning of His saying ﴿before﴾ [al-Nisa’: 136]: it refers to the Gospel, the Psalms, (p-435) the Torah, and others, because your Messenger conveyed that to you; so faith is not attained except by affirming him in everything he says.

Since the believer addressed here knows that sending down and causing to descend belong only to Allah, the verb is in the passive in the reading of Ibn Kathīr, Abū ʿAmr, and Ibn ʿĀmir, because the agent is known; and the reading of the rest makes the agent explicit.

Since the implied sense is: "Whoever believes in that has indeed been guided, and certainly believes in the angels, the Last Day, and other things, of all that the Book and the Messenger have called to," He joins to it His saying: ﴿And whoever disbelieves﴾ [al-Nisa’: 136]; that is, brings disbelief into being and renews it at any time; ﴿in Allah, His angels, His books﴾ [al-Nisa’: 136]; that is, which He sent down upon His prophets, through His angels or without an intermediary; ﴿and His messengers﴾ [al-Nisa’: 136]; that is, from among the angels and mankind. Thus faith is by ascent, because of the need for it, and disbelief is by descent, because of audacity towards it.

Since faith in the Resurrection, although it is the most evident of things, is among those matters which reason cannot stand on its own to attain, and one reaches it only through the messengers, He mentioned it after them, and said: ﴿and the Last Day﴾ [al-Nisa’: 136]; that is, which His messengers have reported, and which sound reason also judges, though reason cannot independently grasp it before the messengers alert it to it. It is the spirit of existence, its secret, its foundation, and its pillar; in it realities are unveiled, creatures are gathered, the comprehensiveness of knowledge and the completeness of power become manifest, the shade of justice is spread out, and the fruits of grace are gathered. ﴿Then he has certainly strayed﴾ [al-Nisa’: 136]; and for emphasis, because of the multitude of deniers, He said: ﴿a far-reaching straying﴾ [al-Nisa’: 136]; that is, there is no means of returning from it with him.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 137:

Since the one who persists after the descent of this guidance is one who brings unbelief into being and renews it, He (glorified and exalted be He) drew attention to how deeply he has gone astray through His anger at his persistence, informing us that remaining upon unbelief is exceedingly grave, and He depicted it in the ugliest of forms. In this there is the subtlest appeal to turn away from opposition. So He said: ﴿Indeed, those who believed﴾; that is, by what they were prepared for of faith through the original nature (fitrah); ﴿then disbelieved﴾; that is, they committed disbelief, and thereby distorted what Allah had established in their natures; ﴿then believed﴾; that is, truly, or potentially, after the coming of the Messenger, through what He prepared them for by manifesting the proofs and establishing the arguments; ﴿then disbelieved﴾; that is, in that Messenger, or in another messenger, by renewing disbelief or persisting in it; ﴿then increased in disbelief﴾; that is, through their insistence upon disbelief until death; ﴿Allah will not be one to forgive them﴾; that is, He who possesses the attributes of perfection; ﴿nor to guide them to a way﴾; that is, of the ways that lead to the goal, for as long as they remain in this state, since He does not forgive that He be associated with.

Since all the forms of the verse's description apply to hypocrisy, some literally and some figuratively, he said, in answer to one who seems to have asked about their recompense, mocking them: ﴿Give good tidings to the hypocrites that for them is a painful punishment.﴾ He here stated the explicit noun in place of the pronoun, to generalize and to attach the ruling to the attribute.

Then He described them with what shows that they are the ones who conceal their disbelief, by His saying (Exalted is He): ﴿Those who take the disbelievers as allies﴾; i.e., those who openly display disbelief. ﴿As allies﴾; i.e., they seek strength through them, in order to keep away from resembling their attributes, so that the sincere believer is distinguished from the hypocrite. It also clarifies that their intention in aligning with them is only to gain strength through them, for the focus of their affair is on worldly gain. It alerts to the baseness of their affair, and that the one immersed in faith is the highest of people, by His saying: ﴿rather than the believers﴾; i.e., those who are immersed in faith. Then He denounced this intention of theirs by His saying: ﴿Do they seek﴾; i.e., the hypocrites, seeking intensely; ﴿with them﴾; i.e., the disbelievers; ﴿honor﴾. It is as if He said: their seeking honor through them is foolishness of judgment and a remoteness from correctness, for there is no honor at all with them.

When He denounced this seeking, He gave the reason for it by His saying: ﴿Indeed, honor belongs to Allah﴾; i.e., the One for whom there is no equal; ﴿entirely﴾; i.e., while they are enemies of Allah. So only the humbling and the destitution are awaited for them. How beautifully this verse connects to the first verses warning against the People of the Book: ﴿Have you not seen those who were given a portion of the Book?﴾ [an-Nisa 4:44], concluded by His saying: ﴿And sufficient is Allah as a protector, and sufficient is Allah as a helper﴾ [an-Nisa 4:45]!

**Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 140:**

﴿And it has already been revealed to you﴾ (i.e., "they take them as allies" while the situation is that it has already been revealed to you): i.e., O community, both the truthful among you and the hypocrites, ﴿in the Book﴾, i.e., in the surah "al-An'am" (The Cattle), which was revealed in Mecca the Honored, the prohibition against sitting with them, let alone taking them as allies. Do you not fear the might of the One who forbade you from that, that He may strike you with a humiliation from which you will never escape? For they do not part from disbelief in the signs of Allah; and their allegiance is not permitted in any circumstance except upon turning away from disbelief. That is what is meant by His saying: ﴿that﴾, i.e., that He, ﴿when you hear the signs of Allah﴾, i.e., of the One of Majesty and Honor. Since hearing is general, He clarified the intended meaning with His saying: ﴿being disbelieved in and mocked﴾, i.e., the evidences they manifest are concealed by any disbeliever, whether from the Jews or others, ﴿and mocked﴾, i.e., they are sought with intense effort to be made objects of ridicule. ﴿Then do not sit with them﴾, i.e., with those who do this to them, ﴿until they engage﴾ (he expressed beginning the discourse by "engaging" to indicate that their speech is never free of something out of its place, as a symbol of not sitting with them in any state), ﴿in a conversation other than it﴾. This is a prohibition from merely sitting with them; so how much more so from taking them as allies?!

Since the verse of "al-An'am" is Meccan, it was limited to mere turning away and cutting off sitting, because one was not able to object except in the heart. As for this verse, it is Medinan, so change at its revelation by the tongue and by the hand is possible for every Muslim. Thus whoever sits without objection is content. Therefore He gave the reason with His saying: ﴿Indeed you, then﴾, i.e., if you sit with them while they do that, ﴿are like them﴾, i.e., in disbelief, because sitting with one who displays faith yet openly speaks disbelief indicates that his display of what he displays is hypocrisy, and that he is content with what this disbeliever declares; and contentment with disbelief is disbelief. Thus the excellence of the closing of the verse was intensified by gathering both groups in Hell, with His saying, resuming as an answer to the question about what the likeness consists of: ﴿Indeed, Allah﴾, i.e., the One whose knowledge encompasses all and whose power is complete, ﴿will gather﴾. Since the state of the concealed is more important, He placed first His saying: ﴿the hypocrites﴾, i.e., those who show faith and conceal disbelief, and so sit with those whom they hear disbelieving; ﴿and the disbelievers﴾, i.e., those who openly proclaim their disbelief because of their firmness in it; ﴿in Hell﴾, which is the prison of the King, ﴿all together﴾, just as the gathering of disbelief in the assembly has gathered them together, which is an insult to the King of Kingdoms; and the equating of them in disbelief by sitting with them indicates the equating between the sinner and his companion through association, without objection.

Then He (glory be to Him, exalted) described them with that which identifies them, saying: ﴿Those who wait and watch for you﴾; that is, they remain steadfast in their state, waiting for what would vex you to occur. ﴿If there is a victory for you﴾; that is, a manifestation (of success), might, and triumph. He said: ﴿from Allah﴾; that is, the One to whom all greatness belongs. This is a reminder to the believers of what sustains their reliance upon Him and their need for Him. ﴿They say﴾; that is, those who believed outwardly, out of hypocrisy, say to you, O believers: ﴿Were we not with you?﴾; that is, outwardly, in our bodies, through what you hear of our words. ﴿So let us share in your victory.﴾ ﴿And if there is a portion for the disbelievers﴾; that is, those who openly disbelieve. He said ﴿a portion﴾ to belittle their success, and to show that it does not harm what the believers have gained of victory. ﴿They say﴾ to the disbelievers, so that they may include them in their share: ﴿Did we not gain mastery over you﴾; that is, did we not seek to keep watch over you and to safeguard your affection, until we prevailed over all your secrets and took control of them, and mixed with you as blood mixes with the body. It derives from their saying "hāzahu," meaning he guarded him and protected him. ﴿And did we not protect you from the believers﴾; that is, from their domination over you, by means of what we used to deceive them with, and by spreading among them rumours and matters that tempt them, which divert them from many of their aims, so that they would believe us, because we displayed faith and were content with what they disliked, flattering them with what no person would accept.

Since this was a matter that vexed, troubled and pained the people of Allah (glory be to Him, exalted), He made the following consequent statement: ﴿So Allah﴾; that is, with all the attributes of greatness that belong to Him; ﴿will judge between you﴾; that is, O believers, and the disbelievers, both those who conceal and those who openly declare.

Since judgment belongs to both abodes, He clarified that it is in the abode in which no matter remains apparent to anyone other than Him, neither outwardly nor inwardly, and in which all hidden things are made manifest. So He said: ﴿on the Day of Resurrection﴾. Since this may have caused them to despair of the world, He said: ﴿And Allah will never grant﴾; He expressed it with the emphatic particle and with the greatest Name, to show the improbability of the disbelievers prevailing, given their strength and numbers in that time. ﴿To the disbelievers﴾; that is, whether they conceal or openly declare (their disbelief). ﴿Over the believers﴾; that is, all of them. ﴿A way﴾; that is, in any manner, in this world or the next.

This is a rebuke of their opinions and a dismissal of their intellects. It is as if He were saying: "O you who wait and watch for the calamities to befall the beloved ones of Allah, and who wish victory for His enemies, when the proofs have already established that all might belongs to Allah, how misguided you are in your assumption that He would forsake His allies! How hard your livers are!" It also includes, in its generality, that a Muslim is not to be killed for a dhimmi, and that a disbeliever may not seize the property of a Muslim by force.

Then he explained that their condition in their vacillation between the two sides is the condition of the deceiver. How misguided they are, in that they deceive One to whom deception cannot apply, since He knows the hidden things. So He said, giving the reason for their being barred from the way: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites﴾, because they display to everyone who they think they are dealing with ﴿seek to deceive Allah﴾; that is, they act by showing what pleases and concealing what harms, like the conduct of the deceiver toward one who has complete encompassing knowledge of everything, for He, glorified and exalted, draws them on gradually from where they do not perceive. Yet they deceive the believers by showing faith and concealing disbelief. ﴿And He is the One who deceives them﴾, the One who commanded the believers with what He commanded them; so it is as if they were doing this with Him. He is the one who ﴿deceives them﴾ by drawing them on from where they do not know, because He is able to seize them from their place of safety, while they are not able to deceive Him in any way. ﴿And when﴾; that is, while they are deceiving Him, and the situation is that they have already exposed themselves by what revealed their scheme to those who have insight, namely that when ﴿they stand up to the prayer﴾; that is, the obligatory prayer, ﴿they stand lazily﴾ (p-442) sluggish, habitually reluctant and heavy, never free of this, such that everyone who observes them recognizes it, because they see it as toil without benefit. So the motive for abandoning it, which is ease, is stronger than the motive for performing it, which is fear of people. Then he went on answering one who might have asked: why do they do this? So he said: ﴿They show off to the people﴾; that is, they do this only so that people may see them, in order that they may think them believers, and that people may show them, for that reason, what pleases them, by counting them among the believers, since people see them as believers when they pray. ﴿And they remember Allah not, except a little﴾; that is, the One who possesses all attributes of perfection, in prayer and other than it, except a little, where it becomes necessary as a means of deceiving them; they do so while being in the state of...

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 143:

﴿Mudhabdhabeen﴾ (wavering, vacillating); that is, agitated (muḍṭarribīn), just as a light object suspended in the air is agitated. In its true sense, it is that which is pushed (dhabb) away from both sides with great force.

Since what preceded indicates their faith at one time and their disbelief at another, He said: ﴿between that﴾; that is, between faith and disbelief. And since faith points to its people and disbelief likewise, He said: ﴿neither to﴾; that is, they do not find a path of escape ﴿to these﴾; that is, the believers; ﴿nor to these﴾; that is, the disbelievers. And since the implicit meaning is: "because Allah has led them astray," He built upon it His saying: ﴿And whomever Allah leaves astray﴾; that is, (p-443) the One whose power is all-encompassing and whose knowledge is perfect; ﴿you will never find﴾; that is, at all; ﴿for him a way﴾; that is, a path to anything he seeks.

ولَمّا انْقَضى ما أرادَ مِنَ الإنْكارِ عَلى مَنِ ادَّعى الإيمانَ في اتِّخاذِ الكافِرِينَ أوْلِياءَ؛ المُسْتَلْزِمِ لِلنَّهْيِ عَنْ ذَلِكَ الِاتِّخاذِ؛ صَرَّحَ بِهِ مُخاطِبًا لِلْمُؤْمِنِينَ؛ فَقالَ: ﴿يا أيُّها الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا﴾؛ أيْ: أقَرُّوا بِالإيمانِ بِألْسِنَتِهِمْ؛ صِدْقًا أوْ كَذِبًا؛ ﴿لا تَتَّخِذُوا﴾؛ أيْ: تُكَلِّفُوا أنْفُسَكم غَيْرَ ما تَدْعُو إلَيْهِ الفِطْرَةُ (fitrah: the innate, natural disposition) الأُولى السَّلِيمَةُ؛ فَتَأْخُذُوا ﴿الكافِرِينَ﴾؛ أيْ: المُجاهِرِينَ بِالكُفْرِ؛ الغَرِيقِينَ فِيهِ؛ ﴿أوْلِياءَ﴾؛ أيْ: أقْرِباءَ؛ تَفْعَلُونَ مَعَهم مِنَ الوُدِّ والنُّصْرَةِ ما يَفْعَلُ القَرِيبُ مَعَ قَرِيبِهِ.

ولَمّا كانَ الغَرِيقُ في الإيمانِ أعْلى النّاسِ؛ وكانَ تَحْتَ رُتْبَتِهِ رُتَبٌ مُتَكاثِرَةٌ؛ نَبَّهَ عَلى ذَلِكَ؛ وعَلى دَناءَةِ مَقْصِدِهِمْ؛ بِالجارِّ؛ فَقالَ: ﴿مِن دُونِ المُؤْمِنِينَ﴾؛ أيْ: الغَرِيقِينَ في الإيمانِ؛ وهَذا إشارَةٌ إلى أنَّهُ لا يَصِحُّ لِمَن يُوالِيهِمْ دَعْوى الإيمانِ؛ ولِذَلِكَ قالَ مُنْكِرًا: ﴿أتُرِيدُونَ﴾؛ أيْ: بِمُوالاتِهِمْ؛ ﴿أنْ تَجْعَلُوا لِلَّهِ﴾؛ أيْ: الَّذِي لا تُطاقُ سَطْوَتُهُ؛ لِأنَّ لَهُ الكَمالَ كُلَّهُ؛ ﴿عَلَيْكُمْ﴾؛ أيْ: في النِّسْبَةِ إلى النِّفاقِ؛ ﴿سُلْطانًا﴾؛ أيْ: دَلِيلًا واضِحًا عَلى كُفْرِكُمْ؛ بِاتِّباعِكم غَيْرَ سَبِيلِ المُؤْمِنِينَ؛ ﴿مُبِينًا﴾؛ واضِحًا؛ مُسَوِّغًا لِعِقابِكُمْ؛ وخِزْيِكُمْ؛ (p-444) وجَعْلِكم في زُمْرَةِ المُنافِقِينَ.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 145:

When He had forbidden them from the conduct of the hypocrites, He resumed explaining their recompense in His presence, saying: ﴿Indeed, the hypocrites will be in the lowest depth (al-dark) of the Fire﴾; that is, the lowest belly and abode, ﴿below the Fire﴾, because that is the most concealed, most hidden, nearest and lowest part of the Fire. Just as their disbelief is the most concealed and nearest of disbelief, so too it is the most wicked of the levels of the Fire, just as their disbelief is the most wicked kind of disbelief. In this there is also the principle that it is appropriate for the ruler to place the doer of such an act in the abode of the hypocrites, because of his doing a deed like theirs; and whoever imitates a people is one of them. The levels of the Fire are called adrak (levels) because they are successive, following one another downward, just as stairs (al-daraj) ascend one after another upward.

When He had informed that they are in this narrow place, He informed of its permanence for them in a very painful manner, saying: ﴿And you will not find for them a helper﴾; that is, ever. By the prohibition against allying with them and the absence of helping them, He alluded to the conclusion of the first verses warning against the disbelievers: ﴿And sufficient is Allah as Protector, and sufficient is Allah as Helper﴾ [al-Nisa: 45].

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 146:

When it was previously stated that forgiveness is impossible for the disbeliever (whether or not he is a hypocrite), and he followed this with what fits it, until he concluded with what indicates that hypocrisy is the most severe type of disbelief, he made an exception from it, as an indication that others among the disbelievers are even more deserving of this exception, alerting that this emphatic negation applies only to one who (p-445) dies upon that state. However, it was framed in that manner to magnify what he mentioned in its context and to repel from it. So He (Exalted) said: ﴿Except those who repent﴾; that is, they turned back from what they had been upon of hypocrisy, through regret and abandoning it; ﴿and amend﴾; that is, their outward deeds, from the prayer in which they had been showing off, and others, by abandoning hypocrisy; ﴿and hold fast to Allah﴾; that is, they strove that their protection, i.e., their attachment, be to the Supreme King, in not returning to what they had been upon.

Since abandoning hypocrisy, of which showing off is one of the types, is a fundamental and principal matter that is extremely difficult, He said, urging the striving of the soul against it: ﴿and make their religion sincerely for Allah﴾; that is, all of it, ﴿for Allah﴾; that is, the One to whom belongs all perfection, so they did not intend by any of their worship other than His countenance, neither showing off nor otherwise; ﴿then those are﴾; that is, those of elevated rank; ﴿with the believers﴾; that is, those for whom faith has become a firmly established attribute; they will be in Paradise, even if they are punished for their sins, so they will be in the upper tier of the Fire; ﴿and Allah will soon give﴾; that is, He who encompasses everything in power and knowledge; ﴿the believers﴾; that is, by a promise that admits no failure, even if what has befallen them before that has befallen them, and even if their punishment is prolonged, as a refinement for them from sins, by what the word "soon" indicates; ﴿a great reward﴾; that is, by eternal abiding in Paradise, whose bliss never ends and whose dweller is never troubled by any day; thus whoever was with them will share in it, for they are a people with whom their companion never becomes wretched.

(p-446) Since the meaning of the exception (al-istithna') is that He will not punish them, and that they will find an intercessor by His permission, He said, emphasising this by way of inference and rebuking whoever thinks that He will not accept them after they have plunged into destruction: ﴿What would Allah do with your punishment﴾; that is, and He is the One characterised by the attributes of perfection, among which is absolute self-sufficiency; ﴿with your punishment﴾; that is, O people; for He gains no benefit from it, and He does not repel any harm from Himself by it. Since the address is with those who believe, He said: ﴿if you are grateful﴾; that is, for His blessings, the greatest of which is the sending down of the Book that guides to right direction, that rescues from every error, and that clarifies everything the servants need. Your reflection upon its condition led you to knowledge of the One who bestowed it, so you submitted to Him, hastened to obey Him with sincerity in worshipping Him, and were kept far from disobeying Him.

Since gratitude is what moves one to faith, He placed it before faith; and since faith is not accepted without it, He said: ﴿and believe﴾; that is, in Him, with sincere faith, in which the heart agrees with what the tongue professes. Since the meaning of the denial is that He will not punish you but will rather show appreciation for that, He said, conjoining it to what precedes: ﴿And Allah is ever Grateful﴾; that is, the Possessor of majesty and honour, eternally and everlastingly; ﴿All-Appreciative﴾ toward whoever is grateful to Him, by rewarding him for his obedience beyond what he deserves; ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of whoever does anything for Him, however small; no inadvertence, error, or confusion is possible for Him.

When God, glorified and exalted be He, had completed what He intended of condemning the state of those who sit with and immerse themselves in His verses, when those verses are free of such things, and of what follows from describing them and clarifying their intention in that sitting, including the prohibition against imitating their conduct and the recompense for whoever does what they did, up to His concluding with the severest punishment of the hypocrites, and His urging repentance by ending with the two attributes of thankfulness and knowledge, He informed that He dislikes the speech of the disbelievers, those whose company He had condemned while one is engaged in it. Likewise, He dislikes every public utterance of evil, except what He excepted. Whoever undertakes what He does not love has not fulfilled the right of His servanthood. So He said, giving the reason for what preceded, before the opening of the matter of the hypocrites, concerning the command to good greeting: ﴿Allah does not like the public utterance of evil speech﴾. That is, the One specified with the attributes of perfection. "Public utterance" means what becomes apparent and so falls into the category of public speech. "Evil" means what offends and harms. "Speech" means directed at anyone, whoever he may be, for that is not part of thanking God, exalted is He, for His kindness to His servants and His dependents, nor is it in any way part of thanking people, and whoever does not thank people does not thank God. ﴿Except one who has been wronged﴾. That is, one who has been subjected to injustice from some person, whoever he may be. For him it is permissible to speak openly of his grievance, to seek redress, and to invoke (God's curse) against the one who wronged him, even if that displeases the wrongdoer, provided he does not transgress.

Since speech is something that is heard, and since injustice may be hidden, He said, encouraging and warning: ﴿And Allah is ever Hearing﴾. That is, the One who has complete encompassing knowledge hears everything that can be heard, whether public or otherwise. ﴿Knowing﴾. That is, He knows everything that can be known. (p-٤٤٨) So beware of Him, lest He deal with you as one deals with someone who is angry. Although the public complaint of one who has been wronged falls within what Allah loves, on the assumption that the exception is contiguous (istithna' muttasil), nevertheless placing it within the category of evil, even if it is by way of mushakalah (rhetorical correspondence), contains a subtle point: a warning to the discerning against engaging in it, and an urging toward forgiveness. For whoever knows that his act is of a kind to which the name of evil applies, in whatever sense that name is applied, refrains from it, if he is granted success.

The Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on Surah 4, Verse 149:

Since the sources of good, despite their multiplicity, are confined to two categories, conveying benefit, whether openly or secretly, and repelling harm, He (Glorified and Exalted is He) alluded to pardon and concluded with the two attributes of hearing and knowledge. He then explicitly urged pardon and goodness (al-nadb, recommendation), thereby exhorting to it twice: the first time by way of allusion, for people of insight (ulu al-basa'ir); the second time by way of explicit statement, for those who desire commerce, urging toward what is most beloved to Him, Glorified is He, most excellent in His sight, and most aligned with the door of generosity. He said: ﴿If you disclose good﴾, that is, of speech or otherwise, ﴿or conceal it﴾, that is, do it secretly from the outset, or in return for an evil deed done to you. Having mentioned doing good, He followed it with a kind of it that is the best of it, so He said: ﴿or pardon an evil﴾, that is, a deed done against you. Since the implied meaning is: "He knows it, by His attributes of hearing and knowledge, and will reward it with a better good and a greater pardon than your pardon," He made the following statement a consequence: ﴿then indeed﴾ (p-449), that is, you are deserving of pardon, because of your knowledge that ﴿Allah has been﴾, that is, always, from eternity and to eternity, ﴿Pardoning﴾. Since abstaining from punishment is not called pardon unless it comes from one who is able, and since restraining oneself from retaliation when one has power, from one who has left great impacts on hearts, is distant and burdensome upon the soul and severe, He (Exalted is He) said, reminding the servants of their sins against Him and of His power over them: ﴿Competent﴾, that is, reaching the utmost in pardoning whatever He wills to pardon of the offenses of wrongdoers, and in power over whatever He wills, and whomever He wills.
