Therefore, one who is never free of sin and incapacity is more deserving of pardon, hoping for the pardon of the Capable One concerning him, fearing His retaliation against him, and adopting His great character and following His example.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 150:

When that was concluded in the most complete manner and the best arrangement and structure, and [the discourse] ended with the two attributes of pardon and power, he began to explain the states of those among the People of the Book who are not pardoned, and to explain that they are the ones who misled the hypocrites by what they cast to them of doubts (shubah, pl. shubuhat), for which their minds were broadened by the knowledge that He, glorified and exalted, had bestowed upon them. Thus they revealed evil and concealed good, and they placed His favour where He dislikes it. Then He, glorified and exalted, uncovered some of their doubts, and He said, explaining what He had opened with regarding their narratives, that they have bought misguidance in exchange for guidance and desire the misguidance of others, after He had concluded there, before their narratives, with His saying: "Pardoning, Powerful" (p-450): ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve﴾; that is, they conceal what they have of knowledge; ﴿in Allah﴾; that is, the One to whom belongs exclusive majesty and beauty; ﴿and His messengers﴾. When He mentioned the end of their affair, He mentioned the cause that brought it about, so He said: ﴿And they intend to differentiate between Allah﴾; that is, the One to whom belongs the entire command, and there is no command for anyone with Him; ﴿and His messengers﴾; that is, so that they believe in Allah and disbelieve in some of the messengers, thereby denying their messages, which necessarily entails attributing lies to Allah, which requires that Allah, glorified and exalted, be free of them.

When He mentioned the intention, He mentioned what arises from it, so He said: ﴿And they say, "We believe in some"﴾; that is, of Allah and His messengers, like the Jews who believed in Moses, peace be upon him, and others, except for Jesus and Muhammad ﷺ, so they disbelieved in these two; ﴿and we disbelieve in some﴾; that is, of that, namely the messengers, like Muhammad ﷺ; ﴿and they intend to adopt﴾; that is, they strive to take; ﴿between that﴾; that is, between belief and disbelief; ﴿a way﴾; that is, a path by which they disbelieve. The coordination of the clauses with "and" (wa) — although some of them are a cause of others — indicates that they deserve to be described by each of them individually, and that each trait is sufficient for attributing disbelief to them; and He placed its result first (p-451) and concluded with the judgement upon it, in a more emphatic form, to denounce their condition. The original sense of the statement is: "They wanted a way between two ways, so they said: We disbelieve in some, and they intended differentiation, so they disbelieved with a disbelief that is at the extreme of abomination, knowingly." Thus this produced:

﴿Those﴾; i.e., the distant and the hateful; ﴿they are the disbelievers﴾; i.e., those immersed in disbelief; ﴿truly﴾. Disbelief in all of them necessarily follows for them, because the proof (dalil) for the prophethood of some necessarily entails certainty about the prophethood of everyone to whom a similar proof has come. And since it is permitted that a proof occur without what it proves, it becomes impossible to use it as evidence for anything, like a miracle (mu'jizah). Disbelief in all of them then necessarily follows. Thus it is established that whoever denies the prophethood of any one of the prophets, upon them be peace, necessarily disbelieves in all the prophets. Whoever necessarily disbelieves in them necessarily disbelieves in Allah and in all that He brought.

Since the implied sense was: "So, undoubtedly, We have prepared, i.e., readied, for them a humiliating punishment," He conjoined to it, for generalization: ﴿And We have prepared for the disbelievers﴾; i.e., all of them; ﴿a humiliating punishment﴾; i.e., just as they treated some of the messengers with contempt, though they were worthy of love and honor. The verse encompasses them and others whose state is like theirs. Placing this after the account of the hypocrites' conditions is most fitting and best, to identify them as hypocrites, in that they show some of the Prophet's (ﷺ) affair and conceal other than it, even though what they show is contrary to what the hypocrites show; and in that they are the ones who misled the hypocrites; and as a warning against their statements, and an exposure of what they distorted from its places. In this there is a shift of address (iltifat) back to the beginning of this narrative: ﴿O you who believe, believe in Allah and His Messenger﴾ [al-Nisa', 136].

[p-452]

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 152:

When He, glory be to Him and exalted, had explained what He had prepared for them, He explained what He had prepared for their opposites among the people of His obedience, by His saying: ﴿And those who believe in Allah﴾; that is, the One who possesses perfection and beauty; ﴿and His messengers﴾. And when they were gathered together in faith, in contrast to what the people of disbelief did, He stated explicitly what this had implied, saying: ﴿and do not make distinction﴾; that is, in their belief; ﴿between any of them﴾; that is, they did not make any one of them into a state of extreme separation from another, by disbelieving in some and believing in others, as the wretched ones did. Making a distinction requires two things or more. And "aḥad" (any one) is general in reference to the singular, the masculine and the feminine, and their dual and plural forms. Therefore its use is valid in the sense of "between two" or "between a group." It seems it was chosen for emphasis, in that if a single person could be subject to distinction, then believing in some and not others would be disbelief. ﴿Those⦆; that is, the high-ranking; in the ranks of happiness.

And since the purpose is to affirm their promise, and what is generally observed in it is delay, He said: ﴿He will soon give them﴾; that is, by what We possess of greatness; with a promise that admits no failure, even if it is delayed. The aim is to affirm its realization, not to affirm its delay. Yet He used the particle that has more letters and is more expansive in its extension, because this context is for those who have pure, comprehensive faith, including those who have no deeds. For this reason He attributed the rewards to them and concluded with forgiveness, lest despair arise in them, however long the term may be. ﴿Their rewards⦆; that is, complete in accordance with their intentions and their deeds.

And since man is a locus of deficiency, He said: ﴿And Allah is⦆; that is, the One whom describers cannot reach the full reality of His attributes of perfection; ﴿Forgiving⦆ of the lapses He wills; ﴿Merciful⦆; that is, toward whomever He wills to make happy with the gardens.

Al-Biqa'i, *Nazm al-Durar*, on Surah 4, verse 153:

When (Allah, exalted is He) had informed them of what awaits those who make distinctions between Allah and His messengers, and what awaits their opponents, He followed it with some of what they intended by that division. The reason is that Ka'b ibn al-Ashraf and Finhas ibn Azura, from among the Jews, said falsely: "If you are a prophet, then bring us a Book all at once from heaven, which we may witness as it descends, just as Musa (upon him be prayers and peace) brought his Book in that manner." So Allah (exalted is He) revealed this, rebuking them for this lie, pointing to their falsehood in it, undermining their demand, warning against its dangers, and making clear their disbelief in Allah and His messengers: ﴿They ask you﴾. Since this was one of the greatest doubts by which they misled those whom Allah willed (to be misled), because they saw that this clear Book was the greatest of miracles, and that the Arabs could not level a criticism against it in a way that could be accepted, they directed their schemes toward it (p. 454) with this doubt and others like it. Allah, glorified and exalted, exposed it with the most complete exposure and disgraced them through it to the utmost degree of disgrace. He increased their rebuke by saying: ﴿O People of the Book﴾, indicating that the scholar ought to be the farthest of people from deception, let alone from outright lying. ﴿That you bring down upon them﴾, meaning specifically for them, by naming them, ﴿a Book from heaven﴾. And what they implied in this statement, that Musa (upon him be prayers and peace) brought the Torah all at once, is a lie. It was a falsehood that those among the people of Islam whom Allah willed accepted from them, thinking that Allah, blessed and exalted, had confirmed them in it. This is not so, as the whole context indicates, and what is nearly explicit in this regard comes in His saying: ﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you﴾ [al-Nisa': 163], the verse, as its explanation will come. The Jews today acknowledge that it did not descend all at once. Al-Kalbi said, concerning the story of the cow that they slaughtered because of the slain man over whom they disputed: "That was before the revelation of the *qasama* (the oath procedure) in the Torah."

Since this was something that the Prophet ﷺ found greatly troubling, He alluded to it, making clear, as a consolation to him (ﷺ), that their habit is obstinacy, their custom is disbelief, and that they are the most deeply immersed of people in hardness of heart and coarseness of nature. Their predecessors were obstinate toward those whom they now claim to believe in, and they (the Jews) are following his (Musa's) law, and the most beloved thing in it is what He showed them of those great signs, among them their deliverance from bondage and even from slaughter. This obstinacy was repeated from them despite what they witnessed of calamities and of pardon. So He said: ﴿Then they had asked﴾, meaning: if you find this momentous, then indeed ﴿they asked﴾, meaning their forefathers, meaning that they were on the same path of obstinacy, so they are partners in it, ﴿Musa﴾, without any justification other than obstinacy, ﴿a greater (thing)﴾, meaning more grave, ﴿than that﴾, meaning the great matter with which they confronted you, after I had shown you miracles that obligated everyone who knew of them to believe in you and to show you courtesy. Then He specified it by His saying: ﴿They said, "Show us Allah"﴾, meaning the Sovereign Most High, who has no likeness, and whose greatness the intellects fall short of encompassing, ﴿openly﴾, meaning face to face, without any veil, without any screen, and without any kind of concealment, but rather our eyes would encompass Him just as hearing encompasses a clearly spoken word. This shows that each of the two requests is forbidden, because it is an injustice, since it leads to belittling the miracles We bring and regarding them as insufficient. Moreover, the sending down of the Book all at once is not suited to the wisdom upon which this world was built, namely linking effects to causes and being founded upon that. It is known that dividing the commands is a cause of lightening their burden, and that this is more conducive to obeying them, easier for memorizing them, more helpful for understanding them, greater in firming up the one to whom it is revealed, more soothing to his heart, stronger for his heart, and more stimulating to his longing. And seeing Him in the manner they requested, which is encompassing Him, is impossible. Therefore their request for it is belittling, and it is also obstinacy. For this reason He made the reason for their request the statement: ﴿Then the thunderbolt seized them﴾, meaning immediately after this request, and because of it, without any delay, a seizing of subjugation and overpowering, ﴿the thunderbolt﴾, meaning a fire that descended from (p. 456) heaven with a mighty sound, deserving that nothing else be called a *sa'iqah* (thunderbolt) when it is attributed to it, ﴿and it destroyed them﴾, ﴿for their wrongdoing﴾, meaning because of their wrongdoing in this request and other things, since it was obstinacy without any justification at all, and because of their demand to see Him in an impossible manner, namely demanding to encompass Him. ﴿Then﴾, after pardoning them and reviving them from the death caused by this thunderbolt, ﴿they took the calf﴾, meaning they undertook to take it and exceeded all bounds in fashioning it.

Since the one who has gone astray after the clearest explanation is more deserving of rebuke, He said: ﴿after﴾, and He introduced the preposition to indicate that their taking of the calf did not last for the whole period of their absence, but rather they repented of it. ﴿After the clear proofs had come to them﴾, meaning through this revival and other miracles. ﴿Then We pardoned﴾, meaning with the greatness that belongs to Us, ﴿that﴾, meaning the great sin, by accepting their repentance, without uprooting them. ﴿And We gave﴾, meaning by Our greatness, which nothing approaches, ﴿Musa authority﴾, meaning dominion and overpowering dominance, ﴿clear﴾, meaning manifest. For he commanded them to kill themselves, and they hastened to comply after they had committed this great error. In this there is a clear hint that He, glorified and exalted, empowers Muhammad ﷺ over everyone who opposes him, with an authority greater than this.

(p-457) When he had explained this aspect of His greatness, He followed it with another matter, greater than it, saying: ﴿And We raised﴾, i.e., by Our majesty. Since the mountain had filled the upper side by overshadowing all their bodies, and none of them was spared from this, He dropped the preposition and said: ﴿above them the Tur﴾, i.e., the great mountain. Then He mentioned the cause of its raising, saying: ﴿because of their covenant﴾ (p-457), i.e., until they bound themselves to it, submitted to it, and accepted it.

When He had mentioned the covenant in this wondrous manner, He followed it with what they broke in it, despite its ease, as evidence of the badness of their natures, saying: ﴿And We said to them﴾, i.e., through what they had repeatedly witnessed of Our greatness: ﴿Enter the gate﴾, i.e., the gate of Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem): ﴿prostrating﴾, i.e., so they broke that firm covenant and changed it. ﴿And We said to them﴾, i.e., through the tongue of Musa, upon him be peace, in many places of the Tawrah (the Torah): ﴿Do not transgress﴾, i.e., do not exceed what We have set for you: ﴿in the Sabbath﴾, i.e., do not do any work in it, and this is a designation of the thing by the name of its cause. It was called "transgression" (ʿadw) because one who is absorbed in something, through the intensity of his attention to it, is as if he runs toward it (yaʿdu). ﴿And We took from them﴾, i.e., concerning all of that: ﴿a binding covenant﴾. I have definitively concluded that what is meant by this, and Allah (Exalted) knows best, is through the tongue of Musa, upon him be peace, because He (Exalted) repeatedly stressed to them in the Tawrah the observance of the Sabbath, enjoined it upon them, and bound them to it with a covenant that is rarely imposed concerning any other of the branch rulings. Some translators of the Tawrah said, in the second book (al-Sifr al-Thani, Exodus), in the passage of the ten commandments whose beginning is: (I am the LORD thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage. Thou shalt have no other gods before me), what (p-458) its text is: (Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy. Six days shalt thou labour, and do all thy work; but the seventh day is the sabbath of the LORD thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy manservant, nor thy maidservant, nor thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates: for in six days the LORD made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that in them is, and rested the seventh day: wherefore the LORD blessed the sabbath day, and hallowed it. Honour thy father), to the end of what passed in Surat al-Baqarah. Then he repeated the ten commandments at the beginning of the fifth book (Deuteronomy), and said concerning the Sabbath: (Keep the sabbath day to sanctify it, as the LORD thy God hath commanded thee. Six days thou shalt labour, and do all thy work; but the seventh day is the sabbath of the LORD thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, nor thy manservant, nor thy maidservant, nor thy ox, nor thy ass, nor any of thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates; that thy manservant and thy maidservant may rest as well as thou), to the end of what is at the beginning of this surah, at His words: ﴿and guide you to the ways of those before you﴾ [al-Nisa' 4:26]. He said in the second book after that: (And the LORD spoke unto Moses, saying: Speak thou also unto the children of Israel, saying: Verily my sabbaths ye shall keep; for it is a sign between me and you throughout your generations; that ye may know that I am the LORD that doth sanctify you. Ye shall keep the sabbath therefore; for it is holy unto you: every one that defileth it shall surely be put to death; for whosoever doeth any work therein, that soul shall be cut off from among his people. Six days may work be done; but in the seventh is the sabbath of rest, holy to the LORD: whosoever doeth any work in the sabbath day, he shall surely be put to death. Wherefore the children of Israel shall keep the sabbath, to observe the sabbath throughout their generations, for a perpetual covenant. It is a sign between me and the children of Israel for ever: for in six days the LORD made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day he rested, and was refreshed), and when His speech to him on Mount Sinai was finished, He gave Musa, upon him be peace, the two tablets of testimony. He also emphasized its observance upon them in other places, to the extent that He legislated for them the agricultural rules and the like. He said in the second book as well: (Six years thou shalt sow thy land, and shalt gather in the fruits thereof: but the seventh year thou shalt let it rest and lie still; that the poor of thy people may eat: and what they leave the beasts of the field shall eat. In like manner thou shalt deal with thy vineyard, and with thy oliveyard. Six days thou shalt do thy work, and on the seventh day thou shalt rest: that thine ox and thine ass may rest, and the son of thy handmaid, and the stranger, may be refreshed), then He mentioned the festivals in the third book and forbade work in them. He said, concerning some of them: (For whatsoever soul it be that doeth any work in that same day, the same soul will I destroy from among his people. Ye shall do no manner of work: it shall be a statute for ever throughout your generations in all your dwellings. It is the sabbath of rest unto you), then He commanded the Feast of Booths for seven days, and said: (That your generations may know that I made the children of Israel to dwell in booths, when I brought them out of the land of Egypt) (p-460). Then He mentioned some of the offerings and said: (And Aaron shall order the shewbread before the LORD continually… on the sabbath day he shall set it in order before the LORD continually). He also said: (And the LORD spoke unto Moses in mount Sinai, saying: Speak unto the children of Israel, and say unto them: When ye come into the land which I give you, then shall the land keep a sabbath unto the LORD. Six years thou shalt sow thy field, and six years thou shalt prune thy vineyard, and gather in the fruit thereof; but in the seventh year shall be a sabbath of rest unto the land, a sabbath for the LORD: thou shalt neither sow thy field, nor prune thy vineyard. That which groweth of its own accord of thy harvest thou shalt not reap, neither gather the grapes of thy vine undressed: for it is a year of rest unto the land. And the sabbath of the land shall be meat for you; for thee, and for thy servant, and for thy maid, and for thy hired servant, and for thy stranger that sojourneth with thee. Thou shalt number seven sabbaths of years unto thee, seven times seven years; and the space of the seven sabbaths of years shall be unto thee forty and nine years. Then shalt thou cause the trumpet of the jubilee to sound… and ye shall hallow the fiftieth year, and proclaim liberty throughout all the land unto all the inhabitants thereof: it shall be a jubilee unto you; and ye shall return every man unto his possession… And ye shall not sow, neither reap that which groweth of itself in it, nor gather the grapes in it of thy vine undressed. For it is the jubilee; it shall be holy unto you… And the land shall not be sold for ever: for the land is mine), and so on.

Among what it contains, and what may not be applied to our Law, is the attribution of resting (istirahah) to Him, glorified is He. This is despite the fact that He, glorified is He, stressed the covenants upon them concerning monotheism and the observance of the rulings throughout the whole Tawrah, in the manner you see in what I have quoted from it in this book.

When Allah, glory be to Him, made clear that He had confirmed the covenant upon them and had repeatedly stressed the duty of keeping the pact, He then showed that they broke it. As a consequence, He brought upon them what had been threatened to them in the Torah: disgrace and the striking of humiliation, together with what He has stored up for them in the Hereafter. So He said: ﴿So because of﴾, emphasising with the addition of "mā" (the emphatic particle), ﴿their breaking of their covenant﴾. That is: We did to them, because of this, all that We mentioned in the Torah of disgrace. Much of it has already been mentioned in the Qur'an. In my view, it is not far-fetched to connect this with His words that follow: ﴿We forbade them good things﴾ and ﴿We have prepared﴾. The "good things" here may include honour and comfortable living, and this combines the hardship of both abodes.

Then He joined to this general matter (of breaking the covenant) something that received particular emphasis by singling it out, as a specific item after a general one. He said: ﴿and their disbelief in the signs of Allah﴾, namely what came to them through the tongue of Muhammad (ﷺ). The wisdom of Allah, glory be to Him, required that its greatness be proportionate to the greatness of His Greatest Name (al-ism al-a'ẓam), which is the designation of all the names. Their disbelief in it therefore entailed their disbelief in what was sent down to Musa, upon him be prayer and peace, because this is the greatest thing they broke, and it is more specific than breaking the covenant in general. ﴿And their killing of the prophets﴾, which is greater than their disbelief in general, because that closes the door of faith to them and to others, since the prophets are the cause of faith, and when the cause is erased, the effect is erased too.

Since the prophets are protected from every defect and free from every base quality, and no right is owed by them that they fail to fulfil, He said: ﴿without right﴾, meaning, whether great or small, at all. This phrase, because it occurs in the context of their attack on the Qur'an, which is the greatest of the signs, is expressed more forcefully here than in Al 'Imran, which was itself more forceful than what preceded it. This is because here, together with the plural of abundance and the indefiniteness of "right", He used the verbal noun, which conveys that audacity in killing had become a habit for them and a firmly established quality. This differs from what came before, where the present tense was used, which may indicate something occasional.

Then He mentioned something greater than all of that: their attributing their great sins to Allah (exalted). He said: ﴿and their saying: "Our hearts are wrapped"﴾, meaning: we are not to blame, because our hearts were created from the outset distant from understanding the like of what the prophets say, being enclosed in coverings, so they are very hard. This, they claimed, is the cause of their killing of the prophets and their rejection of what they said. This was after they had acknowledged this noble Prophet, testified to his messengership, that he is the seal of the prophets, described him by his most famous attributes, and awaited his coming. So, undoubtedly, Allah answered them with His words, linked to what is implied as: "They have lied, because they were born upon the natural disposition (fiṭrah), like all children, so their hearts were not originally wrapped": ﴿Rather, Allah has sealed over them﴾, meaning, He who holds the reins of might and the sources of greatness, ﴿upon them﴾, a sealing that is acquired, ﴿because of their disbelief﴾. Indeed, He had first created their hearts upon the natural disposition, able to choose good and evil. When they turned away from good, through what He had prepared their hearts for, namely accepting the breaking (of the covenant), and chose evil, by following their desires that arise from their souls and abandoning what their intellects call them to, Allah, glory be to Him and exalted, sealed over them, making their hearts hard and veiled from His mercy. For this reason He made His words consequent: ﴿so they do not believe﴾, meaning they do not renew faith at any time to come.

It is also possible that this is connected to something implied as a continuation of their statement: "Allah has sealed over them, so they do not understand", and that "Rather" is a correction to the sealing being caused by disbelief alone, because disbelief may be accompanied by other things. It is also possible that "Rather" turns away from their saying that their hearts are in wrappings, because what is in a wrapping may be prepared to be taken out of the wrapping into a sealing, which by nature is lasting. ﴿Except a few﴾ of them, who believe, briefly, like the brightness of the day, and disbelieve at other times, believe in some things and disbelieve in others, or except a few of them, as their forefathers used to believe in the signs that came through Musa, upon him be prayer and peace. Yet they were not slow to disbelieve and to be obstinate, demanding another sign, as is mentioned in their Torah that is among them. I have quoted much of it in this book. Thus the proof was established against them, for they distinguish between their ability to believe and their ability to fly.

When he had explained their disbelief in killing the prophets, he explained their disbelief in the slander that was the cause of the killing—and temptation (fitnah) is greater than killing. So he said, glorifying it by repeating the verb: ﴿And for their disbelief﴾; that is, the absolute disbelief, which is the cause of their boldness in disbelieving in a specific prophet, such as Musa—upon him be prayer and peace—and in the slander; so that some of their disbelief is conjoined to some other. Therefore he said: ﴿and for their saying against Maryam﴾; that is, after their knowledge of what appeared at her hands of miracles (karamat) indicating her innocence, and that she was constant in worship through various kinds of obedience; ﴿a tremendous slander﴾;

Then He taught them about what they did not attain, namely the killing of the greatest of the prophets who came to them, with the greatest of the signs they had seen after Musa; he is Isa, upon both of them be prayer and peace. Then (they taught about) their claim to have killed him and crucified him, boasting about it, while they doubted regarding it. So He said: ﴿And their saying, "Indeed, we killed the Messiah"﴾. Then He clarified it by His saying: ﴿Isa, son of Maryam﴾. Then they mocked him by their saying ﴿the Messenger of Allah﴾ (p-465), that is, the one to whom belongs the highest greatness. So they combined among several kinds of ugly deeds. Among them is the claim to a status they were not given. Among them is that he, even if their claim were true, would be combining the greatest of the major sins absolutely, which is disbelief through killing a prophet because he is a prophet; and after it the greatest of the major sins, which is killing in general. That did not suffice them, until they described him with prophethood attached to the Greatest Name, mocking him and the One who sent him, Mighty is His name, exalted is His majesty, supreme is His pride, complete are His words, and effective are His commands, because He did not prevent him from them, according to their assumption. ﴿And they did not﴾, that is, while the state of affairs was that they ﴿did not kill him, nor did they crucify him﴾, even though many of them said so; and the Christians handed him over to them. ﴿But﴾, since the intended purpose was that confusion fell upon them, harmful to them, and not because he was from a specific person, He said: ﴿it was made to appear so to them﴾, that is, in their resolve to do this they were claiming a status they were not given.

Since the resemblance made difference of opinion understood, the implied sense is: "They differed, because of the resemblance, about his killing: some of them said, 'We killed him,' decisively; some said, 'He is not the one killed'; and some said, 'The apparent (truth) is that he is.'" He followed this with His saying, indicating their doubt through their disagreement: ﴿And indeed, those who differ concerning it﴾, that is, concerning his killing, ﴿are in doubt about it﴾, that is, in a hesitation whose two sides are equal, all of them, even if some of them were decisive. Then He emphasized this meaning by His saying: ﴿They have no knowledge of it﴾, and He went deep into negation by His saying: ﴿no knowledge﴾ (p-466). Since they used to burden themselves with believing this by looking at its evidence, a doubt might grow strong among them, becoming a sign that obliged them, due to their eagerness for its hopes, to hold a conjecture; then it dissolved immediately, because it had no reality, so doubt returned, and it was more profound in bewilderment. He said: ﴿except﴾, that is, but ﴿following conjecture﴾, that is, they burden themselves with climbing from the level of doubt to the rank of conjecture. He expressed it with the particle of exception rather than "but" (lakin), which is set for contrast, indicating that their grasp of what they claimed of his killing, while in reality it was doubt, they burden themselves to make it conjecture, then they decide upon it, then it became among them a mutawatir, decisive matter; so none is more ignorant than them.

Since He had informed of their doubt about it after informing of its negation, He repeated that in a more emphatic manner, so He said: ﴿And they did not kill him﴾, that is, their killing of him was negated with certainty; ﴿certainly﴾, that is, its negation was by way of certainty. It may also be a circumstantial clause (hal) from "killed him", meaning: they did not commit the killing while certain that he was Isa, upon him be prayer and peace; rather they committed it while doubting about him. The truth is that they did not kill except the man upon whom his likeness was cast. The first aspect is more preferable, due to His saying:

(p. 467) **"Rather, Allah raised him"** (﴿بَلْ رَفَعَهُ اللَّهُ﴾), by His immense majesty and dazzling wisdom. He raised Jesus, peace be upon him, **"to Himself"** (﴿إلَيْهِ﴾), meaning to a place that no human authority can reach. It is related from Wahb that he was sent with revelation at thirty, and was raised at thirty-three, so his mission lasted three years. **"And Allah is"** (﴿وكانَ اللَّهُ﴾), meaning the One who possesses all attributes of perfection in every state, when they intend Him and before and after that, **"Mighty"** (﴿عَزِيزًا﴾), meaning He overcomes and is not overcome, **"Wise"** (﴿حَكِيمًا﴾), meaning when He does something He perfects it, so that no one hopes to undo any part of it. The ending of the verse with these two attributes indicates that what is meant is the mockery they had established, and that He intended to refute them. That is, He has done what prevents your mockery: He raised him to Himself by His might and preserved him by His wisdom, and He will soon send him down by the full power of His ability, so he will turn you back from your desires, shed your blood, and destroy your multitude. In his raising and in placing the confusion upon you, He has a wisdom too subtle for the thoughts of the likes of you.

The story of his raising, peace be upon him, is from the Injil (the Gospel) that exists today among the Christians. It contains a warning about the Dajjal (the Antichrist), an announcement of his descent upon the earth, and good tidings of our Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ), whom it describes as "al-Faraqlit" (the Paraclete) and "al-Arkun." Their report of his killing and crucifixion is based on nothing but doubt, as Allah (Exalted) said, and the best refutation of a person is by what he himself believes. Their translator in the Gospel of Matthew said: He, peace be upon him, entered the Temple in Yerushalayim, which is al-Quds (Jerusalem), and exchanges took place between him and the rabbis, the last of which was that he said to them: "I say to you, you will not see me now until you say: Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord." Then he went out of the Temple, and his disciples came to him to show him the building of the Temple. He answered and said to them: "See all this? Truly I say to you, not one stone will be left here upon another that will not be thrown down." Then he sat on the Mount of Olives, and Mark said: in front of the Temple. His disciples came to him saying: "Tell us, when will this be? And what is the sign of your coming and the end of the age?" He said to them: "Watch that no one leads you astray." Mark and Luke said: "For many will come in my name saying, 'It is the Messiah,' and they will lead many astray." "When you hear of wars and reports of wars, watch that you are not alarmed, for all this must happen. Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom, and there will be great fear, turmoil, hunger, and plague." Luke said: "and great signs from heaven," "and earthquakes in places, and all this is the beginning of the birth pangs." Mark said: "and this is the beginning of the labor pains. Watch yourselves, for they will hand you over to the councils and the assemblies, and you will be beaten." Luke said: "Before all this they will lay their hands on you, and they will drive you to the assemblies and the prisons, and you will be brought before kings and governors as a witness against them and against all the nations. The gospel must first be preached, so when they bring you and hand you over, do not worry about what you will say or how you will answer, for you will be given at that hour what you should say, and it will not be you who speak, but the Holy Spirit." Luke said: "For I will give you a mouth and wisdom that those who oppose you will not be able to resist or answer." "Brother will hand over brother to death, and the father his son, and children will rise against their parents." Matthew said: "Then they will hand you over to affliction and kill you, and you will be hated by all nations. Then many will fall away, and some will betray others, and some will hate others. Many false prophets will arise and lead many astray, and because of the increase of lawlessness, the love of many will grow cold. But whoever endures to the end will be saved. This good news of the kingdom will be preached in all the inhabited world, as a testimony to all nations." Mark said: "When you see the abomination of desolation spoken of by the prophet Daniel standing where it should not be (let the reader understand), then those in Judea must flee to the mountains. Whoever is on the housetop must not come down to take anything from his house, and woe to pregnant women and nursing mothers in those days." Luke said: "Then those in Judea must flee to the mountains, and those in the midst of the city must leave, and those in the countryside must not enter it, for these are days of vengeance, that all that is written may be fulfilled. There will be great distress upon the earth and wrath upon this people, and they will fall by the edge of the sword and be taken captive among all nations, and Jerusalem will be trampled by the nations until the times of the Gentiles are fulfilled. There will be signs in the sun, the moon, and the stars, and people's souls will faint from fear." Matthew said: "Then the end will come." Then he said: "There will be great tribulation," Mark said: "those days," "such as has not been from the beginning of the world until now, nor will be. And if those days had not been shortened, no flesh would be saved." Mark said: "If the Lord had not shortened those days, no flesh would live, but for the sake of the elect those days have been shortened. If anyone says to you, 'Here is the Messiah,' do not believe it. False messiahs and false prophets will arise and give great signs and wonders, and they will lead astray the chosen if they can. Behold, I have told you beforehand. If they say to you, 'He is in the wilderness,' do not go out; or 'in the inner rooms,' do not believe it. For as lightning comes from the east and shines to the west, so will the coming of the Son of Man be. For wherever the corpse is, there the vultures will gather." "After the tribulation of those days, the sun will be darkened, the moon will not give its light, the stars will fall from the sky, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken. Then the sign of the Son of Man will appear in the sky, and all the tribes of the earth will mourn, and they will see the Son of Man coming on the clouds of the sky with power and great glory. He will send the angels with a great trumpet sound, and they will gather his elect from the four winds, from the farthest heavens," Mark said: "from the ends of the earth to the ends of heaven." "From the fig tree," Luke said: "and from all the trees, learn the parable: when its branches become tender and its leaves sprout, you know that summer is near. So also, when you see all this, know that it is near, at the doors. Truly I say to you, this generation will not pass away until all this takes place. Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away. But concerning that day and hour, no one knows, not even the angels of heaven," Mark said: "nor the Son," "but the Father alone." Luke said: "The Pharisees asked him, 'When will the kingdom of God come?' He said, 'The kingdom of God does not come with observation, nor will they say, Look, here it is, or there it is! Behold, the kingdom of God is in the midst of you.' Then he said to his disciples: 'The days will come when you will long to see one of the days of the Son of Man, and you will not see it. If they say to you, Look, here it is! or there it is! do not go or follow them. For as the lightning flashes and lights up the sky from one side to the other, so will the Son of Man be in his day.'" (End.)

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 158 (part 2 of 5):

"And as it was in the days of Noah, peace be upon him, so will be the revealing (istilā') of the Son of Man. For just as they were before the days of the Flood, eating, drinking and marrying, until the day Noah entered the ark, and they did not know until the Flood came and swept them all away, so will be the coming (ḥuḍūr) of the Son of Man. Luke said: 'And as it was in the days of Lot, they were eating, drinking, buying, selling, planting and building, until the day Lot went out from Sodom, and fire and brimstone rained from heaven and destroyed them all. So will it be on the day the Son of Man is revealed. On that day, whoever is on the housetop with his goods in the house, let him not come down to take them; and likewise whoever is in the field, let him not turn back. Remember Lot's wife. Whoever seeks to save his life will lose it, and whoever loses it will preserve it. I tell you, on that night'—Matthew said: 'Then'—'two will be in the field; one will be taken and the other left; two women will be grinding at one mill; one will be taken and the other left'" (p-٤٧٣) "the other." Mark said: "Watch, then, and pray, for you do not know when the time will come. Keep watch, for you do not know when the master of the house will come, at evening, at midnight, or at cockcrow, or in the morning; lest he come suddenly and find you asleep. What I say to you I say to all: Keep watch." Luke said: "At all times," "and pray that you may be strong enough to escape all these things that are about to happen, and to stand before the Son of Man." Matthew said: "Watch, therefore, for you do not know on what hour your Lord will come. But know this: if the master of the house had known in what watch the thief would come, he would have watched and not allowed his house to be broken into. Therefore you also must be ready, for the Son of Man will come at an hour you do not expect. Who then is the faithful and wise servant whom his master has set over his household to give them their food at the proper time? Blessed is that servant whom his master finds so doing when he comes. Truly, I tell you, he will set him over all his possessions. But if that wicked servant says in his heart, 'My master is delayed,' and begins to beat his fellow servants and eat and drink with drunkards, the master of that servant will come on a day he does not expect and at an hour he does not know, and will cut him in pieces and assign him his portion with the hypocrites. There will be weeping and gnashing of teeth." The kingdom of heaven is likened to ten virgins who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom. Five of them were foolish, and five were wise. The foolish ones took their lamps but took no oil with them, while the wise took oil in their vessels along with their lamps. As the bridegroom was delayed, they all became drowsy and slept. But at midnight there was a cry: "Behold, the bridegroom! Come out to meet him!" Then all those virgins rose and trimmed their lamps. The foolish said to the wise, "Give us some of your oil, for our lamps are going out." But the wise replied, "No, there will not be enough for us and for you; go rather to the dealers and buy for yourselves." And while they went to buy, the bridegroom came, and those who were ready went in with him to the wedding feast, and the door was shut. Afterward the other virgins came too, saying, "Lord, Lord, open to us!" But he answered, "Truly, I tell you, I do not know you." Therefore keep watch, for you know neither the day nor the hour. For it is like a man going on a journey, who called his servants and entrusted to them his property. To one he gave five talents, to another two, to another one, each according to his ability. Then he went away. He who had received the five talents traded with them and made five more talents. So also he who had the two made two more. But he who had received the one went and dug in the ground and hid his master's money. After a long time the master of those servants came and settled accounts with them. He who had received the five talents came forward, bringing five more talents, saying, "Master, you delivered to me five talents; here I have made five more talents." His master said to him—Luke said—"Well done, good servant; you have been faithful over a little." Matthew said: "Yes, good and faithful servant; you have been faithful over a little; I will set you over much. Enter into the joy of your master." And the one who had received the two talents also came and said, "Master, you delivered to me two talents; here I have made two more talents." His master said to him, "Yes, good and faithful servant; you have been faithful over a little; I will set you over much. Enter into the joy of your master." Then the one who had received the one talent came and said, "Master, I knew you to be a hard man, reaping where you did not sow and gathering where you did not scatter; so I was afraid, and I went and hid your talent in the ground. Here is what is yours." But his master answered him, "You wicked and slothful servant! You knew that I reap where I did not sow and gather where I did not scatter. You ought then to have put my money in the bank, and at my coming I would have received what was mine with interest. Take the talent from him and give it to him who has the ten talents. For to everyone who has will more be given, and he will have abundance; but from him who has not, even what he has will be taken away. And cast the worthless servant into the outer darkness; there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth." When the Son of Man comes in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then he will sit on his glorious throne. Before him will be gathered all the nations, and he will separate them one from another as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats, and he will place the sheep on his right and the goats on his left. Then the King will say to those on his right, "Come, you who are blessed by my Father; inherit the kingdom prepared for you from the foundation of the world. For I was hungry and you gave me food, I was thirsty and you gave me drink, I was a stranger and you welcomed me, I was naked and you clothed me, I was sick and you visited me, I was in prison and you came to me." Then the righteous will answer him, saying, "Lord, when did we see you hungry and feed you, or thirsty and give you drink? And when did we see you a stranger and welcome you, or naked and clothe you? And when did we see you sick or in prison and visit you?" And the King will answer them, "Truly, I tell you, as you did it to one of the least of these my brothers, you did it to me." Then he will say to those on his left, "Depart from me, you cursed, into the eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels. For I was hungry and you gave me no food..." to the end of it. These will go away into eternal punishment, but the righteous into eternal life.

When Jesus had finished all these sayings, he said to his disciples: "You know that after two days the Passover is coming"—Mark said: "The Passover and the Unleavened Bread were after two days"—"and the chief priests, the scribes and the elders of the people gathered in the palace of the high priest, who was called Caiaphas, and they plotted together to seize Jesus by stealth and kill him." Mark said: "by deceit," and they said, "Not during the feast, lest there be an uproar among the people." Mark said: "a disturbance among the people." John said: "So the chief priests and the Pharisees gathered a council and said, 'What are we to do? For this man performs many signs. If we let him go on like this, everyone will believe in him, and the Romans will come and take away both our place and our nation.' But one of them, named Caiaphas, who was high priest that year, said to them, 'You know nothing at all. You do not understand that it is better for you that one man should die for the people than that the whole nation should perish.' This he did not say of his own accord, but being high priest that year he prophesied that Jesus would die for the nation, and not for the nation only, but to gather into one the children of God who are scattered abroad. So from that day on they made plans to put him to death. Jesus therefore no longer walked openly among the Jews, but went away to the region near the wilderness, to a town called Ephraim, and there he stayed with the disciples. Now the Passover of the Jews was at hand, and many went up from the country to Jerusalem before the Passover to purify themselves. They sought Jesus and said to one another as they stood in the temple, 'What do you think? Will he not come to the feast at all?' Now the chief priests and the Pharisees had given orders that if anyone knew where he was, he should let them know, so that they might arrest him. Six days before the Passover, Jesus came to Bethany, where Lazarus was, whom Jesus had raised from the dead. There they gave a supper for him, and Martha served, while Lazarus was one of those at table with him. Then a large crowd of the Jews learned that he was there, and they came, not only on account of Jesus but also to see Lazarus, whom he had raised from the dead. So the chief priests planned to put Lazarus to death as well, because on account of him many of the Jews were going away and believing in Jesus. The next day the great crowd that had come to the feast heard that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem. So they took branches of palm trees and went out to meet him, crying out, 'Hosanna! Blessed is he who comes in the name of the Lord, even the King of Israel!' And Jesus found a young donkey and sat on it, as it is written: 'Fear not, daughter of Zion; behold, your king is coming, sitting on a donkey's colt!' Then he said..." And Jesus said: "The hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified. Truly, truly, I say to you, unless a grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains alone; but if it dies, it bears much fruit. Whoever loves his life loses it, and whoever hates his life in this world will keep it for eternal life." And he said: "Father, glorify your name." Then a voice came from heaven: "I have glorified it, and I will glorify it again." The crowd that stood by heard it and said that it had thundered; others said, "An angel has spoken to him." Jesus answered, "This voice came not for my sake but for yours. Now is the judgment of this world; now will the ruler of this world be cast out. And I, when I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to myself." The crowd answered him, "We have heard from the Law (al-Nāmūs) that the Christ remains forever; how can you say that the Son of Man must be lifted up? Who is this Son of Man?" So Jesus said to them, "The light is among you for a little longer. Walk while you have the light, lest darkness overtake you. He who walks in darkness does not know where he is going. While you have the light, believe in the light, that you may become sons of light." When Jesus had said these things, he departed and hid himself from them. And he said: "My children, I am with you a little longer, and you will seek me, and where I am going you cannot come." As I said to the Jews, "Where I am going you cannot come," so now I tell you. John, in his discussion with the Jews in the Temple, said: Jesus said, "I am going away, and you will seek me, and you will die in your sin. Where I am going you cannot come." So the Jews said, "Will he kill himself, since he says, 'Where I am going you cannot come'?" He said to them, "You are from below, I am from above; you are of this world, I am not of this world. I told you that you would die in your sins; for if you do not believe that I am he, you will die in your sins." So they said to him, "Who are you?" Then he said to them... And they said to him, "Our father is Abraham." He said, "If you were Abraham's children, you would do what Abraham did. But now you seek to kill me, a man who has told you the truth that I heard from God (exalted is He). This Abraham did not do. You are doing the works of your father." They said, "We were not born of fornication." He said to them, "You are of your father the devil, and you want to do your father's desires. He was a murderer from the beginning, and does not stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he lies, he speaks out of his own character, for he is a liar and the father of lies. But because I tell the truth, you do not believe me. Which of you convicts me of sin?" The discourse ends. "And now I tell you: that you love one another as I have loved you; by this everyone will know that you are my disciples." And Jesus said:

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 158 (part 3 of 5):

Whoever believes in me does not merely believe in me alone; rather, he believes also in the One who sent me. Whoever sees me has seen the One who sent me. I have come as the light of the world, so that everyone who believes in me may be saved from the darkness. Whoever hears my words and does not believe in me, I do not judge him; for I did not come to judge the world, but to give life to the world. Whoever rejects me and does not accept my words, there is one who judges him: the word that I have spoken will judge him on the Last Day. For I did not speak on my own authority; the Lord who sent me has given me the commandment. Then he said:

Truly, truly, I say to you: whoever believes in me will do the works that I do, and will do even greater than these. If you love me, keep my commandments. I will ask the Father, and he will give you another Farqalit (Paraclete, Advocate), so that he may remain with you forever: the Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive, because they neither see him nor know him. But you know him, for he dwells with you and is in you. I will not leave you orphans; I will come to you shortly. Whoever loves me keeps my word, and whoever does not love me does not keep my words. The word you hear is not mine, but belongs to the Lord who sent me. I have said these things to you while I am still with you. The Farqalit is the Holy Spirit (Ruh al-Qudus), whom my Lord will send in my name; he will teach you everything and remind you of all that I have said to you. Peace I leave with you; my peace I give to you. Let your hearts not be troubled, nor let them fear. You have heard that I said to you:

I am going away, and I will come back to you. If you loved me, you would rejoice that I am going to the Father, for the Father is greater than I. Now I have told you before it happens, so that when it happens you may believe. I will not speak with you much, for the ruler of the world is coming, and he has no claim over me. But so that the world may know that I love the Father, I do as the Father commanded me. I am the true vine, and my Father is the vinedresser. Every branch that does not bear fruit he takes away, and every one that bears fruit he prunes, so that it may bear more fruit. You are clean because of the word I have spoken to you. Abide in me, and I in you. Just as the branch cannot bear fruit by itself unless it abides in the vine, so neither can you unless you abide in me. I am the vine, and you are the branches. Whoever abides in me, and I in him, bears much fruit; for apart from me you can do nothing. If anyone does not abide in me, he is thrown out like a branch and withers; they gather them and throw them into the fire, and they are burned. If you abide in me and my words abide in you, you will ask whatever you wish, and it will be done for you. By this my Father is glorified, that you bear much fruit. You are my beloved. If you know all that I have commanded you, [you will be blessed]. I have commanded you these things so that you may love one another. If the world hates you, know that it hated me before you. If you were of the world, the world would love its own; but you are not of the world, for I have chosen you out of the world. Therefore the world hates you. If I had not come and spoken to them, they would have no sin; but now they have no excuse for their sin. If I had not done works that no one else has done, they would have no sin. This is so that the word written in their Namus (Law) may be fulfilled: that they hated me without cause. When the Farqalit comes, whom I will send to you, the Spirit of truth who proceeds from the Lord, he will bear witness, and you also will bear witness, because you are with me from the beginning. I have said these things to you so that you will not stumble. They will expel you from their synagogues (ma'ajid). I did not tell you this before, because I was with you. Now I am going to him who sent me. I tell you the truth: it is better for you that I go away; for if I do not go, the Farqalit will not come to you. But if I go, I will send him to you. When he comes, he will convict the world concerning sin. I have much more to say to you, but you cannot bear it now. When that Spirit of truth comes, he will guide you into all truth; for he does not speak on his own, but speaks whatever he hears, and he will tell you what is to come. He will glorify me, for he will take from what is mine and declare it to you. A little while and you will not see me; and again a little while and you will see me.

They said:

What is this "little while" he speaks of?

He said to them:

Are you discussing this among yourselves?

Truly, I say to you: you will weep and mourn, but the world will rejoice; you will grieve, but your grief will turn into joy. A woman in labor is in distress because her hour has come; but when she has delivered the child, she no longer remembers the anguish for joy that a human being has been born into the world. Yasu' spoke these words, lifted his eyes to heaven, and said:

O Lord, the hour has come. Glorify your servant, so that your servant may glorify you, just as you gave him authority over all flesh, to give eternal life to all whom you have given him. This is eternal life: that they know you, that you alone are the true God, and Yasu' the Messiah whom you sent. I have glorified you on earth; I have finished the work that you gave me to do. And now, Father, glorify me with the glory that I had with you before the world existed. I have revealed your name to the people. Now they know that everything you have given me is from you; they know truly that I came from you, and they believe that you sent me. I am coming to you, O holy Father. Keep them in your name, which you gave me, so that they may be one as we are one. While I was with them in the world, I kept them in your name. I do not ask that you take them out of the world, but that you keep them from the evil one, for they are not of the world, just as I am not of the world. Sanctify them in your truth; your word is truth. As you sent me into the world, so I have sent them into the world. I do not pray for these alone, but also for those who believe in me through their word, that they may all be one, just as you, Father, are in me and I in you, that they also may be in us, so that the world may believe that you sent me.

Yasu' said this, and went out with his disciples (Hawariyyun) to the spring of Umrah, the valley of the cedars. There was a garden there, which he and his disciples entered. Yahuda al-Iskhariyuti, who was going to betray him, knew the place, for Yasu' often gathered there with his disciples. Before the feast of Passover (Fasḥ), Yasu' knew that his hour had come to depart from this world. When supper was served, the devil put it into the heart of Yahuda, son of Shim'un al-Iskhariyuti, to betray him. Yasu' rose from supper, laid aside his garments, girded himself with a towel, and began to wash the disciples' feet and dry them with the towel he had girded on. When he came to Shim'un al-Safa (Peter), Shim'un said to him:

Master, are you going to wash my feet?

Yasu' said:

What I am doing you do not understand now, but you will understand it later.

Shim'un al-Safa said:

You shall never wash my feet!

Yasu' said to him:

If I do not wash you, you have no part with me.

Shim'un said:

Master, then wash not only my feet, but also my hands and my head!

Yasu' said to him:

[Page 485] Whoever has bathed needs only to wash his feet. When he had washed their feet, he took his garments, reclined, and said to them:

Do you know what I have done to you?

You call me Teacher and Lord, and you speak well, for so I am.

If I, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you ought to wash one another's feet. Truly, truly, I say to you! A servant is not greater than his master, nor a messenger greater than the one who sent him. He also said:

Truly, truly, I say to you: one of you will betray me. Matta said:

While Yasu' was at Bethany, in the house of Shim'un the leper, a woman came with an alabaster flask of very costly ointment, and poured it on his head as he reclined. Then one of the Twelve, that is, of the Hawariyyun, who will be mentioned in "al-Ma'idah" and "al-An'am" by name, and who is called Yahuda al-Iskhariyuti, went to the chief priests and said:

What will you give me if I hand him over to you?

They weighed out for him thirty pieces of silver. From that time he began to look for an opportunity to betray him. On the first day of Unleavened Bread (al-Fitr), Marqus said:

When they sacrificed the Passover lamb, his disciples said to him:

Where do you want us to go to prepare the Passover for you to eat?

He said:

Go into the city to a certain man and say to him: "The Teacher says, my time is near; I will keep the Passover at your house with my disciples." The disciples did as Yasu' had commanded them, and they prepared the Passover. Luqa said:

He taught in the temple during the day, and at night he went out and rested on the mountain called the Mount of Olives. All the people came early to him to hear him. When the feast of Unleavened Bread, called the Passover, drew near, [Page 486] the chief priests sought how they might destroy him, but they feared the people. Then Satan entered into Yahuda, called al-Iskhariyuti, who was one of the Twelve. He went and spoke with the chief priests and officers about how he might betray him to them. They were glad and promised him money. He sought an opportunity to betray him to them away from the crowd. Then the day of Unleavened Bread came, on which the Passover lamb must be sacrificed. He sent Butrus (Peter) and Yuhanna (John), and said:

Go and prepare the Passover for us.

Then he said:

They went and prepared the Passover. When evening came, he reclined with the twelve disciples. He said:

He said to them:

I have earnestly desired to eat this Passover with you; for I tell you, I will not eat it again until it is fulfilled in the Kingdom of God. Matta said:

While they were eating, he said:

Truly, I say to you, one of you will betray me. They were deeply grieved, and each one began to say:

Surely it is not I?

Yuhanna said:

He said:

Truly, truly, I say to you: one of you will betray me. The disciples looked at one another, uncertain of whom he meant. One of his disciples, whom Yasu' loved, was reclining in Yasu's bosom. Shim'un al-Safa motioned to him to ask which one he meant. That disciple leaned back on Yasu's breast and said to him:

Master, who is it?

Yasu' answered:

It is the one to whom I will give this piece of bread when I have dipped it. He dipped the bread and gave it to Shim'un al-Iskhariyuti. Matta said:

He said:

The one who dips his hand with me into the dish is the one who will betray me. The Son of Man goes as it has been written concerning him [Page 487]. Woe to that man by whom the Son of Man is betrayed! It would have been better for that man if he had never been born. Yahuda, the one who would betray him, answered:

Is it I, Master?

He said:

You have said so.

They sang a hymn and went out to the Mount of Olives. Luqa said:

He said to them:

The kings of the nations lord it over them, and those who exercise authority over them are called benefactors. But you shall not be like that. Rather, the greatest among you must become like the youngest, and the leader like the servant. Who is greater: the one who reclines at table, or the one who serves? Is it not the one who reclines? But I am among you as one who serves. You are the ones who have stood by me in my trials. And just as my Father appointed a kingdom for me, I appoint for you a kingdom, that you may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel. Then he went on:

Then he went out as usual and proceeded to the Mount of Olives, and his disciples went with him. When he came to the place, he said to them:

Pray that you may not enter into temptation. He withdrew from them about a stone's throw, knelt down, and prayed. Matta said:

Then Yasu' said to them:

All of you will fall away because of me this night, for it is written: "I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered." Butrus answered and said to him:

Even if all fall away, I will not fall away. Yasu' said to him:

Truly, I say to you, this very night, before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times. Yuhanna said:

The truth, the truth I tell you: the rooster will not crow until you deny me three times. Do not let your hearts be troubled. Believe in God, and believe in me.

(p. 488) Matthew said: Peter said to him: Even if I am compelled to die with you, I will not deny you. Mark said: Peter persisted and said: My father, even if I am compelled to die with you, I will not deny you. All the disciples said likewise.

Then he came with them to a village called Gethsemane, and said to the disciples: Sit here while I go and pray over there. Stay and keep watch with me. After that he fell on his face and prayed, and he came to the disciples and found them asleep. Mark said: Then Peter said: Simon, are you asleep? Could you not keep watch with me for one hour? Keep watch and pray, lest you enter into temptations. The spirit is eager, but the flesh is weak. He went away again and prayed, and came again and found them asleep, for their eyes were heavy. So he left them and went away again to pray.

Luke said: An angel from heaven appeared to him to strengthen him. He was praying fervently, and his sweat was like clots of blood falling upon the ground.

Matthew said: Then he came to the disciples and said to them: Sleep now and rest. The hour has drawn near. While he was still speaking, Judas Iscariot, one of the Twelve, came, with a great crowd, with swords and clubs, from the chief priests and elders of the people. The one whom he kissed is he; seize him. He came to Yasu' and said: Peace, teacher. (p. 489) And he kissed him. Yasu' said to him: Friend, for this did you come? Then they came, laid their hands on Yasu', and seized him. Then he said: At that hour Yasu' said to the crowds: You have come out as against a robber, with swords and clubs, to take me. Every day I sat among you teaching in the Temple, and you did not seize me. All this happened so that the writings of the prophets, peace be upon them, might be fulfilled.

John said: Judas took a band of soldiers from the chief priests and the Pharisees, and officers, and came there with lanterns, torches, and weapons. Yasu', knowing everything that would befall him, went out and said to them: Whom do you seek? They said: Yasu' the Nazarene. He said: I am he. Judas was standing with them. When he said: I am he, they drew back and fell to the ground. Yasu' said: If you are seeking me, let these go, that the word he spoke might be fulfilled: Of those whom you gave me, not one has perished.

Matthew said: Then all his disciples left him and fled. Those who had seized Yasu' led him to the house of Caiaphas, the high priest. Peter followed him at a distance to the house of the high priest, and he entered inside and sat with the servants to see the outcome. Mark said: And he sat with the servants by the fire, (p. 490) warming himself. John said: Simon Peter and the other disciple, the one of whom it was said earlier that 'Isa loved him, followed Yasu'. The high priest knew that disciple, so Yasu' entered the house of the high priest. But Simon stood outside the door. The other disciple, who was known to the high priest, went out and spoke to the doorkeeper and brought Simon Peter in. The maid who kept the door said to Simon: Are you not one of this man's disciples? He said to her: No. The servants and the officers were standing, kindling a fire to warm themselves, for it was a cold night, and Simon stood with them, warming himself too.

Matthew said: The high priest said: I adjure you by the living God to tell us whether you are the Messiah. Yasu' said to him: You have said it. Then he mentioned that they resolved to kill him. He said: Then they spat in his face, covered his face with a cloth, and struck his face, saying: O Messiah, prophesy to us who it is that struck you.

Mark said: While Peter was in the lower part of the courtyard, a girl, one of the high priest's maidservants, came and said to him: You too were with Yasu' the Nazarene. Matthew said: With Yasu' the Galilean. Luke said: When a maidservant saw him sitting by the light, she recognized him and said: This man too was with him. He denied it and said: I do not know him. Matthew said: He denied it before them all. When he went out to the gate, another maidservant saw him and said: This man too was with (p. 491) Yasu' the Nazarene. He denied it again with an oath: I do not know the man. After a little while, those who stood by came up and said to Peter: Truly you are one of them, for your speech betrays you. Mark said: You are a Galilean, and your speech resembles theirs. He said: Then Peter began to curse and swear: I do not know the man. Immediately the rooster crowed. Peter remembered the word of Yasu': Before the rooster crows, you will deny me three times. He went out and wept bitterly.

When morning came, all of them made a plot against Yasu' to put him to death. They bound him, led him away, and delivered him to Pilate the Nabataean. When Judas, who is called Judas Iscariot, saw that he had been condemned, he repented and returned the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests, saying: I have sinned in delivering innocent blood. They said: What is that to us? He threw the silver into the Temple and departed, and he hanged himself. The chief priests took the silver and said: It is not lawful for us to put it into the treasury of charity, since it is the price of blood. So they consulted together and bought the potter's field as a burial place for strangers. For this reason that field was called the Field of Blood, to this day. Then was fulfilled what Jeremiah the prophet said: They took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of the one whom the Children of Israel priced, and gave them for the potter's field, as the Lord commanded me.

As for Yasu', he stood before the governor (p. 492) and then it is mentioned that the governor was unwilling to kill him, and that his wife sent to him saying: Have nothing to do with that righteous man, for I have suffered much today on his account in a dream. He strove with them to release him, but they refused anything but his crucifixion, and they shouted against him. He said to them: What evil has he done? They shouted all the more and said: Let him be crucified. When Pilate saw that he was gaining nothing, he took water and washed his hands before the crowd, and said: I am innocent of the blood of this righteous man. They said: His blood be on us and on our children. Luke said: Pilate said to the chief priests: I have found no fault in this man, until he said: When he learned that he was under the authority of Herod, that is, of Galilee, he sent him to Herod, for Herod was in Jerusalem in those days. When Herod saw Yasu', he rejoiced greatly, for he had long desired to see him, because of the many things he had heard about him, and he hoped to see some sign performed by him. He questioned him at length, but he did not answer him. Herod and his soldiers held him in contempt and mocked him, clothed him in a gorgeous robe, and sent him back to Pilate. Pilate and Herod became friends that day, for previously there had been enmity between them. Then it is mentioned that Pilate said to them: I have found no fault in him to charge him with, nor has Herod. They did not accept this from him, and they kept shouting: Crucify him, crucify him.

John said: Then he sat (p. 493), that is, Pilate, on a seat in a place known as the Pavement, and in Hebrew it is called Gabbatha.

Then all the narrators of their Gospels mentioned that they crucified him between two robbers, and that they used to mock him, even the two robbers who were crucified with him. Mark said: When it was the sixth hour, darkness covered all the earth until the ninth hour. He cried out with a loud voice: My God, my God, why have you forsaken me? The veil of the Temple was torn in two from top to bottom. The earth quaked, the rocks split, the tombs were opened, and many bodies of the holy ones who had slept rose from their graves, entered the city, and appeared to many. There were many women there, looking on from afar, who had followed Yasu' from Galilee, among them Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the younger, and the mother of Joses, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee. John said: Standing by his cross were his mother and his mother's sister, Mary the daughter of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene. Then they mentioned that he was buried. Mark mentioned that it was a Friday. John said: As for the Jews, because it was the Friday, they said: These bodies must not remain on the cross, for the Sabbath was a great day. Then he mentioned that they took them down, and that 'Isa was buried. Matthew said: The King came (p. 494) after three days and raised him up, and said to the women: He has risen. Hurry and tell his disciples: Behold, he has gone before you to Galilee. The chief priests of the Jews bribed the soldiers who were guarding his tomb, saying: His disciples stole him from the tomb. They said so, and this rumor spread among the Jews until this day. As for the eleven disciples, they went to Galilee, to the mountain where they had been commanded. When they saw him, they prostrated themselves before him, but some doubted. Luke said: While they were speaking, 'Isa stood in their midst and said to them: Peace be upon you, O people. Do not be afraid. They were startled and frightened, and thought they were seeing a spirit. He said to them: Why are you troubled, and why do doubts arise in your hearts? Look at my hands and my feet, for I am he. Touch me, and look at me. A spirit does not have flesh and bone as you see that I have. When he had said this, he showed them his hands and feet, and they still did not believe for joy and amazement. He said to them: Have you anything here to eat? They gave him a piece of broiled fish and some honeycomb. He took it before them and ate, and gave them the rest. Then he led them out as far as Bethany, lifted up his hands, and blessed them. While he was blessing them, he parted from them and ascended into heaven. John said: He said to Mary: Go to my brothers and tell them: I am ascending to my Father and your Father, and to my God and your God. Matthew said: Then Yasu' came (p. 495) and spoke to them, saying: All authority in heaven and on earth has been given to me. Go, therefore, and make disciples of all nations.

The conclusion of what I intended to say here from the Gospels about this story is this: it has become clear to you that all their Gospels agree that their knowledge about him ended with one man, al-Iskharyuti (Judas Iscariot). As for the other enemies, they did not know him. He only laid his hand on him, and did not say with his tongue that he was him. The time was night. Jesus himself said to his companions: "All of you will doubt me this night." All his disciples fled, so they had no knowledge afterward of what had happened concerning him. Peter only followed him from a distance. The one who pointed him out hanged himself. The narrator's claim that the king said he had risen from the dead is only the report of women who were at the tomb from a long distance, and the women did not know the king apart from others. And similar matters that yield nothing but conjecture with effort. As for the signs that are said to have occurred, even granting their authenticity, believing in them does not harm us, and they would be a sign of their audacity toward God in crucifying the one they thought was the Messiah. Among the best things said on this is his statement after they gathered with him following his ascension: "All authority has been given to me," which establishes that the giver is other than him. All of this confirms the Qur'an in that they were in doubt about him, and it indicates that the one crucified, if it is true that they crucified the one they thought was him, is the one who was pointed out. As (p-496) some scholars have said: his likeness was cast upon him. This is supported by their saying that he hanged himself, for the apparent meaning is that when they did not see him after that, they assumed he had hanged himself, so they asserted it, and God knows best. As for his saying: "You, O Lord, are in me, and I am in you, so that they (i.e., the disciples) may be in us," and similar expressions that give the impression of incarnation, what is meant is unity in purpose, such that each of them wills only what the other wills and is pleased only with what the other is pleased with. This is of the same kind as what is in the sacred hadith: "I was his hearing with which he hears..." to its end. Likewise, the use of "Son" and "Father" means that He treats them with His kindness in the manner of a father treating his son, so the intended meaning is the purpose, just as this is interpreted in the case of the attribution of anger, love, and the like to God (exalted) in our law. Much of the explanation of the ambiguous (mutashabih) by reference to the clear (muhkam) has passed in similar cases in "Aal 'Imran," and it passed at that place and elsewhere that everything that suggests a deficiency may not be attributed to God (exalted) in our law. And God is the Granter of success.

When the discourse concluded regarding the affair of 'Isa (peace be upon him) in this excellent method, through what He mentioned of the advice of the Jews and their foul deeds, and that they intended to kill him (peace be upon him), but their intention failed and their spark was extinguished, and their opinion was refuted and their transgression was turned back upon them, and he gained thereby the highest ranks and the most excellent stations, He said, confirming what He established in the verse before it of the certainty of their lie, affirming that in their extreme enmity toward him they would become among his followers who affirm all of his command, of which is the affirmation of Muhammad (ﷺ), and emphasizing this most strongly because of their denial of him:

﴿And there is not any of the People of the Book﴾ (ahl al-kitab), that is, not one who lives to see his descent at the end of time, ﴿except﴾, by My might, ﴿that he will surely believe in him﴾, that is, in 'Isa (peace be upon him), ﴿before his death﴾, that is, before the death of 'Isa (peace be upon him). That is to say, he will not die until he descends at the end of time, and Allah will strengthen the religion of Islam through him, until all the people of the religious communities (milal) enter into it. This indicates that Musa (peace be upon him), although Allah (exalted be He) supported him with prophets who renewed his religion for a long time, the prophet who abrogated the law of Musa, who is 'Isa, peace be upon them both, is the one through whom Allah will strengthen this Arab Prophet in renewing his law, paving the way for his affair, and defending his religion. He will be from his community after having been the bearer of an independent law and followers in great numbers. This is a matter that Allah decreed in eternity, and so He carried it out. So lengthen (your argument), O Jews, or shorten it.
