The meaning of the verse, then, Allah knows best, is that there is none of the People of the Book who differ concerning 'Isa (peace be upon him) who is in doubt, except that he will be certain of 'Isa (peace be upon him) before his death, after his descent from heaven, that he was neither killed nor crucified, and he will believe in him when doubt is removed, Allah knows best.

Al-Shaykhan (al-Bukhari and Muslim), Ahmad, Abu Bakr ibn Mardawayh, and others narrated from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him) that the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "By He in whose hand is my soul, the son of Maryam will shortly descend among you as a just judge and a righteous leader. He will break the cross, kill the swine, and abolish the jizya (poll tax), and wealth will be so abundant that one prostration will be better than the world and all that is in it." In another narration: "and the prostration will be one, for Allah, Lord of the worlds." In another narration: "until Allah destroys all the religions except Islam; Allah will destroy in his time all the religions except Islam."

Abu Hurayrah said: "Recite, if you wish: ﴿And there is not any of the People of the Book except that he will surely believe in him before his death﴾," the verse, "his death" referring to the death of 'Isa (peace be upon him). Then Abu Hurayrah repeated it three times. "And hatred, animosity and envy will vanish, and wealth will be offered, but no one will accept it." In another narration: "wealth will overflow until no one will accept it."

Muslim narrated from him (may Allah be pleased with him): "How will you be when the son of Maryam descends among you and your imam is from among you?" In another narration: "your leader (amman) from among you." Al-Walid ibn Muslim, one of the narrators of the hadith, said: Ibn Abi Dhi'b said: "Do you know what 'your imam from among you' means?" I said: "Tell me." He said: "He will lead you by the Book of your Lord, blessed and exalted, and the Sunnah of your Prophet (ﷺ)."

Muslim also narrated from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah (may Allah be pleased with them both) who said: I heard the Prophet (ﷺ) say: "A group of my community will continue to fight for the truth, prevailing until the Day of Resurrection. Then 'Isa ibn Maryam (peace be upon him) will descend, and their leader will say: 'Come and lead us in prayer.' He will say: 'No, for some of you are leaders over others,' as an honor from Allah to this community."

It is also narrated from Ibn 'Abbas and Muhammad ibn 'Ali, known as Ibn al-Hanafiyyah (may Allah be pleased with them), that the meaning is: "except that he will believe in 'Isa (peace be upon him) before the death of that People of the Book, at the time of the death-rattle (gharghara), when faith will no longer benefit him, so that this will increase his regret." Al-Asbahani said: The reading of Ubayy supports this interpretation: "they will believe before their death," with a damma on the nun.

When He (exalted be He) had informed of their condition with Him in this world, He followed it with His action toward them in the next, so He said:

﴿And on the Day of Resurrection﴾, that is, the day whose mention cuts off the hearts, whose contemplation leads to every good, and restrains from every evil, ﴿He will be﴾, and He announced their wretchedness by His saying: ﴿a witness against them﴾, that is, for what they did.

*Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 160:*

When the particle of elevation (ḥarf al-istiʿlāʾ, the preposition *ʿalā*) in the testimony indicated that there is no good for them in either of the two abodes, and the implied sense is "*fa-bi-ẓulmihim*" (so because of their wrongdoing), it made the following statement its consequence, to show that the Torah (al-Tawrah) was revealed in installments: ﴿Then, because of wrongdoing﴾. That is, great in extent, firmly established and fixed. It encompasses the detail of breaking the covenant and what is joined to it, of what they made lawful after the Torah had made it unlawful. And he said, pointing to the increase in their rebuke: ﴿of those who were Jews﴾. That is, those who had adopted Judaism in the past, claiming that they belonged to the people of the Torah and returned to the truth. He did not leave it implicit, specifying them and adding to their reproach: ﴿We forbade them good things which had been made lawful﴾. That is, their lawfulness had been established in the Torah, ﴿for them﴾, such as the fats which Allah (exalted be He) mentioned in *al-Anʿām*.

When he mentioned their wrongdoing, he mentioned comprehensive instances of it, and began with their turning away from the true religion. He said, repeating the governing element (ʿāmil) for emphasis: ﴿and their hindering [others] from the way of Allah﴾. That is, the way than which none is clearer, easier or greater, because the path He laid down contains a greatness and wisdom that cannot be grasped. The verb *ṣadda* may be intransitive (qāṣir), in which case ﴿much﴾ is an adjective of an omitted verbal noun (ṣifat maṣdarin maḥdhūf), meaning "a great hindering." It may also be transitive (mutaʿaddin), in which case it is the direct object, meaning: "and their hindering many people from the way by misguidance." Thus they were deprived of the pleasures of those foods, in return for what they had prevented themselves and others from enjoying of the sweetness of faith.

[p. 500]

﴿وأخذِهِمُ الرِّبا﴾ [and their taking usury]: that is, it is itself ugly and disgraces its practitioner. ﴿وقَدْ﴾ [while]: that is, while the state of affairs is that they ﴿نُهُوا عَنْهُ﴾ [had been forbidden from it]. Thus they added to opposing sound natural disposition the audacity of violating the sanctity of the Mighty God.

When he mentioned usury, he followed it with what is more general than it, saying: ﴿وأكْلِهِمْ أمْوالَ النّاسِ بِالباطِلِ﴾ [and their consuming people's wealth unjustly]: that is, whether it was usury, bribery, or other than these two. When he mentioned some of what He punished them with in this world, he followed it with their recompense in the Hereafter, saying, coordinating it with His saying "We forbade" [in verse 160]: ﴿وأعْتَدْنا لِلْكافِرِينَ﴾ [and We have prepared for the disbelievers]: that is, those for whom disbelief had become a firmly established attribute, so that they died upon it. And since He knew that among them were those who would believe and enter Paradise, He said: ﴿مِنهُمْ﴾ [among them]. And since the recompense is of the same kind as the deed, He said: ﴿عَذابًا ألِيمًا﴾ [a painful punishment]: that is, because of what they caused people pain by consuming their wealth, and by concealing their rights from them of virtues and bounties.

The prohibition of wealth gained through usury, and of other kinds of falsehood, is mentioned in the explicit text of the Torah (al-Tawrah). In the second book (sifr) of it, after what I have already cited in "al-Baqarah" concerning the command to be good to people and the prohibition of harming them, it says: "If you lend money to the poor man who is with you from among my people, you shall not be to him as a creditor, nor shall you take from him usury." In the third, it says: "If your brother becomes poor and seeks help from you, do not leave him like a stranger residing with you, but make provision for him. Beware of taking from him usury or 'aynah (a sale-and-buyback device used to disguise interest); do not lend to him at 'aynah." In the fifth, it says: "Do not give the wages of a prostitute or the price of a dog as an offering in the house of the LORD your God. Do not take usury from your brothers, whether in silver, in food, or in anything that is lent out at interest. As for the foreigner, you may take from him if you wish."

Thus the prohibition of usury is established in their Torah. As for restricting it to the foreigner, that is without doubt an alteration made by them, as evidenced by what I have already cited from it in "al-Baqarah" at His saying: ﴿إنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا والَّذِينَ هادُوا﴾ [Indeed, those who believed and those who were Jews, Christians and Sabians (al-Baqarah 2:62)], concerning the prohibition of treachery toward the enemy, and at His saying: ﴿لا تَعْبُدُونَ إلا اللَّهَ﴾ [You shall not worship except Allah (al-Baqarah 2:83)], concerning kindness to people in general, especially the foreigner. And God is the Granter of success.

Having explained what awaits those whose hearts are sealed, who are plunged deep in disbelief, of punishment, He (exalted is He) explained what awaits those whose insight is illuminated, who are firmly rooted in knowledge and faith, of reward. He said: ﴿But those firm in knowledge among them﴾; that is, those whose hearts were prepared in their original creation to accept knowledge, so nature (al-ṭab') was removed from them; they were polished by wisdom, firmly established by mercy, filled with the light of knowledge, and settled in the intimacy of faith.

When He mentioned the quality of knowledge, which brings all virtues, He followed it with what arises from it, saying: ﴿And the believers﴾; that is, those who were prepared for faith, entered into it, and so it became a settled disposition (khuluq lāzim) for them, both among them and among others; ﴿believe﴾; that is, they renew their faith at every moment; ﴿in what has been sent down to you﴾, because they are the people most aware that it is true; ﴿and what was sent down before you﴾ (p-503), that is, to Moses (peace be upon him). And through their sincere faith they believed in what was sent down to Jesus (peace be upon him), and then in what was sent down to you.

Since prayer is the greatest pillar of the religion, and for this reason it forbids indecency and evil, it is put in the accusative (naṣb) of praise among these nominative (marfū') words, to show its excellence. So He (exalted is He) said: ﴿And those who establish prayer﴾; that is, by performing it with all its prescribed limits. It is also possible, though remotely, that the reason for its accusative case is that "lākin" (but) is treated, with respect to it, as meaning "illā" (except), and its wording is given to it, because of the affinity between them. The meaning then is that they are excepted from those prepared for a painful punishment, in the sense that Allah (glory be to Him, exalted is He), who is the Doer who chooses, foreknew that one who establishes prayer with all its limits does not die as a disbeliever dies, but its blessing reaches him, so he is safe. This is the greatest praise of it. The upshot is that "lākin" was used metaphorically for the meaning of "illā," by the common factor that what follows each of them differs in ruling from what precedes it, just as "illā" was used metaphorically for the meaning of "lākin" in the munqaṭi' exception (al-istithnā' al-munqaṭi', the exception that is not of the same category).

Since returning to the verbal style of the preceding words would make the praise of it clearer, He said: ﴿And those who give zakāh﴾. When He mentioned that they combined their connection with the Creator with kindness to creatures, He mentioned faith, building upon its greatness, detailing some of its details, and indicating that its benefit, just as it must come first, must also come last. So He said: ﴿And the believers in Allah﴾; that is, keeping in mind what He has of attributes of perfection; and He joined to it what drives toward every good and restrains from every evil, as encouragement and warning, so He said: ﴿and the Last Day﴾. Thus faith is mentioned five times, for these descriptions belong to one subject, and they are joined by "wa" (and) to magnify them and to indicate that the quality of firmness in knowledge requires that they be at the summit of each of these qualities. Attachment to each of them implies belief in the Day of Judgment, for no one is praised who possesses any of them while being devoid of belief in it. Therefore, to point out the magnitude of their matter and the loftiness of their rank, He used the demonstrative of distance, saying: ﴿Those﴾; that is, the high in rank and aspiration. And since the context concerns those firm in knowledge who act, He used the strongest emphasis with "sa-" (sa-), because the deceit here is less than in the first case. He did not define the reward, and described it as great, saying: ﴿We shall give them﴾; that is, by Our overwhelming greatness, by a promise that will not be broken; ﴿a great reward﴾.

(p-505) When these attributes applied to the prophets, peace be upon them, and revelation was among their conditions, He (Exalted is He) said, refuting their doubt, which stated: "If he were a prophet, he would have brought his book from heaven all at once, as Moses, peace be upon him, brought the Torah all at once," while they acknowledged the prophethood of these prophets, peace be upon them, despite their lacking that characteristic. That did not detract from the prophethood of any of them, nor from their mission. ﴿Indeed, We have revealed to you﴾. It is also possible that this is a reason for "they believe" (in the previous verse): that is, they believed in what was sent down to you because ﴿We have revealed to you as﴾, that is, just as, ﴿We revealed to Noah﴾. They have believed in what he brought, due to the miracle (mu'jiz, a sign that compels belief) he brought, which necessitates faith, without depending on another miracle or anything else. This is because establishing the thing signified depends only on the establishment of the proof. When the proof is complete, demanding another proof is a request for more and a display of obstinacy and stubbornness. And Allah, glorified is He, does what He wills and decrees what He desires.

Since the station of inspiration, which is the prophets, comes from Allah (Exalted is He), He said: ﴿and the prophets after him﴾. That is, they know this through their firm grounding in knowledge and the purity of their attributes, and they have no doubt that all of them come from one niche (of light). Moreover, this Book is more eloquent, its expression of its purposes is clearer and more comprehensive, so they are more inclined toward it and more receptive to it. As for those whose hearts are sealed, who are prevented from firmly grounded knowledge because of the thickness of the veil, to the extent that they look at its secrets only from behind a covering, they are not receptive to the light of knowledge that prepares one for faith. So they hastened to disbelief and rushed toward humiliation and abasement, and in the Hereafter, toward wrath and the Fire.

(p-506) When (Exalted is He) had summarized the mention of the prophets, He detailed them, saying, drawing attention to the nobility and fame of those He mentioned: ﴿And We revealed to Abraham﴾, that is, your father and their father as well; ﴿and Ishmael﴾, that is, his eldest son, who is your father apart from them; ﴿and Isaac﴾, who is his second son and their father; ﴿and Jacob﴾, that is, the son of Isaac; ﴿and the tribes﴾, that is, the sons of Jacob.

When He summarized by mentioning the tribes after detailing those before them, He detailed those after them, saying: ﴿and Jesus﴾, that is, the last of them from the descendants of Jacob; ﴿and Job﴾, who is from the descendants of Esau son of Isaac, according to what they (the scholars) have mentioned; ﴿and Jonah, Aaron and Solomon﴾. Since the context was the glorification of revelation, and David, peace be upon him, was among the People of the Book, He said: ﴿And We gave David the Psalms﴾, that is, while they claim to believe in it, despite acknowledging that it was not sent down all at once, nor written, from heaven.

[p. 507] When the requirements of the station of prophethood had been fulfilled, and there were among them Messengers, and a captious objector might say, "The status of the Messengers differs from that of the Prophets in revelation," He said, coordinating with what is implied by the word "We revealed" (awhayna) in what precedes: "We have sent whom We will of these whom We have related to you here, and to whom We will of mankind": ﴿and Messengers﴾, that is, other than these; ﴿whom We have related to you﴾, that is, We have recited their mention; ﴿to you﴾. Since relating them to him did not encompass the whole of past time, He said: ﴿before﴾, that is, before the sending down of this verse; ﴿and Messengers We have not related to you﴾, that is, up to now.

Since the intended meaning is that there is no distinction between the Prophet (nabi) and the Messenger (rasul) in revelation, He drew attention to this with His words: ﴿And Allah spoke﴾, that is, He to whom all perfection belongs, so He does what He wills, and no one has any command along with Him; ﴿to Moses directly﴾, that is, gradually, bit by bit, according to what is beneficial, without the intermediary of an angel. Thus there is no distinction in revelation between what came through an intermediary and what came without one. The meaning is that if you were only hesitating to believe in some of the Prophets out of a demand for proof, so that you might know that He did to him what He did to Moses, peace be upon him, of honour, you would not believe in Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, the Tribes, Aaron, and others either, for he was singled out for direct speech over them. Why then do you make bringing the like of what Moses, peace be upon him, brought a condition for believing in some Prophets but not others? And if you make the condition the bringing of a Book in its entirety from heaven, claiming that he had this but not direct speech and other things that were granted to him, that would be, even on the assumption of granting it for argument's sake, arbitrariness and preference without a preponderating cause. Moreover, the Torah too, as its explanation has previously passed, is like this Qur'an in its being sent down in portions according to events, as His word "directly" indicates. And not a single copy of it was written down all at once, except the two tablets which were placed in the Ark of Testimony, just as some surahs of the Qur'an were sent down all at once, such as Surat al-An'am. The fact that Moses, peace be upon him, brought down these two tablets written from the mount of Sinai is no proof of their being sent down from heaven. Many of its texts indicate this, the clearest of which is that He (exalted be He) forbade them to work on the Sabbath, after their deliverance from the sea, at the time of the sending down of the manna, as He explained in the second Sifr (Book) of it. He did not explain how the one who disobeyed in this should be dealt with until a long time afterwards, as evidenced by what is in the fourth Sifr of it, in the story of the wandering: "The children of Israel remained in the wilderness, and they found a man gathering sticks on the Sabbath day. Those who found him gathering sticks brought him to Moses, and Aaron, and to all the congregation. And they put him in custody, because it had not been declared what should be done to him. Then the LORD said to Moses: The man shall surely be put to death; all the congregation shall stone him with stones outside the camp. And all the congregation brought him outside the camp and stoned him with stones, and he died, as the LORD commanded Moses." Among them is that He commanded them, as He explained in the second Sifr, to set up the Tent of Meeting toward which they prayed, and Moses heard the speech from it. Then after a period He commanded them, as He explained in the fourth Sifr, to enlarge it. Among them is that He wrote the tablets for him on the mountain: the two tablets which he broke in anger at their making the calf, then two tablets in their place. Then, when the Tent of Meeting was set up, He (glorified and exalted be He) began to speak to him from it. Most of their rulings were legislated by the speech that was in the Tent of Meeting, as is most clear in the Torah. Among them is what is said at the end of the fifth Sifr, which is its last: "When Moses had finished writing the words of this Torah in a book, and had completed them, Moses commanded the priests who bore the Ark of the Covenant of the LORD, and said to them: Take this Book of the Law and put it beside the Ark of the Covenant of the LORD your God, that it may be there as a witness against you. For I know your rebelliousness and your stiff neck. If today, while I am still alive with you, you have been rebellious against the LORD, how much more after my death! Assemble to me all the elders of your tribes and your officers, that I may speak these words in their hearing and call heaven and earth to witness against them. For I know that after my death you will surely act corruptly and turn aside from the way that I have commanded you. And in the latter days evil will befall you, because you will do what is evil in the sight of the LORD, provoking Him to anger through the work of your hands." And Moses spoke in the hearing of the whole assembly of Israel the words of this song until they were complete: "Give ear, O heavens, and I will speak; let the earth hear the words of my mouth." And he spoke many words in censure of them, which I shall mention, God willing (exalted be He), in "al-Ma'idah," at the words: ﴿Whom Allah has cursed and with whom He is angry﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 60]. Then he said: "Thus says God: They have provoked Me to jealousy with what is no god, and angered Me with their idols; and I will provoke them to jealousy with what is no people, and anger them with a foolish nation." And he went on speaking from the word of God, which is among the finest of the Torah, until he said: "When Moses had finished speaking all these words to all Israel, he said to them: Set your hearts toward all the words which I testify to you today." Then he said: "And the LORD spoke to Moses that same day, saying: Go up this mountain of the Abarim, Mount Nebo, which is in the land of Moab, across from Jericho, and view the land of Canaan, which I am giving to the children of Israel for a possession." He mentioned after that a long speech. In all of this, for whoever contemplates it, there is much that is evident, indeed explicit, of that. And in the stories of Noah and Abraham, peace be upon them both, there is what is explicit that the revelation to them both came in portions, as has passed concerning them in the story of Abraham, peace be upon him, in "al-Baqarah." It will also come, God willing (exalted be He), in the mention of the rabbis in "al-A'raf," and in the story of Noah, peace be upon him, in Surat Hud. And Allah is the Granter of success.

He (glorified be He) began in this verse with Noah, peace be upon him, the first of the Ulu al-'Azm (the steadfast Messengers, possessors of resolve), and the first of the bearers of sacred law in existence, and he is among the earliest of the Prophets. His time in antiquity is such that its true measure is known only to Allah (exalted be He). Then He followed him with the second of them in existence, who is Abraham, peace be upon him. Then He mentioned his offspring in their order. As for "the Tribes" (al-Asbat), it may be intended that they are the sons of Jacob, peace be upon him, themselves and their tribes, and the meaning would then be: and the Prophets of the Tribes. This would be a case of a word used in its literal and figurative senses together, and it would include all the Prophets of the Children of Israel. Then He named some of those who entered into the general statement, beginning with the last of them in sending, who is Jesus, peace be upon him, who is one of the two Prophets of the People of the Two Books. He concluded the verse with one of the possessors of books among them, who is his famous forefather, in relation to whom (the Jews call Jesus, peace be upon him, "Son of David"), because his mother was among his descendants. He concluded the verse with the first of the two Prophets of the People of the Two Books, Moses, peace be upon him, who is the last brick laid upon Islam, so those who claim affiliation transferred it to their followers. He placed his brother Aaron, peace be upon him, between two men of affliction, Job and Jonah, and two men of kingship, one of whom was a possessor of a book, namely Solomon and David. All of this is an indication that there is no distinction in the manner of revelation in installments to the Prophets, between the earlier and the later among them, whether they were of the Children of Israel or of others, whether they were granted kingship or not, whether they brought a book or did not. Among the subtleties of this arrangement is that those singled out by mention in the first verse, after their inclusion in the general statement, number eleven names. The Tribes are one of them. The most famous of them for books and scrolls are three: Abraham, Jesus, and David, and each of them came sixth after his counterpart, which is the number in which creation took place. Perhaps this is an indication that Allah does not love haste. Just as He did not hasten in creating creation, so likewise [p. 512] He did not hasten to send down the Books by which their stability and survival depend all at once, but sent them down in installments, in accordance with their benefit and to strengthen their pillars. Among its subtleties is that He (exalted be He) began with those mentioned and concluded with two of the Ulu al-'Azm, who share in that each of them destroyed those who opposed him, like one soul, through incitement, as a warning to those who cover the truth with falsehood among the People of Islam, claiming that they are followers. He placed between them and the rest of those named the general body of the Prophets and Messengers, and perhaps he is the last of the Messengers, so that it may be understood that everyone they were joined to is a Messenger. And because the rank of prophethood precedes the rank of messengership, in the sense that it is more general than it.

When He had listed the names of those who entered into the general statement, He began with the most noble of them, then with those nearest to this noble Prophet, then the nearest after them, among those arranged according to the order of existence, as an indication that through him He established in revelation the custom of their fathers, their brothers, and their descendants. And Allah knows best.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 165:

Since the greater part of the mission of our Prophet (ﷺ) is good tidings and warning, He said, making clear that they were like him in this, as they were before him in revelation, because the purpose of sending the messengers to all of them is the gathering of creation through good tidings and warning: ﴿Messengers﴾; that is, We made them messengers. It is permissible that it be a substitute (badal) for "messengers" (rusulan) mentioned earlier, and that it be a circumstantial clause (hal), in the state of their being ﴿bearers of good tidings and warners﴾. Then He gave the reason for that with His saying: ﴿So that there will not be﴾; that is, so that it is negated that there could exist ﴿for people﴾; that is, any kind of one who has the power of reflection, ﴿an argument against Allah﴾.

Since "hujjah" (argument, proof) may be applied to mere excuse even if it is rejected, He expressed it with the particle of elevation (isti'la'), saying: ﴿an argument against Allah﴾; that is, one whose acceptance is obligatory upon the King, who is singled out with all the attributes of perfection, that He should not punish their disobedient ones. Since the intended meaning is the total negation over all the time that follows the sending, He dropped the preposition and said: ﴿after﴾; that is, that was negated with a negation encompassing all the time that exists after the sending of ﴿the messengers﴾ and their conveying [the message] to people. This is because the obligation of knowing Him (exalted is He) is established only by revelation (al-sam'), whereas knowledge itself, reflection (al-nazar), and tawhid, their path is reason ('aql). So knowledge is received from reason, and obligation is received from the Law (shar') and transmission (naql).

Since that might give the impression that perhaps, before that, a proof or something else could have been established against Him, glory be to Him, He said, removing that: ﴿And Allah is﴾; that is, the One who combines the attributes of greatness; ﴿Mighty﴾; that is, He overcomes everything, and nothing overcomes Him; so He is capable of what they demanded, but nothing is obligatory upon Him, because their demand was by way of obstinacy, and they were not able to render Him powerless; ﴿Wise﴾; that is, He places things in their most perfect places; therefore He arranged matters with which no one has any argument; and among His wisdom is that He does not answer the one who seeks to trouble (mutaʿannit).

(p-514) Since He, glory be to Him, had left them no pretext, and they persisted in their obstinacy, He (exalted be He) pointed to what is implied: that they will not bear witness for you when the matter becomes clear. So He said: ﴿But﴾; that is, despite the proofs that have been established for your truthfulness, and that your Book is from Allah, they do not bear witness to that. ﴿But Allah﴾; that is, the One to whom all command belongs, and for whom there is no equal; ﴿bears witness﴾; that is, to you; ﴿to what He has sent down to you﴾; that is, of this inimitable Book, which has silenced the eloquent and rendered the rhetoricians mute, and which contains these true rulings that agree with what they possess, while they wish to lead people astray from them. So His witness to its eloquence, and His judgment of the truthfulness of the one who brought it, is the witness of Allah, since He is its speaker. This is why He gave the reason in His words: ﴿He has sent it down with His knowledge﴾; that is, knowing its sending down in the inimitable manner, despite the abundance of opponents; so no one has been able, nor is able, to bring about in it any alteration, change, addition, subtraction, or opposition. ﴿And the angels﴾; likewise; ﴿bear witness﴾; to that; because they were present at its sending down, and were trustees over those through whose hands it was to be conveyed, as He (exalted be He) said: ﴿For He makes a guard go before him and behind him﴾ [al-Jinn: 27] ﴿that He may know that they have conveyed the messages of their Lord﴾ [al-Jinn: 28]. This is an address to the servants according to what they understand.

(p-515) Since this might suggest a deficiency, He negated it by His words: ﴿And sufficient is Allah﴾; that is, the One to whom all perfection belongs; ﴿as a witness﴾; that is, and sufficient is His witness in this matter as a testimony above the testimony of others. This is because He sent it down, glory be to Him, as a witness by His own testimony, speaking by it, through its inimitability in its composition, and through the knowledge it contains of wise principles and rulings, and its agreement with the books of the People of the Scripture. So His witness to that is the witness of Allah, and by my life, it does not need the testimony of anyone other than Him.

When Allah, glorified is He, had shown that He established the proofs of its truth through the miracles, so that it was as if He had testified to its reality, it was most beneficial to follow that with a description of the one who denied it in himself and turned others away from it, as a warning against the likes of his condition and as a censure of the error he displayed. So He said: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved﴾; that is, they concealed what they had of knowledge of its truth, by what the witness of reason and the decisive transmitted proof indicate, from among the Jews and others. ﴿And hindered [others] from the way of Allah﴾; that is, the King, the Most High, to whom no command belongs besides Him; by themselves, and by misguiding others through the doubts they cast, such as this one, and their statement, falsely, that the Torah says the law of Musa, upon him be peace, is not abrogated, and their statement that prophets are only to be from the sons of Harun and Dawud, upon both of them be peace. ﴿Have certainly strayed﴾; that is, from the path that leads to their intended goal in their envy, and in preventing what is intended by its elevation; ﴿a far straying﴾. That is, because the most misguided of people is the falsifier who believes he is right, then carries others onto the likeness of his falsehood; so they have reached a state in which there is no hope of their returning to the beneficial path, especially if envy is added to that, for the disease of envy is the most incurable of diseases.

Then he gave the reason for their deep immersion in error as His leading them astray, because of their persistence in what the base tendency of the soul calls them to, which is wrongdoing. This is by His saying, as a threat against them: ﴿Indeed, those who disbelieved﴾; that is, they concealed what they had of the light of reason; ﴿and wronged﴾; that is, they acted, out of envy, like one walking in darkness, through their turning away and their leading others astray; ﴿Allah would not forgive them﴾; that is, by His majesty, for their wrongdoing; ﴿nor would He guide them to a path﴾; that is, because they wasted what He had given them of the light of reason, and because they rejected it;

Then He mocks them with His saying: ﴿except the path of Hell﴾; that is, because of what they did to those they wronged, they opened their hearts to the Fire.

Since the meaning is: indeed He will settle them in it; He said: ﴿abiding therein﴾; that is, because Allah does not forgive shirk; and He emphasized this with His saying: ﴿forever﴾. And since that, together with what they possess of intellect, is a strange matter, He (Exalted is He) said: ﴿And that is for Allah easy﴾; that is, the great matter of their disbelief, their misguidance, and their punishment is easy for Allah, ﴿upon Allah easy﴾; that is, because He is capable of everything.

When the truth became clear to them through argument, and right guidance became evident by removing all their doubts from many angles, and the corruption of their ways was made plain, and his warning to them was made most forceful, this produced the truthfulness of the Messenger and the reality of what he says, and souls submitted. It was therefore most fitting that He, glorified is He, addressed them in general terms, because following him is obligatory for everyone, at the point of explaining the path and establishing the proof. So He said, encouraging and warning: ﴿O mankind﴾, that is, all of you; ﴿the Messenger has come to you﴾, that is, the one perfect in messengerhood (al-rusuliyya), whom the People of the Book (Ahl al-Kitab) were awaiting to remove doubt; ﴿with the truth﴾, that is, what the reality corresponds to. You will see the events and match them against the reports that preceded them, the truth being ﴿from your Lord﴾, that is, the One who bestows favour upon you. If you follow His messenger, you will accept His favour, and His blessing will be complete upon you. For this reason He linked to that His saying: ﴿so believe﴾. Since the implied meaning, as the context indicates as a warning to them, is: "If you believe, faith will be ﴿better for you﴾," He followed it with His saying: ﴿but if you disbelieve﴾, that is, you persist in your ingratitude, or you renew disbelief, then disbelief will be ﴿worse for you﴾, that is, that harm is confined to you, and nothing of it harms Him, nor does it diminish anything of His dominion, just as faith did not benefit Him at all, nor did it add anything to His dominion, because He possesses absolute self-sufficiency. This is the meaning of His saying: ﴿for to God belongs﴾, that is, the One of perfect majesty, ﴿whatever is in the heavens and the earth﴾. This is the placing of the cause in the place of the effect. He did not emphasize it by repeating "whatever," even though the address is to those who are disputing, because the establishment of the proofs has reached a degree of clarity beyond which there is no further increase, by the testimony of God, so that what is indicated by it has become like what is perceived by the senses.

Since the implied meaning is: "He is independent of you; He has servants other than you who do not disobey Him; and He is able to punish you by dropping upon you what He wills from the sky, or causing the earth to swallow what He wills, and other things besides," and since the bestowal of blessing upon the one who agrees, the punishment of the one who opposes, and the acceptance of counsel with acceptance all revolve around knowledge and wisdom, which is the outcome of knowledge and power, He said: ﴿And God is ever﴾, that is, the One to whom belongs complete exclusivity in all attributes of perfection, eternally and everlastingly, together with His possession of all sovereignty, ﴿All-Knowing﴾, that is, no one of understanding should deviate from what He has informed about, that the matter of this Messenger is true, since he did not inform of it except from complete knowledge; and no one who disobeys or obeys is hidden from Him. ﴿All-Wise﴾, so no intelligent person should neglect any of His commands, because He did not set them except according to the perfection of rulings; thus He is worthy to inflict upon whoever opposes Him any vengeance, and to reward whoever obeys Him with every kind of blessing.

Since the matter required the most complete context regarding the story of ʿĪsā (peace be upon him), following the earlier discussion of the great audacity and harshness of the People of the Book, and since what they did with him was the clearest proof of this, and since each of his enemies and his devotees had gone astray regarding his affair, the Jews exaggerating in belittling him and the Christians in elevating him, the law of knowledge and wisdom, indicated by the conclusion of the preceding verse, required explaining what the truth about his station is and calling both parties to it. So He said: ﴿O People of the Book﴾, that is, all of them, ﴿do not commit excess in your religion﴾, that is, do not go to extremes regarding his affair, so that by it you transgress the limits of the Law and the norms of reason. ﴿And do not say about Allah﴾, that is, the Supreme King, to whom none is equal, ﴿anything but the truth﴾, that is, that which corresponds to reality. Whoever says of ʿĪsā (peace be upon him) that he was born of illegitimacy has indeed plunged into falsehood, for if that were so, his mother would not have persisted in acts of obedience, nor would wondrous marvels have appeared through her, nor would he have spoken in the cradle, nor would the springs of wisdom have flowed from his tongue, nor would he have been able to raise the dead. And this implies that Allah, the All-Knowing, the All-Wise, manifested miracles at the hand of one whom He does not love, and that contradicts wisdom; so it is a lie against Allah and far from His transcendence. And whoever says: "He is Allah," or "the son of Allah," is even more and more utterly false, for if that were so, he would not have been created, would not have needed food and drink and what results from them, no one could have harmed him, and the need for a consort for God would be established, so he would not be fit for divinity; and that is the utmost falsehood.

When the Jews claimed that he was not a messenger, and the Christians claimed that he was God, it was fitting to follow with His saying: ﴿The Messiah﴾, that is, the blessed one, who is fit for the Imam to anoint him with the oil of holiness, because of what is in him of suitability for leadership; and he is also fit to anoint people and purify them, because of the honour he has. When He, glorified be He, began with his most famous attribute, and since others may also be described with it, He clarified it by saying: ﴿ʿĪsā﴾; then He informed about him by saying: ﴿the son of Maryam﴾, which attaches him to her as children attach to their mothers, so that his ascription to sonship cannot be correctly made to anyone else; and he is not God, nor the son of God, as the Christians claim, but ﴿the messenger of Allah﴾, not "born of illegitimacy" as the Jews lied.

Since his coming into being was by the word of Allah, without the intermediary of a male, he was described as the word itself, so He said: ﴿and His word﴾, because he was by it, without causation from a father, but rather an existence contrary to customary norms; ﴿which He conveyed﴾, that is, He delivered it, by the highness of His command and the greatness of His power, a swift delivery; ﴿to Maryam﴾, and He placed it within her. And He increased his honour by His saying: ﴿and a spirit﴾, that is, a great one, which He breathed into what came into being in Maryam from the body that stood by the word, not from any male substance. The spirit, in the language of the Arabs, is the breath, and it is like the wind, except that it is stronger, by what it has of the waw and the motion that is homogeneous with it; and because the spirit overpowered him, he used to give life to the dead when he willed. And He perfected his nobility by His saying: ﴿from Him﴾, that is, although Jibrīl was the one who blew it. When something is described with the utmost purity, it is said to be "a spirit," especially if there is life in it by religion or body.

When He had made this truth plain, He based on it His saying: ﴿So believe in Allah﴾, that is, the One whom nothing can overpower and who needs nothing; ﴿and His messengers﴾, that is, ʿĪsā (peace be upon him) and others, all of them, without excess or deficiency; do not believe in some and disbelieve in others, for that is truly the complete disbelief, as has passed.

When He commanded them to affirm the truth, He forbade them from clinging to falsehood, so He said: ﴿And do not say﴾, that is, regarding the affair of ʿĪsā (peace be upon him): ﴿Three﴾, that is, persist, O Jews, in denying what the Christians say about him; and do not say that he was begotten of a father and mother by illegitimacy, which necessitates the trinity; and return, O Christians, from the trinity by which you mean that God is three, even if you add to it that He is one God, because that is self-evidently false. The conclusion is that He forbade each party from the trinity, even though the two intended meanings differ; the just position regarding him is that he is the son of Maryam, so they are two and no more, and he is the servant of Allah, His messenger, His word, and a spirit from Him.

When He forbade them from that by the form of prohibition, He stated it explicitly in its root, encouraging and warning, in the form of a command, by His saying: ﴿Desist﴾, that is, from the trinity which you ascribed to Allah on account of it, and from every disbelief. The context of the threat indicates that the implied meaning is: "If you desist, desisting will be ﴿better for you﴾."

When He negated that He is God, as their saying implied, He restricted the saying concerning Him, glorified be He, to its opposite, as He did regarding ʿĪsā (peace be upon him), so He said: ﴿Indeed, Allah is﴾, that is, the One to whom all perfection belongs. Since the dispute concerns only oneness with respect to divinity, not with respect to essence, He said: ﴿one God﴾, that is, there is no plurality in Him in any way.

Since the station is great, He increased its emphasis, declaring Him far above what they said, so He said: ﴿Glory be to Him﴾, that is, He is exalted, far removed with a great remoteness, and высоко elevated with a great elevation; ﴿from having﴾, that is, from that there should be; ﴿a child﴾, as you said, O Christians, for that entails need, and entails composition and homogeneity, so He would not be one. Then He gave the reason for that by His saying: ﴿To Him belongs﴾, that is, because He is one God with no partner; to Him belongs ﴿whatever is in the heavens﴾; and He emphasised because the station is His, so He said: ﴿and whatever is on the earth﴾, that is, by creation, by ownership, and by sovereignty. Thus it is inconceivable that He would need anything of them; nor anything occupying space within them; and it is not valid in any way that some of what the owner possesses should be a part of Him and a child of His; and ʿĪsā and his mother (peace be upon them both) are among that, and each of them is in need of what exists.

Since the meaning of that is that He is the One who governs both of them and what is in them, for the earth is within the heaven, each heaven is within the one above it, the seventh is within the Kursī, the Kursī is within the Throne, and He is the Lord of the Mighty Throne, there is no dispute about that; and that is in reality the function of the Trustee, so that He suffices whoever has entrusted Him with everything that concerns him. It was as if it were said: He is the Trustee over them and over all that is in them, in arranging your interests; so He based on it His saying: ﴿And sufficient is Allah﴾, that is, the One who encompasses everything in knowledge and power; ﴿as a Trustee﴾, that is, everything needs Him, and He needs nothing; otherwise He would not be sufficient.

Since the *wakil* (agent, trustee) is one who stands in the place of the one who appoints him (*al-muwakkil*) and does what the appointer cannot do, and since God (Exalted is He) is not overcome by anything and needs nothing, and since ʿIsa (peace be upon him) claimed power over nothing except by God and needed sleep, food, drink, and what these entail, it is established that he is a servant of God. Therefore He, glorified is He, said, indicating this: ﴿Never would the Messiah disdain﴾, meaning: he would not seek, wish to refrain, refuse, be shy, be averse, or be arrogant, ﴿the Messiah﴾, meaning the one about whom they claimed divinity, and they were averse to servitude to Him because he was created without a father, and also because he informed of some unseen matters, gave life to some of the dead, and performed extraordinary feats, ﴿to be a servant of God﴾, meaning of the Sovereign, the Greatest, of whose creation ʿIsa (peace be upon him) is one. For he is of the human kind in general, even if his creation was extraordinary compared with human custom, ﴿nor the angels﴾, meaning those who are more wondrous in creation than him, in that they are neither male nor female, (p-524) nor of a substance akin to the human element. Thus they were, for this reason, more wondrous in creation than Adam (peace be upon him) as well. And they do not disdain, by this, to be servants of God.

Since closeness (*taqrib*) generally implies deserving, and since it is a general attribute of the angels, He said: ﴿those brought near﴾, meaning those who are in the presence of holiness (*hadrat al-quds*). They are therefore more fitting for knowledge of unseen matters and for the manifestation of miracles. Jibril, who is one of them, was the cause of the life of ʿIsa (peace be upon him). Some people have also claimed divinity for them. By this, the argument of the Mu'tazilah (a rationalist school) from this verse, for the superiority of the angel over the human, fails. Their argument was that the custom in such a context is ascent from the lower to the higher, after granting their claim; but this applies to the creation, not to the created.

When He (Exalted is He) informed about His sincere servants, that they are honored by servitude to Him, He informed about those who refuse this. So He said, warning, cautioning, and threatening: ﴿And whoever disdains﴾, meaning of all existing things, ﴿from His worship﴾. And since disdain may mean mere refusal and not arrogance, He said, clarifying the intended meaning here: ﴿and is arrogant﴾, meaning he seeks arrogance regarding that and brings it into being, because mere refusal does not necessarily entail it. And since the gathering (*hashr*) is general to the arrogant and others, the pronoun in ﴿then He will gather them﴾ refers to the servants indicated by "servant" and "His worship." Its reference to "whoever" is not considered good, because the detail (in what follows) rejects it. The sense then is: "Then He will humiliate them, because He will gather the servants (p-525) ﴿all of them unto Himself﴾," meaning the arrogant and others, by a promise that does not fail. For all of them die, and whoever dies was certainly created and originated. Whoever is able to originate and annihilate a thing, the ability to restore it is more fitting. And *hashr* (gathering) means assembling by compulsion.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 173:

When He had generalized the mention of the gathering (al-hashr) to include the arrogant and others, the detailed explanation came to the two categories, and He said: ﴿As for those who believed﴾; that is, submitted to Allah (Exalted) and humbled themselves before Him; ﴿and did righteous deeds﴾; confirming their affirmation of faith; ﴿then He will pay them their rewards in full﴾; that is, the rewards which customs among you are accustomed to giving; although in reality they do not deserve them, because Allah (Exalted) is the One who enabled them to do them, so they are a bounty from Him upon them; ﴿and He will increase them﴾; that is, beyond what customs have decreed; ﴿out of His bounty﴾; that is, something that cannot be enclosed within counting, because He is the Possessor of great bounty. ﴿As for those who disdained and were arrogant﴾; that is, they sought both refusal and pride; ﴿He will punish them with a painful punishment﴾; that is, for the pleasure they found in self-exaltation and arrogance, and for the pain they inflicted thereby upon the friends of Allah; ﴿and they will not find for themselves﴾; that is, neither a state nor a final refuge; ﴿besides Allah﴾; the One with whom no command belongs to anyone; ﴿any protector﴾; that is, a relative who does with them what a relative does; ﴿or any helper﴾; that is, even if he were distant. In this there is the most complete restraint against what the hypocrites intended by allying themselves with the People of the Book, and the greatest negation of what they promised them of their standing, and what they claimed of a rank with Allah that would entail bringing near whom they wished and distancing whom they wished. It is among the most fitting matters for concluding the first verses warning against them: ﴿And sufficient is Allah as a protector, and sufficient is Allah as a helper﴾ [An-Nisa: 45].

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 4, verse 174:

When he had removed the doubts of all the opponents from all the sects — the Jews, the Christians, and the hypocrites — and had established the proof against them, and had established the decisive evidences for the gathering of all created beings, and it became established that they are all His servants, he addressed them in general in guidance, out of His gentleness toward them, and said: ﴿O mankind﴾; that is, all of them: the People of the Book and others.

And when the listener was deserving of having his breast expanded by decisive evidences, in a concise and comprehensive statement, He said: ﴿There has certainly come to you a proof﴾; that is, a clear, luminous argument, conveying complete certainty, and he is a messenger supported by decisive evidences of miracles and other things; ﴿from your Lord﴾; that is, the One who bestows favor upon you by sending him, the One from whom you have never seen any favor except that it came from Him.

And when the Qur'an is an attribute of the Most Merciful, He brought the manifestation of greatness, and said: ﴿And We have sent down﴾; that is, by what We possess of greatness, power, knowledge and wisdom, upon the described Messenger, reaching ﴿to you a manifest light﴾; that is, clear in itself and making clear to others; and it is this Qur'an, comprehensive in its miraculousness and the excellence of its exposition, between the verification of transmission and the enlightenment of reason, so that no kind of excuse remains for anyone among those it addresses. The summary is that He, glorified is He, when He created for the human being an intellect, and placed in it a light that does not go astray nor incline, however it be stripped bare, (p-527) yet He, glorified is He, surrounded it with appetites, desires, weariness and lassitude, so that in most of its states it was deficient — except the prophets, peace be upon them, and whomever He joined with them — He sent down His Books with that intellect stripped bare of every hindrance, and commanded them to make their intellects follow it and submit to it, because theirs are mixed, whereas it is unmixed, having no admixture in it in any way.

When, in this verse, He pointed to the purest Messenger and the most rightly guided Prophet, who was formed upon this most upright and clearest intellect, and to the most complete and perfect Book, which proceeds upon this highest law, whose expression is comprehensive and whose rulings on the first and the last matters are concise, whose context and arrangement of verses are secured by the clarity of proofs and the manifestation of arguments, He began to divide those who are warned. So He (exalted) said: ﴿As for those who believed in Allah﴾, i.e., the One whose clarity shows that no one shares any command with Him in His essence, attributes, actions, rulings, or names, as the decisive proof indicates. ﴿And held fast to Him﴾, i.e., they made Him a support (ʿiṣām, a tie or binding) for themselves in the obligations, which are among the greatest aims of this surah. He binds them and restrains them from going astray after guidance and from returning from insight to blindness, because the ʿiṣām is that which ties a container so that nothing of what is in it comes out. The form iftiʿāl (the reflexive verb form) indicates striving in this, because the soul is inclined to neglect, and neglect produces error. ﴿So He will admit them﴾, i.e., by a promise that will not fail. Perhaps the particle sīn (the future marker) was mentioned to convey, along with the certainty of the promise, an urging toward persistence and constancy in works, indicating the greatness of what is with Him, glory be to Him. ﴿Into mercy from Him﴾, i.e., a great reward, which is by His mercy toward them, not by anything they had earned. He indicated righteousness, according to what their deeds would require had they had any, by His saying: ﴿and bounty﴾, i.e., great, which they know is an increase for which they have no cause. ﴿And He will guide them﴾, i.e., in this world and the Hereafter, ﴿to Him on a path﴾, i.e., great and very clear, ﴿straight﴾. That is, He is the guide of His people, as if He were seeking to set Himself right; so He will certainly bring them to His promise, by that which protects them in their secret and open affairs, seeking to make manifest the lights of the realm of holiness in their spirits, and by enabling them to follow what it guided them to regarding the obligations and other matters. So He came, as you see, with ﴿amma﴾ ("as for"), which necessarily entails division, and He brought one of the two categories mentioned in the preceding verse, describing them as holding fast to Allah in support and in accepting all of His rulings, in obligations and otherwise, whether these agreed with their desires or opposed them. This is an allusion to the hypocrites who allied themselves with others, and to the disbelievers who believed in some things and disbelieved in others. He left out the other category, that of those who disdain and are arrogant, and in its place He set a ruling from among the rulings of the obligations with which the surah opens, which is among its greatest aims, without any conjunction particle, but with perfect connection. So He said, denouncing them for repeating the question about women and children after the healing speech, and explaining that in all of this He had guided to the most upright path:

﴿They ask you for a ruling﴾; that is, they ask you to give them a ruling, that is, to make clear to them, by what you have of generosity, bounty and liberality, what has become obscure to them and whose secret is hidden from them, concerning the ruling on the *kalālah* (a person who leaves neither child nor parent). It also concerns the attention given to the matter of inheritance. He said, indicating that God did not entrust this matter to anyone else: ﴿Say: "God gives you a ruling concerning the kalālah."﴾ That is, the Supreme King. The *kalālah* is one who has neither child nor parent. Al-Bukhari related in *al-Tafsir*, on the authority of al-Bara' (may God be pleased with him), who said: "The last surah to be revealed was *Bara'ah* (al-Tawbah), and the last verse to be revealed was: ﴿They ask you for a ruling. Say: God gives you a ruling concerning the kalālah.﴾" Al-Asbahani related on the authority of al-Sha'bi: Abu Bakr and 'Umar (may God be pleased with them both) differed concerning the *kalālah*. Abu Bakr said: "It is whoever is other than the father." 'Umar said: "It is whoever is other than the father and the child." Then 'Umar said: "I am truly ashamed before God to oppose Abu Bakr (may God be pleased with him)."

Then he resumed his statement: ﴿If a man dies, leaving no child﴾; that is, while he is described as such, or in a state in which ﴿he has no child﴾, that is, no descendant however remote, whether male or female, with respect to the inheritance of the half; and he also has no parent. If he has either of them, he is not called a "*kalālah*." The Sunnah has clarified this. Al-Asbahani said: "These are not the first of two rulings of which one was clarified by the Book and the other by the Sunnah." It is His saying, peace and blessings be upon him: "Give the fixed shares to their rightful owners; what remains goes to the nearest male agnate (*'aṣabah*)," and "the father takes precedence over the brother."

(p. 530) And the situation is that he has a sister, that is, one, from the father, whether full (*shaqīqah*) or not, because it will come that her brother residuates (*ya'ṣibuha*) her; for if he were a son of the mother he would not residuate. ﴿Then she receives half of what he leaves, and he﴾; that is, this deceased brother; ﴿inherits from her﴾; that is, if she dies and he survives, all of her property; ﴿if she has no child﴾; that is, male or female, as was mentioned in the reverse case. This applies if by inheritance is meant the entirety of the property; otherwise he inherits along with a female, just as she too inherits along with a female, as the context also indicates, but not beyond the half.

When He had clarified the matter in the case of a single heir, He followed it with its clarification in the case of plurality, and He mentioned its minimum first. So He said: ﴿If there are two﴾; that is, the two heirs, by the context's clarification of them and its guidance toward them. Since what the context implies was left unstated, and the predicate could be "righteous," or "young," or otherwise, He made clear that the intended meaning, as the context also indicates, is simply the number, of whatever description it may be. So He said: ﴿two﴾; that is, of sisters from the father, whether full or not; ﴿then for them is two-thirds of what he leaves.﴾ If they are full sisters, each one of them has a third; if they differ, the full sister has the half, and the one from the father only has a sixth, to complete the two-thirds.

When He had clarified the minimum of plurality, He followed it with what exceeds it, and said: ﴿And if they are siblings﴾; that is, (p. 531) the heirs; ﴿men and women﴾; that is, mixed; ﴿then for the male is the equivalent of the share of two females.﴾ He, glorified is He, has concluded what He intended to clarify regarding the inheritance of siblings from the father, and thereby all the states of what He intended concerning inheritance have been completed. This, despite its brevity as you see, could fill volumes, and God is the Guide. The placement of this verse here, as has preceded, is an indication from Him that whoever refuses to give inheritance to women and minors, about which the request for a ruling was repeated, has turned away from His worship and has been arrogant, even if he believes in all else of the rulings. Whoever turns away from one of the rulings, that person is truly a disbeliever, just as whoever believes in some prophets and disbelieves in others is truly a disbeliever. This is the intention of the devils of the People of the Book, who know the soundness of these rulings, who envy you for them, and who want to lead you astray from them, so that you may share with them in the wretchedness that befell them when they altered the rulings. These are the ones referred to after the mention of the verses of inheritance and what follows them concerning marriage, by His saying: ﴿God desires to make clear to you and guide you to the ways of those before you﴾ [al-Nisa’: 26], and His saying: ﴿But those who follow their desires want you to deviate into a tremendous deviation﴾ [al-Nisa’: 27]; then those explicitly named in His saying: ﴿Have you not considered those who were given a portion of the Book? They purchase error and want you to stray from the way﴾ [al-Nisa’: 44], ﴿And God is most knowing of your enemies﴾ [al-Nisa’: 45]. For this reason, God knows best, He concluded this verse with His saying: ﴿God makes clear﴾; that is, He who (p. 532) encompasses all things in power and knowledge; ﴿to you﴾; that is, and He did not leave you in this clarification to the clarification of anyone else. He said, encouraging and warning: ﴿lest﴾; that is, lest out of dislike ﴿you go astray, and God﴾; that is, He to whom all perfection belongs; ﴿is knowing of all things.﴾ That is, He has, by His knowledge, made clear to you what His clarification benefits you with, in life and in death, in this world and the Hereafter, until He placed you on the white path, as in the light of day, from which none deviates except one who is doomed.

The summary is that the delay of this verse until this point is due to what has preceded: that dividing the statement regarding what souls find repugnant, and presenting it gradually, with gentleness and progression, makes it more apt for acceptance. It also indicates the great concern for the matter of the obligatory shares, by making the discussion of them throughout the surah, at its beginning, its middle and its end. It warns against their situation becoming like that of the hypocrites in the misguidance of the People of the Book with respect to them, by casting doubt and taking them from the place their souls desire, which their forebears followed and their hearts were steeped in. It also warns against becoming like them in believing in some and disbelieving in others, which would lead them to complete disbelief, since religion is not divisible; rather, whoever disbelieves in part of it disbelieves in the whole of it. From here the connection between the end of this surah and its beginning becomes apparent: its beginning points to the fact that all people are like a single thing, and that requires that there be no distinction among them except in what God has legislated; and its end points to this by equalizing women and men in general inheritance, according to nearness of kinship, even though their shares differ. It is as if it were said: "O people, fear your Lord, who created you from a single soul, and created from it its mate, and spread from the two of them many men and women, and made them equal in the rulings He willed. Whoever is arrogant, even toward one of His rulings, He will requite him on the Day of Gathering, and he will find no helper besides God, and nothing of his state is hidden from Him." How very apt is the conclusion of this with the encompassing of knowledge, in view of what its beginning indicated of the perfection of power! Thus its end is evidence for its beginning, since the perfection of knowledge entails the comprehensiveness of power. The Imam said: "These two attributes are those by which lordship, divinity, majesty and might are established, and by them it is incumbent upon the servant to be obedient to the commands and prohibitions, and submissive to all obligations." End of quotation. And the conclusion of the first verse in it, His saying: ﴿Indeed, God is ever watchful over you﴾ [al-Nisa’: 1], that is, He is knowing of all things of your states and others; so do not suppose that anything is hidden from Him, however subtle; let your caution toward Him be intense and your vigilance of Him constant. This is the most fitting thing for the beginning of *al-Ma'idah*. And God is the Granter of success in what is right, and to Him is the return and the final place.
